en: The *Lamaka Sūtra*, Scroll One, translated by the Śramaṇa Shengjian of the Later Qin:
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, the Garden of Anāthapiṇḍada.
In the solemn and majestic Hall of Universal Victory, together with bodhisattva-mahāsattvas such as Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva—
namely: Prabhāketu Bodhisattva, Meruketu Bodhisattva, Ratnaketu Bodhisattva, Anāvaraṇaketu Bodhisattva,
Puṣpaketu Bodhisattva, Śuddhaketu Bodhisattva, and Sūryaprabhāketu Bodhisattva— ...
The Bodhisattva Śāntisamyakdhvaja, the Bodhisattva Virajadhvaja, the Bodhisattva Lokasamayadhvaja,
the Bodhisattva Mahītejas-dhvaja, the Bodhisattva Ratnatejas, the Bodhisattva Mahātejas,
the Bodhisattva Vajrajñānatejas, the Bodhisattva Viśuddhatejas, the Bodhisattva Dharmādityatejas, and the Bodhisattva Guṇa...
The Bodhisattva Mountain Majesty, the Bodhisattva Wisdom-Flame Majesty, the Bodhisattva Universal Manifestation Supreme Majesty,
the Bodhisattva Sustaining Earth-Treasury, the Bodhisattva Space-Treasury, the Bodhisattva Lotus-Treasury,
the Bodhisattva Jewel-Treasury, the Bodhisattva Sun-Treasury, the Bodhisattva Merit-Purity-Treasury, and the Bodhisattva Dharma-Seal-Treasury.
The Bodhisattva Sarvaśuddhigarbha, the Bodhisattva Anunnata, the Bodhisattva Padmavijragarbha,
the Bodhisattva Suviśuddhanetra, the Bodhisattva Viśuddhanetra, the Bodhisattva Śuddhanetragarbha, the Bodhisattva Asaṅganetra,
the Bodhisattva Samantamukhanetra, the Bodhisattva Sudarśananetra, and the Bodhisattva Utpala...
Flower-Eye Bodhisattva, Vajra-Eye Bodhisattva, Jewel-Eye Bodhisattva, Space-Eye Bodhisattva, Virtuous-Eye Bodhisattva,
Universal-Eye Bodhisattva, Celestial-Crown Bodhisattva, Dharma-Realm Flame-Wisdom Celestial-Crown Bodhisattva,
Site-of-Enlightenment Celestial-Crown Bodhisattva, and Sandalwood Light Celestial-Crown Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Buddha-Treasury Celestial-Crown, the Bodhisattva Mountain-Valiant Celestial-Crown, the Bodhisattva World-Pure Celestial-Crown,
the Bodhisattva Dignified-Conduct Celestial-Crown, the Bodhisattva Unconquerable, the Bodhisattva All-Buddhas-Lion-Throne-Overlooking,
the Bodhisattva Universal-Dharma-Sphere-Akasha-Radiance-Contemplating, and the Bodhisattva Brahma-Superior Topknot.
...the Bodhisattva Dragon-Victory Topknot, the Bodhisattva Buddha-Transformation Flame Topknot, the Bodhisattva Mani-Jewel Topknot of the Ocean of All Vows,
the Bodhisattva Circular Radiance Pearl Topknot of the Tathāgata, the Bodhisattva Reward Topknot of the Space-Palm Jewel,
the Bodhisattva Tathāgata-Playful Jewel-King Net Topknot, and the Bodhisattva Fragrance Topknot of the Tathāgata’s Dharma-Wheel.
The Bodhisattvas: Sarvatryadhvānugata-gandhakeśa Bodhisattva, Mahāprabha Bodhisattva, Vimalaprabha Bodhisattva,
Ratnaprabha Bodhisattva, Virajaprabha Bodhisattva, Arciṣprabha Bodhisattva, Dharmaprabha Bodhisattva,
Śāntiprabha Bodhisattva, Sūryaprabha Bodhisattva, and Vilasitaprabha Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Celestial Radiance, the Bodhisattva Radiance of Meritorious Marks, the Bodhisattva Radiance of the Mark of Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Radiance of the Mark of Dharma,
the Bodhisattva Radiance of the Mark of Supernatural Powers, the Bodhisattva Radiance of the Mark of Light, the Bodhisattva Radiance of the Mark of Flowers,
the Bodhisattva Radiance of the Mark of Jewels, the Bodhisattva Radiance of the Mark of Bodhi, and the Bodhisattva Radiance of the Mark of Brahmā.
The Bodhisattva Samantaprabhārci-lakṣaṇa, the Bodhisattva Brahma-svara, the Bodhisattva Sāgara-svara,
the Bodhisattva Pratibhāna-svara, the Bodhisattva Loka-rāja-svara, the Bodhisattva Parvata-saṃghaṭṭana-svara, the Bodhisattva Sarva-dharmadhātu-vyāpi-svara,
the Bodhisattva Sarva-dharma-sāgara-nirghoṣa-svara, and the Bodhisattva Māra-dhātu-vinaya.
Ghoṣa Bodhisattva, Mahākaruṇameghanirghoṣa Bodhisattva, Sarvalokapraśamanasvara Bodhisattva,
Dharmavīryamati Bodhisattva, Jñānavīra Bodhisattva, Guṇameruvīra Bodhisattva,
Guṇadaṃṣṭravīra Bodhisattva, Yaśovīra Bodhisattva, Samantajvālāvīra Bodhisattva, and Mahāmaitrī [Bodhisattva].
Vīra Bodhisattva, Jñānasāgaravīra Bodhisattva, Tathāgatagotravīra Bodhisattva, Prabhāsaśreṣṭha Bodhisattva,
Suvikrāntaśreṣṭha Bodhisattva, Vīraśreṣṭha Bodhisattva, Lokaviśuddhaśreṣṭha Bodhisattva,
Dharmaśreṣṭha Bodhisattva, Candraśreṣṭha Bodhisattva, Gaganaprabhaśreṣṭha Bodhisattva, and Ratnaśreṣṭha Bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Nakṣatrarājaśrī, the Bodhisattva Jñānarājaśrī, the Bodhisattva Vṛkṣarājapratimaṇḍitaśrī,
the Bodhisattva Dharmarājapratimaṇḍita, the Bodhisattva Lokarājapratimaṇḍita, the Bodhisattva Brahmārājapratimaṇḍita, the Bodhisattva Parvatarājapratimaṇḍita,
the Bodhisattva Maṇirājapratimaṇḍita, the Bodhisattva Nāgarājapratimaṇḍita, the Bodhisattva Śāntarājapratimaṇḍita, and the Bodhisattva An... [omitted]
Bodhisattva King of Movement Seal, Bodhisattva Sage Worthy Power King Seal, Bodhisattva Victorious King Seal,
Bodhisattva Tranquil Fragrance, Bodhisattva Infinite Fragrance, Bodhisattva Earth Fragrance Sound, Bodhisattva Ocean Thunder Fragrance Sound,
Bodhisattva Dharma Beauty Fragrance Sound, Bodhisattva Space Fragrance Sound, and the multitude...
The Bodhisattva Sound of the Fragrance of Produced Merit, the Bodhisattva Sound of the Fragrance of the Roots of Goodness of Sentient Beings,
the Bodhisattva Sound of the Mara Realm, the Bodhisattva Light of the Mountain of Wisdom, the Bodhisattva Space-Mind, the Bodhisattva Pure Mind,
the Bodhisattva Unattached Mind, the Bodhisattva Awakened Mind, and the Bodhisattva Flame-Mind of the Three Times.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Radiant Intention, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Universally Illuminating Intention, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Dharma-realm Flame Intention,
and five hundred other such Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas were present together.

Their conduct is identical to that of Samantabhadra; they are fully endowed with the realm of non-attachment, universally manifesting throughout the infinite Buddha-lands of the ten directions, their physical dimensions being limitless as they appear before all Buddhas.

Furthermore, while cultivating the sphere of the unimpeded pure eye, their minds never rest; they universally gather the merits of all Buddhas, becoming decisively clear regarding the path to Bodhi. They universally collect immeasurable light, deeply entering the ocean of wisdom of all dharmas, constantly practicing non-attachment and non-reception. Their minds attain great wisdom, and their bodies remain fulfilled throughout immeasurable and innumerable kalpas. Their four analytical knowledges (*catasraḥ pratisaṃvidaḥ*) are inexhaustible, and their wisdom is like space—without dependence and without attachment. According to the inclinations of sentient beings, they manifest physical bodies at will. Their pure eyes are free from defilement and obstruction, like the sun dwelling in the midst of the sky, filling the entire dharma-realm with radiance.

Furthermore, there were five hundred śrāvakas who had long since attained mastery of the Four Noble Truths and clearly understood the primordial limit (*pūrvakoṭi*). Having deeply entered the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) and transcended the ocean of birth and death, they followed the noble assembly of the Tathāgata’s disciples; their minds were liberated from the fetters of existence, and they harbored no doubts regarding the ocean of the Buddha’s Dharma.

Furthermore, he was accompanied by countless celestial kings; having planted the roots of all virtues under previous Buddhas, he served as an uninvited friend to all sentient beings. Having received the precepts of the mind and perfected all merits, he surpassed all devas and humans without harboring any sense of superiority. Without abandoning afflictions [yet] having already exhausted them, his mental wisdom was liberated like space. He had no doubts regarding the Buddha-dharma, deeply entered the ocean of the Buddhas' wisdom, and followed the noble deportment of the Tathāgatas. Upholding the Buddha’s instructions, he brought sentient beings to fulfillment, protected the seeds of the Buddha-dharma so they would not be severed, and by virtue of these roots of goodness, he was constantly born into the family of the Buddhas, deeply delighting in the true Dharma-gate of the Knowledge of All Modes (*sarvākārajñatā*).

At that time, the great assembly of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas, along with the devas, māras, brahmās, and various ṛṣis, each surrounded by their retinues, paid respectful homage and all formed this thought:

"We shall contemplate the conduct of the Tathāgata; we shall contemplate the realm of the Buddha; we shall contemplate the Tathāgata’s mastery of supernatural powers and transformations; we shall contemplate the Tathāgata’s upholding; we shall contemplate the Tathāgata’s powers; we shall contemplate the Tathāgata’s fearlessnesses; we shall contemplate the Tathāgata’s abiding; we shall contemplate the Tathāgata’s samādhis; we shall contemplate the Tathāgata’s supreme and wondrous merits; we shall contemplate the Tathāgata’s body; and we shall contemplate the Tathāgata’s wisdom, which is without limit or bottom. It cannot be measured by any gods or humans; it cannot be distinguished, it cannot be manifested, it cannot be known or seen, and it cannot be clearly proclaimed; nor is there anyone capable of explaining it according to reality."

Except for the power of the Buddha’s sustaining, the power of the Buddha’s sovereignty, the power of the Buddha’s wisdom, the power of the Buddha’s eloquence, the power of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, the power of the Buddha’s samādhi, the power of the Buddha’s supernormal knowledges, the power of the Buddha’s original vows, the power of past roots of goodness, the power of attending spiritual friends, the power of pure faith, the power of abiding in skillful means, the power of delighting in seeking pure, supreme, and wondrous roots of goodness, the power of the upright mind of bodhicitta, and the power of the vow for omniscience.
Therefore, World-Honored One!
You know the various desires, various faiths, and various understandings of sentient beings, yet your mind remains non-dual.
With a voice free from attachment, you awaken all those who know the Way and speak the Way, excellently teaching them.
Regarding the various practices, faculties, dispositions, faiths, understandings, and intentions of those on the various stages,
as well as the realm of the Omniscient One— each contemplating the merits of the Tathāgata,
they all wished for him to proclaim the excellence of the vows and practices he performed when he was formerly a bodhisattva.
Through their karma, their prior cultivation, and the supreme *pāramitās* of the vow for omniscience, they manifest the supernatural powers of the various bodhisattva stages,
the adornment of skillful means through a multitude of wondrous sounds, the adornment of bodhisattva practices,
and the emergence of the ocean-like adornments that fulfill the gateways to bodhisattva enlightenment, thereby manifesting the path of bodhisattva mastery.
...giving birth to the ocean of bodhisattva adornments; adorning the supernatural powers of the Tathāgata’s playful manifestations;
adorning the Tathāgata’s sovereign wheel of Dharma; adorning the ocean of the Tathāgata’s lands;

and adorning the Tathāgata’s universal manifestation throughout the ten directions to discipline sentient beings, while remaining without manifesting body or mind, abiding in the true Dharma of all Tathāgatas.
The City of Transcendent and Supreme Merit, the Universal Manifestation of All Paths, the Tathāgata Dharma King, manifests all realms of existence for the sake of all sentient beings;

with the power of pure, luminous, and universal illumination and sovereign spiritual penetrations, the Tathāgata is the supreme field of merit for all sentient beings; the Tathāgata is for all sentient beings...
I speak of the merit of the three wheels of giving; may I transform and deliver all sentient beings.
I only pray that the Tathāgata, out of compassion for all, will fully manifest [this grace].

At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thoughts in the minds of all the bodhisattvas, through his body of great compassion, the gateway of great compassion, the mind of great compassion, and the power of the original vow of great compassion—acting in accordance with great compassion, as vast as the *dharmatā* and ultimate as space—entered the Lion King’s Vigorous Stride Samādhi, in order to cause all sentient beings to delight in the pure Dharma.

Having entered samādhi, the multi-storied lecture hall in the Jeta Grove suddenly became radiant, vast, and pure; the ground was adorned with Brahma-heavenly vajras, interspersed with rare wonders and embellished with various jewels, while wish-fulfilling gems and all manner of famous flowers rained down.

At that time, within that forest, both inside and out were transparently radiant. There were trees of lapis lazuli, whose branches, twigs, flowers, and fruits were all composed of various jewels. Multicolored lights swirled among them, and nets made of the king of *rājavatī* pearls covered the area. Jāmbūnada gold and various ornaments filled every space without any gaps, completely covering the trees from above.

Furthermore, the pavilions were adorned with rare jewels; pillars of *prabhāsa-maṇi* gems served as bright pearl columns, their long, straight radiance shining through the groves. There were golden doors with pearl curtains and railings inlaid with precious gems. Stairways leading out in the four directions were composed of various jewels. Wondrous flowers made of *maṇi-rāja* gems formed floral garlands, from the tips of which true pearl light was emitted. These were planted in rows along the eaves and spread across the steps and thresholds, while banners, streamers, and silk canopies filled the realm of empty space.

Before the windows and casements, jewel trees sprang forth by transformation, standing in natural rows like a grove of sāla trees; their fruits were like precious bells, emitting myriad exquisite sounds.
From beneath the roots of these trees flowed lapis lazuli water—fragrant, pure, and soft—which spread throughout the Jeta Grove.

By the power of the Buddha’s spiritual authority and the power of his original vows, inconceivable asaṃkhyeya buddha-fields as numerous as the atoms of the worlds of the ten directions—all pure and immaculate—along with immeasurable and innumerable articles of offering, were all universally manifested within the Jeta Grove.

Furthermore, there are rivers of fragrant merit that wind through the Pure Land; immeasurable jewel-flowers are produced by transformation as they follow the current, beyond all reckoning. The flowers and the water produce sounds that all proclaim the retributive practices of Bodhisattvas.

The flowering trees flourished in splendor, emitting clouds of fragrant canopies; from within these various fragrant canopies arose inconceivable clouds of multi-storied pavilions, and there were incalculable, inconceivable flower garlands and necklaces, all of which hung down. There were incalculable kingly mani-jewels, and soft garments and various precious banners spontaneously surged forth, while the smoke of incense, pennants, and canopies completely filled the space.

Furthermore, countless clouds of precious flowers revolved in the air; all the banners, streamers, flower-canopies, and various jeweled bells produced wondrous sounds, proclaiming the names of all Buddhas and manifesting the signs of the pure Wheel of Dharma.

Furthermore, there was a Lion-like King of Wish-fulfilling Jewels who, with an ocean of sounds, universally proclaimed the ocean-gates of the original vows of all Buddhas; he was adorned by the light of the Dharma-characteristics of the jewel-kings and mani-jewels throughout the entire dharma-realm.

At that time, in the void above the Jeta Grove, there appeared inconceivable and incalculable clouds of various fragrant trees, as well as all manner of such offerings and the various adornments of Buddha-fields, immeasurable and boundless, beyond full description.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, seeking spiritual friends from the eastern regions, gradually traveled on until he reached the southern regions and then proceeded to the western regions. From afar, he saw the elder Suprabha in the city of Kūṭagrāma; resolving to go toward him, he set out upon the road. He contemplated meditative absorption (*samādhi*), maintaining mindfulness before him without distraction, dwelling in the stage of right concentration (*samyaktva-niyāma*). Although on the road, he delighted in the True Dharma, free from regret and without retreating from his state. With courageous diligence, he did not fear the perilous path; mindful of the spiritual friend and cultivating the path to perfect enlightenment, his body and mind were inexhaustible for the sake of attaining the path of peace. While on the way, he formed this thought: "How shall I attain the supreme realm?"

How shall I now swiftly approach a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*) to inquire about the Bodhisattva path and cultivate the Bodhisattva practices? By regarding the spiritual friend as the causal condition for the Buddha-way, may I attain the various *pāramitās* and universally gather all beings; free from all obstacles, may I enter the unattached *dharmadhātu*. For the sake of all sentient beings, may I sever the karma of the various evil paths, eliminate the mind of self, person, being, and life-span, extinguish all afflictions and defilements, and destroy the net of all views. Having perfected the arrow of goodness, with the bow of compassion, may I shoot at the locus of protecting the Dharma and bring the cause and effect to fruition.
Why is this? If one encounters and meets a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), one will certainly achieve all virtuous merits.

A spiritual friend can serve as the great foundation for all-knowledge; their body and mind are in right reception, their countenance does not change, they seek out spiritual friends with dignified decorum, and they are devoid of any signs of sudden violence.

Gradually proceeding to the city of Kūṭāgāraśālā, he saw the elder Bhadrajyotis in that city’s multi-storied lecture hall. Having approached him, he beheld him surrounded by hundreds of thousands of millions of great elders, all of whom were filled with joy and stood at the elder Bhadrajyotis’s side, each desiring to hear the various teachings. Just as a maritime guide explains the locations of oceanic treasures to a company of merchants, the elder Bhadrajyotis was well able to discern the oceanic treasures of the Buddha-dharma and expounded for the entire assembly the state of non-attachment and non-discrimination.
At that time, the youth Sudhana prostrated himself with his head at [the sage's] feet and addressed him, saying:
"Great Sage, I have long since resolved my mind upon Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, yet I do not know how to practice the bodhisattva path or cultivate the bodhisattva deeds."
The elder Suprabha said to Sudhana:
"Excellent, excellent, noble son!"

You have already been able to give rise to the bodhicitta and skillfully inquire about the jewel of great wisdom; it is for the sake of attaining such profound meanings of the Dharma, and for the purpose of severing all seeds of doubt and suffering.

You have now questioned me because you have reached the shore of omniscience; with an unbreakable mind, you are correctly oriented toward the Great Vehicle, causing you to leave behind all fears of the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, and to proceed rightly toward the Buddha-way. You cultivate various samādhis and gates of tranquility, skillfully practicing all bodhisattva deeds, and vow to sport in supernormal powers and turn the non-retrogressive wheel. You purify the paths of karma, swiftly dedicate yourself to the mind of omniscience, and practice the bodhisattva deeds according to reality; it is for the sake of the bodhisattva path that you have come to question me.

One who practices this conduct perceives the ten directions universally without obstruction; having well understood the gates of remedial means within the ocean of all-knowledge, they have come to question me in order to adorn all bodhisattva practices.
"Good son!

Here, at the multi-storied lecture hall in the city of Kucavati on this seashore, I constantly preach day and night the Dharma-gate of the pure conduct of Bodhisattvas of Great Kindness and Great Compassion."
"Good son!
In this Jambudvīpa, whenever I see sentient beings who are poor and suffering, I first seek to benefit them, and only then do I expound for them the profound meaning of emptiness."

In accordance with their aspirations, he causes them to attain fulfillment; he gathers them in by means of food and drink, or by means of the wealth of the Dharma, or by means of meritorious deeds, or by means of wisdom, or by means of the upright karma of roots of goodness.
Those who should be gathered by means of the faculties of a bodhisattva, they are gathered by means of the faculties of a bodhisattva;
those who should be gathered by generating the mind of a bodhisattva, they are gathered by generating the mind of a bodhisattva;
and those who should be gathered by removing doubts and generating the bodhicitta, they are gathered by means of the method for removing doubts.
If there are those who should give rise to the bodhicitta through joy, they are gathered by means of the dharma of joy;
if there are those who should give rise to the bodhicitta through great compassion, they are gathered by means of great compassion;

if there are those who should give rise to the bodhicitta through the fixed dharma of impermanence that removes the sorrows, lamentations, sufferings, and afflictions of birth, old age, sickness, and death, they are gathered by means of the dharmas of suffering, emptiness, and impermanence.

If there are sentient beings who should be gathered by dwelling within the ocean of birth and death with a mind free from weariness, he dwells together within that ocean of birth and death to gather them;
if there are those who should be inspired to the bodhisattva-mind through the four methods of attraction (*saṃgrahavastu*), he gathers them by means of those four methods of attraction;
if there are those who should be inspired to the bodhisattva-mind through the ocean of all wisdom and merit, he gathers them by means of the Dharma that accords with that ocean of merit and wisdom.

If there are those who should develop the bodhicitta through the gateway of the ocean of the true Dharma of all Buddhas of the three periods of time as an antidote, they are thereby gathered by that very ocean of the true Dharma of the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
"Good son!

By means of such dharmas of gathering as these, for the sake of benefiting sentient beings and so that all sentient beings may obtain the benefit and joy of the Dharma, I remain on this shore of the ocean."

“Good son! I abide on this shore and universally know all the treasures within the ocean and their places of origin; I know their roots, their species, their value—whether noble or base—and their clear characteristics, as well as the radiance of these jewels.”

He is skillfully able to discern and is well-versed in all crafts and arts; he is well-acquainted with the distinctions among all nāgas, nāga kings, and nāga princesses' palaces, and is also able to effectively eliminate the fears and evil omens arising from the quarrels and conflicts of the nāgas.
Furthermore, he thoroughly knows all the palaces and villages of the rākṣasa kings, and is also able to skillfully eliminate the quarrels and disputes of the rākṣasas, as well as their terrors.

Moreover, he thoroughly knows the dwelling places of all the malevolent spirits such as the chis, mei, and wangliang, and is also able to extinguish all the perils of the swirling eddies in the great oceans, while also knowing the colors of the waters, the sources of springs, and the various streams.

He was skillfully able to observe and discern all matters concerning calamities, anomalies, and strange portents involving the sun, moon, and stars; observing their signs day and night, he never for even a single moment lost sight of their regular courses, perceiving them with such clarity and precision that there was not the slightest error.
He was well-versed in all forms of writing, calculation, archery, and charioteering, employing them as the occasion required.
He was skilled in discerning all manner of signs and phenomena, which shift and transform incessantly in a single kṣaṇa, sometimes coalescing and sometimes dispersing.
He is skilled in deliberating upon all worldly affairs. Good son!

You should now know that, by means of this Dharma-gate of the Ten Clarities for all sentient beings, I abide in purity and dwell upon the shore of fearlessness, causing each and every sentient being to attain peace and security, and constantly comforting them with the True Dharma.

If there are merchants and traders in Jambudvīpa who wish to go to the great ocean to seek precious treasures, by invoking my name they shall obtain great quantities of precious treasures and return safely and auspiciously.

If there are sentient beings who hear my name, all the defilements of their body and mind, as well as the impurities of their clothing, shall be forever eliminated; how much more so their afflictions!

If there are sentient beings who gaze upon me with their eyes, they shall always attain pure and unsurpassed Dharma-joy, never wearying of hearing the Dharma, and their bodies and minds shall be filled with delight. By means of this Dharma-joy, may I universally rain down the great rain of Dharma for all suffering beings within Jambudvīpa, causing them to find joy and happiness.

If there are sentient beings who hear me preach the Dharma, they will surely attain peace and security, crossing the ocean of birth and death and escaping all fears; they will certainly be established in the ocean of omniscience, forever free from craving and thirst, no longer subject to sorrow or affliction, and shall dwell eternally in the ocean of clear liberation throughout the three periods of time.

“Good son! You should now know that I am able to enter the ocean of the mental activities of all sentient beings, causing them to cultivate the karma for pure lands. I enable them to universally know the oceans of all pure lands in the ten directions, to be born therein at will and attain unimpeded karma, and furthermore, to adorn the ocean of roots of all pure deeds. I can universally purify the ocean of practices of all sentient beings, causing them to dwell in the great ocean of peaceful, tranquil, and profound sleep.”
"Good son! By means of my knowledge of this Bodhisattva Joy Banner Dharma-door of the Sound of Striking to Counteract and Eliminate Characteristics through Great Compassion, Joy, and Equanimity,
all great bodhisattvas have accomplished an immeasurable ocean of merit and wisdom, and are well able to..."
They discern the ocean of practices of all worlds, sever the ocean of all afflictions and karma,
accomplish the ocean of all dharma-realms, universally encompass the oceans of all sentient beings and worlds,
universally enter the ocean of supreme wisdom, and never abandon the ocean of all sentient beings; their minds are like...
The Ground [of Joy] is well able to accord with the ocean of all sentient beings and is universally able to transform the ocean of all sentient beings;
it skillfully conforms to the ocean of the majestic deportment of all sentient beings.
Since the great Bodhisattvas practice such things so profoundly, how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
Then the youth Sudhana prostrated himself with his head at [the elder’s] feet, circumambulated him hundreds of thousands of times, and took his leave to travel westward.
Susampanna praised him, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!”
"Good son!
You should now contemplate with right mindfulness the samādhi of right reception.

Departing from here, travel gradually westward toward the city named Yaśovatī. Once you have left that city, there is a land called Durāsadā and a city named Kaliṅgī; not far from here is a Forest of Merit (Guṇavana), and within that forest dwells a bhikṣuṇī named Siṃhavijṛmbhitā, whose body is the color of purple-gold, and who is foremost in her exquisite beauty."
"You should go to her and inquire about the conduct of a bodhisattva, inquire about the precepts of a bodhisattva, and inquire about the various Dharma-gates.

At that time, the youth Sudhana took his leave with hesitation and, traveling by degrees, arrived at the side of the Sunlight Spring in the Forest of Merit. There he saw the bhikṣuṇī sitting upright in meditative absorption, attended by five hundred young maidens of beautiful appearance who served as her attendants. Furthermore, five hundred young boys guarded these women, and hundreds of thousands of celestial maidens stood in attendance on their left and right.

At that time, by the side of the Sunlight Spring there was a grove called the Royal Garden. Entering that garden, he saw a great tree named Moon-Sun Light, which radiated light everywhere, illuminating a hundred yojanas and adorning the grove; it transformed into a multi-storied pavilion, adorned with the seven treasures, with light shining from above.

Again, he saw a great tree named Universal Radiance, its branches and leaves spreading luxuriantly, covering the entire trichiliocosm; its shape was like a canopy, flowing with various waters and emitting pure light.

Again, he saw a jewel grove named Flower Treasury (Kusumagarbha), towering and magnificent beyond measure; its flowers were in full bloom like the king of celestial trees, possessing wondrous radiance like a heavenly palace, and its color was a brilliant white, like the Snowy Mountains.
Again, he saw a great tree named "Delicious Flavor," with golden flowers and golden fruits that were soft, fragrant, and beautiful, most pleasing to the hearts of all.

He further saw a tree named "World-Purifying Light," its color and radiance immeasurable and boundless; its fruits were made of sandalwood and *maṇi* jewels, and it was covered by an *asaṃkhyeya* number of various nets of pearls spread over the tree, resembling a celestial palace.
Again, he saw a tree named Celestial Robe, which constantly produced immeasurable, incalculable numbers of robes in the colors of various jewels.
He further saw trees named Music, which, when they brushed against one another, produced sounds surpassing those of Brahmā.
Furthermore, he saw a multitude of groves named Universal Fragrance Adornment; their fragrance wafted everywhere without obstruction.
Within these gardens, he also saw springs and ponds, covered above by nets of light from the seven treasures.

That pond is square, with four channels flowing from it that branch into eight streams, pouring into one another. It is filled to the brim with water of eight virtues, its bottom bedded with powdered ox-head sandalwood and adorned with various jewels; golden sand covers the ground as these fragrant waters surge forth, their sound like celestial music, gladdening the hearts of all. Furthermore, the pond is enclosed by railings made of various jewels, and its banks are strewn with golden sand that constantly emits light of many different colors. Blue lotuses (*utpala*), red lotuses (*padma*), yellow lotuses (*kumuda*), and white lotuses (*puṇḍarīka*) flourish upon the surface of the water.

There were various jewel trees, arranged in rows and magnificently adorned, surrounding the sides of the pond. Beneath each tree, countless precious lion thrones were spread, decorated with immeasurable celestial garments and a multitude of exquisite, rare treasures.

Priceless incense was burned, perfuming the lion thrones; canopies of various fragrant silks were pure white and brilliant, covered above by jeweled nets from which hung many golden bells that emitted harmonious and wondrous sounds.
Furthermore, there were immeasurable couches and canopies made of various jewels surrounding the high seat; it was likewise so beneath each and every tree.
Among the trees, there were also immeasurable lion thrones consisting of jewel-treasury lotuses;
moreover, among the trees, there were thrones consisting of various fragrant treasuries.
Furthermore, among the trees, there were thrones of various fragrant cloud-treasures;
among the trees, there were thrones of lion-jewel-cluster treasures;
and among the trees, there were thrones of pure universal-light maṇi-treasures of all worlds.
Furthermore, amidst the trees, there was a lion-throne treasury named Delightful-to-See, with immeasurable exquisite fragrances serving as its upholstery.

Each of these precious thrones was surrounded by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of small seats; each small seat was adorned with immeasurable jewels, and upon each throne were immeasurable precious gems filling it entirely, like a great jewel island. From each throne issued a supreme radiance that illuminated the royal garden and the Sunlight Grove; from within this light, celestial robes and various precious gems rained down—soft and lovely—spreading across the ground.

It is like the great ocean, which contains all manner of treasures; this Sunlight Spring is filled with sandalwood-scented water that reaches the ankles when stepped upon, swirling around the feet as one walks, and returning to its original state once the foot is lifted.

Within that pond were birds of many colors—ducks, wild geese, mandarin ducks, pheasants, kingfishers, and peacocks—each gazing at its own reflection as their elegant calls harmonized with one another; they soared through the air and gathered in the sandalwood grove.

In this king’s grove, from the Sunlight Spring, there arise inexhaustible pure flowers of various kinds, interspersed with priceless incense. It surpasses even Śakra’s Forest of Delight and its Pools; the jewel trees and their jeweled bells, along with branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits, resound spontaneously without being struck, producing wondrous sounds. There dwell celestial maidens, upright and exquisite, like the consorts of Maheśvara.

This royal garden is twice as radiant and surpasses all celestial palaces; the sounds of these goddesses’ drums, music, strings, and songs pervade the royal garden, filling everyone with joy, while divine *karpāsa* garments hang from the branches of the trees.

On the four sides of the grove, there are the Four Heavenly Kings, all of whom are bodhisattvas of great empowerment; leading their fourfold armies, they serve as a protective guard. Various pavilions, celestial silk canopies, and numerous halls are likewise guarded by these military hosts.

This garden is adorned like Śakra’s Joyful Garden of Radiant Jewel Forests; it is universally pure and serene, such that one never tires of gazing upon it. It surpasses the karmic rewards of humans and devas within the triple world, and even the Great Brahmā’s Hall of Pure and Virtuous Adornment cannot be compared to it. It is beyond the reach of the pure retributive vision of the countless Brahmā kings.
This Forest of Merit and this Sunlight Spring surpass even a hundred thousand Brahma palaces combined; their exquisite and wondrous adornments cannot be fully described.

At that time, the youth Sudhana beheld this grove, adorned with various kinds of subtle and wondrous radiance; all of it was accomplished through the pure conduct of the Bodhisattvas' fundamental karma, their merits as they truly are, and the power of their roots of goodness and vows. It transcended the worldly retributions of the triple world and was planted by the Tathāgatas of inconceivable asaṃkhyeya kalpas as the foundation of manifold virtues. Unattached to the world and far removed from solid food, it was like a master illusionist perceiving various forms and images; it was the result of extensively cultivating pure deeds and unsurpassed practices that cannot be destroyed.

The bhikṣuṇī known as Siṃhavijṛmbhitā thoroughly understands that the nature and characteristics of all phenomena are like illusions; she has cultivated merit in the past, nurtured roots of goodness, and brought the five powers to maturity, yet remains free from attachment.

This king’s grove is vast, magnificent, and pure; it universally accommodates the entire trichiliocosm, such that devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, kiṃnaras, garuḍas, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and all others gather together and enter this royal grove without any crowding.

Why is this? It is all due to the majestic spiritual power of the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā; these inconceivable supernormal transformations all arise from the ocean of the Bodhisattva’s original vows.

At that time, the youth Sudhana saw everywhere beneath all the jewel trees lion thrones; upon each throne sat a bhikṣuṇī named Siṃhavijṛmbhitā. She was upright, majestic, and sublime, her deportment composed and orderly. Her mind was perfectly tranquil, and she had subdued her sense faculties like a great elephant. Like a wish-fulfilling gem, she universally satisfied the aspirations of all; like a lotus flower, her mind was free from attachment. Like a lion king, she held all creatures in awe with her majesty; she dwelt unmoving due to the markless precepts (*animitta-śīla*). Her mind was pure, having eliminated afflictions (*kleśa*) just as a supreme incense king dispels foul odors. Like a great medicinal king adorned with all medicines, she eradicated all maladies like a sovereign panacea. Those who beheld her with a virtuous mind could have their various ailments removed, while those who beheld her with an unvirtuous mind would instead suffer harm as if by poison.

The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is also like this: for those with karmic conditions and those without karmic conditions, he preaches the subtle and wondrous Dharma. Those with karmic conditions see my form and hear my voice, and immediately attain the unimpeded dhāraṇī;
sentient beings without karmic conditions further increase their evil deeds;
and indeterminate sentient beings immediately attain a virtuous mind.
Just as the celestial palace of Pāruṣyaka is exquisitely adorned and universally bestowed upon the world, making all things pure and nurturing roots of goodness like a fertile field of merit;

so too did she see this seat surrounded by various great assemblies, or surrounded by the retinues of the Śuddhāvāsa devas, or surrounded by the retinues of Maheśvara. All these hosts of devas gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with eyes that never for a moment wavered.
At that time, the bhikṣuṇī preached for the assembly of Śuddhāvāsa devas and Maheśvara and the others the inexhaustible Dharma-gate and the practice of the Dharma of non-reception.
Furthermore, I saw the Devaputra Kāmarati surrounded by his retinue, gazing at the bhikṣuṇī with single-minded devotion, his eyes never for a moment wavering;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī, for the sake of the assembly of desire-realm devas, preached the Dharma-door of the Inquiry into Purity through the Sound of Universal Radiance.

Furthermore, he saw this seat surrounded by the sovereign heavenly king, sons of gods, and daughters of gods as their retinue, who gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with undivided attention, their eyes never wavering for a moment;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī, for the sake of the assembly of the Sovereign Heaven, expounded the Dharma-gate of the "Sovereign Purity of the Names of Bodhisattvas."

Furthermore, he saw this seat surrounded by the celestial king of the Nirmāṇarati Heaven, along with his sons, daughters, and retinue, who gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with eyes never for a moment wavering;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī was expounding for the assembly of the Yāma Heaven the Dharma-gate of the Pure Adornment of All Dharmas.

Furthermore, he saw this seat surrounded by the Tuṣita Heaven King, along with his sons, daughters, and retinue, who gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with undivided attention, their eyes never for a moment averting.

At that time, the bhikṣuṇī, for the sake of the assembly of Tuṣita devas, expounded the Dharma-gate of the *Anle xin zang xuan fu zizai wuai dharani* (The Dharani of the Treasury of the Mind of Peace and Bliss, Revolving and Returning with Sovereign Unimpededness).
Furthermore, he saw the King of the Yāma Heaven on this seat, surrounded by his retinue, gazing intently at that bhikṣuṇī with undivided attention, his eyes never for a moment wavering;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī was expounding for the assembly of the Yāma Heaven a dharma-gate on the manifestation of immeasurable, pure, and sublime adornments.
Furthermore, he saw that this seat was surrounded by the retinue of Śakra Devānām Indra, who gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with their eyes never wavering for a moment;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī, for the sake of the assembly of Śakra-devas, expounded the Dharma-gate of impurity, patience, weary detachment, impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self.

Furthermore, he saw this seat occupied by the Dragon King Sagara, who understands emptiness, surrounded by his retinue including the Dragon King Daśaprabha; the Dragon King Nanda and the Dragon King Upananda, surrounded by their retinues; and the Dragon Kings Manasvin, Enapanada, and Anavatapta, each surrounded by their own retinues of dragon sons and dragon daughters. With single-minded attention, they gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī, their eyes never wavering for a moment.
At that time, the bhikṣuṇī, for the sake of these dragon kings, expounded the Dharma gate of skillful means for universal protection.

Furthermore, he saw the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra upon this seat, surrounded by a retinue of male and female gandharvas, both great and small, all of whom gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with undivided attention, their eyes never wavering for a moment;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī preached for them the Dharma-gate of Inexhaustible Joy.
Furthermore, he saw that this seat was surrounded by the retinues of mahoragas and asura kings, who gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with undivided attention, their eyes never wavering for a moment;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī expounded for them the Dharma-gate of the Swift Wisdom Adorned with the Dharma-realm.

Furthermore, he saw this seat surrounded by the male and female, great and small, retinues of the Garuḍa King Mahādeva-śakti, who gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with eyes never wavering for a moment;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī expounded for them the Dharma-gate of fearlessness in crossing the ocean of birth and death.

Furthermore, he saw the Kinnara King Good Sound (Sughoṣa) and his retinue—men, women, elders, and children—surrounding him, all gazing intently at that bhikṣuṇī with undivided attention, their eyes never wavering for a moment;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī was preaching for them the Dharma-gate of the Buddha’s Original Conduct, Pure and Unattached.

Furthermore, he saw this seat surrounded by male and female mahoraga kings—their children and attendants of all ages—gathered like clouds at its golden corners; with single-minded attention, they gazed intently upon that bhikṣuṇī, their eyes never wavering for a moment.
At that time, the bhikṣuṇī expounded for them the Dharma-gate of the Universal Gathering of the Joy of All Buddhas.

Furthermore, I saw this seat surrounded by an immeasurable number of men and women, boys and girls, as their retinue gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with undivided attention, their eyes never for a moment leaving her;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī was expounding for them the Dharma-gate of the Unsurpassed.

Furthermore, she saw this seat surrounded by a retinue of rākṣasa kings and others who constantly feed on the vital essence of sentient beings; they gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with single-minded attention, their eyes never wavering for a moment.
At that time, the bhikṣuṇī expounded for them the Dharma-gate of the Universal Contemplation of Compassion.
Furthermore, he saw that all the ordained śrāvakas had gathered and were seated together in this assembly;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī was expounding for them the supreme Dharma-gate of the Radiance of Wisdom.
Furthermore, he saw those who had left the household life and delighted in the path of the pratyekabuddhas, all coming together to sit in the assembly;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī expounded for them the Dharma-gate of the Pure and Radiant Buddha’s Merits.
Furthermore, he saw those who had left the household life and delighted in the Mahāyāna, surrounded by their retinues, all coming together to sit in the assembly;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī was expounding for them the Dharma-gate of the Samādhi of the Light of Universal-Gate Wisdom.

Furthermore, he saw that this seat was surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas who had first resolved their minds toward enlightenment; with single-minded attention, they gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī, their eyes never wavering for a moment.
At that time, the bhikṣuṇī expounded for them the Dharma-gate of the Multitude of Great Vows of All Buddhas.

Furthermore, he saw that this seat was surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas of the second bhūmi, who gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with undivided attention, their eyes never wavering for a moment;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī expounded for them the Dharma-gate of the Space-Luminous-Pure Lokeśvararāja Samādhi.

Furthermore, he saw that this seat was surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas of the third stage, who gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with undivided attention, their eyes never wavering for a moment;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī was expounding for them the Dharma-gate of Adorned Tranquility.

Furthermore, he saw that this seat was surrounded by a retinue of Bodhisattvas of the fourth stage, who gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with single-minded attention, their eyes never wavering for a moment;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī expounded for them the Dharma-gate of the power and sphere of all-knowledge (*sarvākārajñatā*).

Furthermore, he saw that this seat was surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas of the fifth stage, who gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with undivided attention, their eyes never wavering for a moment;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī preached for them the Dharma-door of the Universal Collection of the Pure Flower Treasury.
Furthermore, he saw that this seat was surrounded by a retinue of Bodhisattvas of the sixth stage, who gazed at that bhikṣuṇī with single-minded attention, their eyes never for a moment wavering;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī was expounding for them the Dharma-gate of the Transcendent Pure Treasury.

Furthermore, he saw that this seat was surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas of the seventh stage, who gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with undivided attention, their eyes never wavering for a moment;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī was expounding for them the Dharma-gate of the Universal Reliance on the Pure Earth-Treasury.

Furthermore, he saw that this seat was surrounded by a retinue of Bodhisattvas of the eighth stage, who gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with single-minded attention, their eyes never wavering for a moment;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī expounded for them the Dharma-door of the Universal Manifestation of the Dharmakāya throughout All Space Realms, titled the *Viloma-ga* (Pervasive) of the Dharma-realm.

Furthermore, he saw that this seat was surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas of the ninth stage, who gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with undivided attention, their eyes never wavering for a moment;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī expounded for them the Dharma-gate of the Adornment of the Power of Unobstructed and Unattached Purity.

Furthermore, he saw that this seat was surrounded by a retinue of Bodhisattvas of the ten stages, who gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with single-minded attention, their eyes never wavering for a moment;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī expounded for them the Dharma-gate of the Samādhi of the Perfect and Unobstructed Vimalakīrti.
Furthermore, he saw this seat surrounded by a retinue of Vajrapāṇi spirits, who gazed intently at that bhikṣuṇī with undivided attention, their eyes never wavering for a moment;
at that time, the bhikṣuṇī expounded for them the Dharma-gate of the Samādhi of the Nārāyaṇa-Vajra Mark Adorned with Wisdom.

Thus, for all these great assemblies, all sentient beings, and all those in the various realms of existence who are ready to be transformed, as well as all their retinues who have planted roots of goodness—according to the various desires, various conducts, and various paths of those sentient beings, and for those who delight in hearing many teachings—in order to nurture roots of goodness, to increase roots of goodness, and to adorn roots of goodness, he reveals and expounds *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* as appropriate to each, turning the irreversible wheel of Dharma so that all sentient beings may attain the irreversible wheel.

Why is this? Because these are all the Lion’s Vigorous Stride Bhikṣuṇīs, who have accomplished the dharma-gate of the light of wisdom of the universal eye that relinquishes all things, and who have accomplished the dharma-gate of penetrating without obstruction the signless and pure dharma-realm of all Buddhas.

This bhikṣuṇī has accomplished the dharma-gate of the stainless, unimpeded, and pure secret treasury; she has accomplished the dharma-gate of the perfect and inconceivable pure treasury; she has accomplished the dharma-gate of the pure treasury of universal joyful vision; she has accomplished hundreds of thousands of billions of incalculable prajñāpāramitās; she has accomplished the prajñāpāramitā of the universal eye; and she has accomplished the prajñāpāramitā that is indestructible within the dharma-realm of all Buddha-dharmas.

In this royal garden, by the side of the Sunlight Spring, the entire assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and others have all long planted roots of goodness; through the teaching and transformation of this bhikṣuṇī’s Dharma discourse, their minds have become profoundly tranquil, reaching even unto anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and they have attained the stage of non-retrogression.

At that time, the youth Sudhana saw the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā, who had long since accomplished such universal gateways of the Dharma and manifested her form-body to adorn herself, causing the royal gardens, the sun-light springs, the various jewel trees, and the many lion thrones to all display rare and extraordinary wonders. He saw all the members of the great assembly and their retinues seated within the gardens, the walking paths, the meditation caves, and amidst all the necessary precious objects, beds, and curtains; they were fully endowed with merit and spiritual power, and with the eightfold voice, they preached the various sublime Dharmas.

At that time, the youth Sudhana beheld these inconceivable and extraordinary wonders, and heard the eight kinds of subtle sounds, as well as an inconceivable, pure, and wondrous voice proclaiming and praising the Dharma-gate of the emptiness of immeasurable phenomena. By means of this Dharma-gate, his body and mind were moistened and made entirely supple; this is called the peerless Dharma-gate of the Counteractive Treatment of the True Dharma. Having attained this Dharma-gate, his body and mind were filled with joy, and he suddenly attained great awakening, accomplishing all the great Dharma-gates. With palms joined in reverence, he circumambulated [the deity] a hundred thousand times and then prostrated himself before him.

Before he had even raised his head, he saw a bhikṣuṇī upon every one of the lion thrones, emitting a great radiance of brilliant golden hue that illuminated the king’s grove and all its trees like a mass of light-clouds. By the power of this radiance, all the trees circled to the right around her countless times; these trees, arranged in orderly rows, each emitted their own light, which in turn illuminated the bhikṣuṇī.
At that time, having beheld these signs, the youth Sudhana joined his palms and stood respectfully; he withdrew a short distance and stood to one side, addressing the Great Sage:
"I have already set my mind upon Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi; I only pray that the Great Sage, out of compassion and pity, will explain this for me."
"I do not now know how to learn the conduct of a bodhisattva or cultivate the path of a bodhisattva.
I only pray that the Great Sage will explain this for me.
At that time, the bhikṣuṇī replied to Sudhana:
“Excellent, excellent,
son of good family!
I now know this omniscience, which can universally reveal and manifest the bottomless Dharma-gate.”
The youth Sudhana said:
"O Great Sage!
What is the essential nature of this bottomless dharma-gate of all-knowledge?"
Then the bhikṣuṇī replied to Sudhana, saying:
"Good man! This is the Dharma-gate of the Adornment of the Light of Wisdom of the Great Sages of the Three Times."
The youth Sudhana said,
“O Great Sage!
What is the scope of the Dharma-door of the Adornment of the Wisdom-Light of the Buddhas of the Three Times?”
He replied: "Good son!

One who enters this Dharma-door attains the profound penetration of the present analytical meditative absorption (*samāpatti*), the Samādhi Adorned by the Forest of the Equality of All Dharmas as Neither Arising nor Ceasing. Abiding in this samādhi, one immediately obtains the sovereign supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) of mastery. Here in Jambudvīpa, one manifests in the Tuṣita Heaven; likewise, in as many Tuṣita Heavens as there are atoms in the infinite worlds of the ten directions, one does the same. In each of those places, before each Buddha, one manifests infinite and innumerable bodies. From one's own body, one produces as many oceans of Buddha-lands as there are atoms, manifesting *maṇi* bodies, to pay respectful homage and cultivate various meritorious deeds."

Furthermore, they brought forth clouds of various colored flowers in numbers as vast as the atoms of unspeakably unspeakable worlds; clouds of various colored necklaces, in numbers as vast as the atoms of unspeakably unspeakable worlds; clouds of various colored jewel garlands, in numbers as vast as the atoms of unspeakably unspeakable worlds; clouds of various colored ointments and powdered incenses, in numbers as vast as the atoms of unspeakably unspeakable worlds; clouds of various colored silk canopies, banners, and pennants, in numbers as vast as the atoms of unspeakably unspeakable worlds; clouds of various colored jewel nets and jewel curtains, in numbers as vast as the atoms of unspeakably unspeakable worlds; and clouds of various colored jewel thrones, in numbers as vast as the atoms of unspeakably unspeakable worlds. Before each throne was a cloud of light-flame adornments, unspeakably unspeakable in number, and each light-flame was further adorned with clusters of various precious jewels.
...up to clouds of all manner of unspeakably unspeakable multicolored ornaments, offered to the Tathāgatas;

furthermore, carrying clouds of unspeakably unspeakable multicolored fragrant waters, from within these clouds of fragrant water emerged clouds of unspeakably unspeakable lotuses of various jewels; from these clouds of lotuses of various jewels emerged clouds of unspeakably unspeakable celestial necklaces and ornaments, as well as ornaments of various jewel-lights, up to the clouds of all the celestial offerings of the gods in Akaniṣṭha;
furthermore, from the fragrant waters emerged unspeakably unspeakable numbers of universal monarchs (*cakravartin*), minor kings, and clouds of all the worldly offerings of every realm.

Furthermore, from the fragrant waters emerge unspeakably unspeakable numbers of nāgas, devas, and the eight classes of beings, as well as clouds of all kinds of unspeakably unspeakable articles of offering, making offerings to the Tathāgata.

Throughout all places, all Bodhisattvas—residing in the Tuṣita Heaven, manifesting by descending into their mothers’ wombs riding upon white elephants, being born in royal palaces, renouncing home to study the Way, proceeding to the Bodhi tree to attain Equal and Perfect Enlightenment, turning the pure Wheel of Dharma, ascending to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven to preach the Dharma for their mothers, and exercising sovereign mastery in transformations among devas and humans until their parinirvāṇa—have planted the roots of myriad virtues under various Buddhas. By the power of the causes and conditions of these original vows, they manifest māṇava-colored bodies, making offerings to all Buddhas in every place; their various articles of offering are likewise thus.
All these various kinds of offering implements arise through the power of having long cultivated great vows to adorn the Dharma-realm.
If there are sentient beings who know that I have cultivated such offerings as these, they shall all attain non-retrogression from Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.
If there are sentient beings who come to me, I immediately teach them the Mahāprajñāpāramitā, instructing, exhorting, benefiting, and gladdening them, saying:
"O son of good family!..."
You should now know this: I am always without the perception of sentient beings and do not cling to the perception of sentient beings, because sentient beings are without marks;
I understand all words and sounds, yet I do not cling to sounds, because sounds have no intrinsic nature or marks.
They behold the marks and signs of the radiance of all Buddhas, yet they do not cling to those marks and signs.
Why is this? Because they profoundly understand that the Dharma-body is devoid of form and characteristics.

They uphold the Dharma wheels of all Buddhas, yet they do not cling to the characteristics of those Dharma wheels, because with their profound mind they have thoroughly understood the true suchness, the limit of reality, and the nature of phenomena.

In every moment of thought, they pervade and fill the entirety of space and the dharma-realm, yet they do not cling to the characteristics of the dharma-realm, for they skillfully understand that all phenomena are like illusions and transformations.
"Good son!
I know only this Dharma-door of the Omniscient Wisdom, which universally reveals and manifests the boundless teachings of the Bodhisattvas. Good son!"

You should now know that all great Bodhisattvas have reached the ultimate limit of the Dharma-realm; they are unattached to any Bodhisattva sphere and are able, with a single body, to sit cross-legged and fill all worlds throughout the ten directions. Within their own bodies, they can manifest all the wondrous adornments of the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, and in every single moment, they travel throughout the ten directions to pay homage and serve all Buddhas.

Within his own body, he is able to universally manifest the supernatural transformations and the power of the vows of all Buddhas; he can bind all Mount Sumerus throughout the ten directions with a single hair and lift them to place them within immeasurable worlds in other quarters; from every single pore, he universally manifests the signs of the formation and destruction of all worlds throughout the ten directions across kalpas; and in a single kṣaṇa, he universally gathers and sustains sentient beings throughout unspeakably unspeakable kalpas in the ten directions, never abandoning them.
As for these great Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, who are fully endowed with the practices of the ocean of all profound wisdom, how could I possibly know or describe their merits and vows?
“Good son! From here, travel south;

there is a land named Kṣema and a city named Ratnavyūha. Within that city, there is a woman named Vāsukī. Go to her and ask: ‘How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?’”
At that time, the youth Sudhana paid homage at the feet of the bhikṣuṇī Siṃhavijṛmbhitā by bowing his head to the ground; gazing up at her with deep reverence, he took his leave and traveled south.
The youth Sudhana, having attained the great light of wisdom to illumine his mind and being fully endowed with the cultivation of all roots of goodness,
desiring to teach and transform all sentient beings, single-mindedly contemplated the true reality (*dharmatā*) of all phenomena.
He established the treasury of *dhāraṇīs* of pure dharma-water and speech, and extensively practiced the upholding of them.
The Sarvadharma-cakra-dhāraṇī, which accomplishes the power of contemplation, serves as a refuge for sentient beings through the great compassion that is the power of all worlds;
it skillfully contemplates the omniscience that fills the dharma-realm,
swiftly contemplating all pure dharmas, and vows to universally observe the gateway of radiant light, adorning the ten [directions].
By the power of universal illumination, he completely filled the entire dharma-realm;
having ultimately perfected all bodhisattva practices and bodhisattva deeds, and being endowed with the fulfillment of his vow-power and all supernatural faculties,
he gradually traveled until he reached the city of Ratnavyūha in the perilous land, where he inquired after the venerable lady Vasumitrā.
"Where is she now? The people within the city thought to themselves:
"We have never heard that this woman possesses profound wisdom, skillfully restrains her sense faculties, or maintains such tranquility of body and mind."

Now this youth is dignified and composed in his deportment; his mind is tranquil and serene, having subdued all the sense faculties. He is far removed from negligence, perversion, and delusion; mindfulness and wisdom are present before him. His gaze is careful and discerning, and his speech is harmonious and elegant. He does not cling to forms or colors, but contemplates the profound characteristics of phenomena with right mindfulness. His mind is free from weariness like the great ocean; he is no one who is defiled by desire or subject to perversion. Without thoughts of sensual passion, he does not sink into the mire of desire. Not following after the sense faculties, he has transcended the realm of Māra and cannot be bound by any of the Māras.
Since this youth is endowed with such manifold virtues, for what reason does he inquire about this woman on account of her physical form?
In this city there are many people who have not even heard the name of this woman, let alone know her.
A certain person said:
“Excellent, excellent! Well-spoken, son of good family!”
"You shall surely obtain great benefit now that you are able to question the Venerable Vasumitra.

According to the intent of your questions, you must have already previously resolved upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*; for the sake of all sentient beings, you will certainly be able to forever leave behind the arrows of lust, anger, and delusion, maintain unshakable pure perception, remain unattached to the impure, and universally liberate all who are bound by fetters."
"Noble son!
This venerable Vāsumitra is currently staying within a magnificent pavilion in the Joyful Garden to the north of this city."

At that time, having heard these words, the youth Sudhana was filled with joy and leaped for gladness. He went to that place and stood by the side of the gate, joining his palms in reverence and gazing into the garden. He beheld that palace and residence, vast, magnificent, and pure, surrounded on all sides by ten rows of precious walls. Ten lines of precious *tāla* trees were planted in orderly rows, and ten tiers of precious moats contained water of deep clarity endowed with the eight virtues, filling them to the brim. *Utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka* flowers bloomed in fresh splendor, covering the surface of the water. The bottom was strewn with golden sand, the jeweled banks were magnificent and beautiful, and various colored radiances pervaded the entire grove.
The jeweled palaces and towers were pure and magnificently adorned; fragrant breezes from the ornate windows gladdened the hearts of all.
Nets decorated with linked coins and crescent moons hung about, while Vajrapāṇi spirits glared with wrath and brandished their maces.
Mighty lion-kings, their tails lashing, roared in defiance as they stood in attendance by the palace gates. At the four corners of the city walls, there were luminous [lamps].
The jeweled pillars and the various precious pavilions emit all manner of light; rainfalls of precious jewel-flowers accumulate up to the knees.
The ground of pure lapis lazuli appears as if suspended in space, with the king of wish-fulfilling jewels reflecting from beneath the earth.
Channels of purple-gold flow with fragrant, colored water, upon which golden lotuses bloom in full splendor. From the lotuses...
From the flower pedestals surged wondrous sounds of water, broadcasting the flow of Dharma-voices that resounded throughout the ten directions;
golden plantain trees emitted great radiance, and precious jewels were piled everywhere like mountain ridges;

clouds of agarwood incense swirled and turned in graceful circles, while powdered and ground incenses perfumed the palace city, and flocks of birds of diverse species sang in harmonious and elegant tones.

A vast precious canopy was spread, from which hung clusters of golden flowers; mani-jewel bells were interspersed with various gems, and a net of Jambūnada gold covered the palace walls. Hundreds of thousands of millions of priceless precious incenses were burned, their fragrant smoke filling the void of space. Innumerable devas stood in attendance to make offerings; celestial music played spontaneously without being struck. Various auspicious vases filled with wish-fulfilling jewels sprang forth from the earth, while there rained down clouds of immeasurable celestial jewel-flowers, clouds of immeasurable celestial jewel-incense, clouds of immeasurable banners, pennants, and jeweled parasols, clouds of immeasurable celestial garments and necklaces, and clouds of immeasurable celestial music and sounds.
Such various clouds of offering implements each emitted immeasurable rays of light that pervaded the void and illuminated the worlds of the ten directions.

Within the palace, immeasurable tens of billions of vajra-treasure repositories were filled to overflowing; each jewel garden was intricately carved and engraved, with their radiant lights mutually reflecting one another in unobstructed clarity.
Furthermore, it was surrounded by immeasurable tenfold jewel gardens, exquisitely adorned and infinitely pure.

The Venerable Vasumitra was of exquisite and subtle beauty, like a flower in full bloom; his marks and signs were complete, and his body was the color of pure gold. He was neither tall nor short, neither stout nor lean; his eyelashes were deep blue like the petals of a blue lotus, and his hair and beard were soft and lustrous, a brilliant deep blue in color. His deportment was perfectly composed and his movements were dignified and orderly. His hands and feet were fresh and radiant, marked with the sign of the thousand-spoked wheel; even the queens of the six heavens of the desire realm could not compare to him. His voice surpassed that of Brahmā, and he understood all languages. He was well-versed in worldly crafts and arts, profoundly penetrating the roots of all treatises, and had thoroughly mastered the methods of debate. He was skilled in the meaning of words, adept at discerning correct wisdom, and possessed skillful means regarding the realm of illusion.

He is well-versed in the bodhisattva’s dharma-gate of skillful means and well-versed in the bodhisattva’s dharma-realm of skillful means. His body is adorned with the various marks and signs as if with necklaces; his mani-jewel crown emits great radiance, and the bright pearl of the mind-king serves as his flower garland. He is surrounded by the retinue of his original vows; his merit is fully perfected and indestructible. He possesses an inexhaustible treasury of jewels of merit, and from his body issues forth light that universally illumines all. This is the light of benefit, the light of gentleness, the light of joy, the light that opens the mind, and the light that adorns the bodhisattva’s path of the mind. With these lights, he adorns the minds of all sentient beings; those who encounter this light attain liberation from the five desires and uproot the foundations of all suffering.
At that time, the youth Sudhana went to where the Venerable Vasumitra was, joined his palms in reverence, and said:
"O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind upon Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, yet I do not yet know how to learn the conduct of a bodhisattva or cultivate the path of a bodhisattva."
He replied, "Good son!
I know only this single dharma-door of the Bodhisattva, which is the adornment of the one hundred million who are free from desire and undefiled."
Good son! If a deva sees me, I appear in the form of a celestial maiden, adorned with celestial light and necklaces, pervading all places;
if a human sees me, I adorn myself with supreme, wondrous beauty and a heart of pure compassion, appearing in the form of a young girl.
When non-humans see me, I manifest in the form of a non-human woman, exquisite and most wonderful, throughout all non-human realms.

If there should be sentient beings who come to my presence and give rise to lust, anger, or delusion, such a thing is impossible; they shall instead receive the true Dharma of the Bodhisattva’s non-appropriation, and I shall constantly preach for them the Dharma-gate of pure liberation and the departure from suffering.
Those who hear my name shall attain the contemplation of weary detachment and swiftly achieve the samādhi of merit; their bodies and minds will be tranquil and free from all obstacles.
Those who behold my form shall immediately attain the samādhi of joy;
those who hear my voice shall immediately attain the samādhi of the treasury of immeasurable sounds.

Those who hear my name shall immediately attain refuge in the Triple Gem of the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha, and shall immediately attain the Samādhi of Universal Manifestation of Form in all Buddha-fields;
if there are sentient beings who dwell together with me, they shall immediately attain the Samādhi of the Light of Liberation;
if there are sentient beings who contemplate me with focused attention, they shall immediately attain the Samādhi of Tranquil Adornment.
If there are those who see me yawning and stretching, they shall attain the Samādhi of the Dispersion and Destruction of Externalists;
if there are sentient beings who observe me, they shall attain the Samādhi of the Radiance of the Realm of All Buddhas;
if there are sentient beings who speak with me, they shall immediately attain the Samādhi of the Treasury that Protects and Gathers in All Sentient Beings.
If there are sentient beings who scratch me when I am itchy, they shall immediately attain the Flower-Treasury Samādhi of the Accumulation of All Virtues;

if there are sentient beings who draw near to me, they shall immediately attain the Dharma-gate of the Immaculate, Desire-Free Adornment of a Bodhisattva’s Boundless, Radiant, and Pure Realm of Universal Wisdom.
Sudhana the youth said:
"O Great Sage!
In the past, where did you cultivate what merit, plant what roots of goodness, and perform what deeds to attain this Dharma-door?"
He replied: "Good son!
In the past, there was a Buddha named Aruṇavata-caryā Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-carana-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavat."

At that time, the Tathāgata Unstained Conduct appeared in the world; out of compassion and for the benefit of all sentient beings, he set out toward the city of Samantabhadra and arrived at its borders.

When he lifted his foot, the lands, cities, and towns shook in six ways; when he set his foot down, mounds, ruins, pits, and hollows were all naturally leveled, and the sky became clear and bright, spontaneously solemn and pure.

At that time, as the World-Honored One stepped upon the threshold of the gate, the great earth immediately shook once more; tiles, rubble, and walls were transformed into the seven treasures. A profusion of various jewel-flowers scattered and remained suspended in the air, covering the palace city in hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis. Celestial musical instruments, adorned with myriad jewels, hung in the void and resounded spontaneously without being struck. Innumerable devas, each accompanied by their own palaces, stood in attendance in the sky, prostrating at the Buddha’s feet and raining down celestial flowers as an offering to the Buddha.
When the Buddha entered the city, he emitted golden light like a mountain of gold.

At that time, I was born in that city as the wife of an elder, also named Vasumitrā; seeing the Buddha’s physical body, complete with its marks, signs, radiance, and supernormal powers, my roots of goodness from past lives were immediately awakened.

At that time, I, together with my husband, the elder, went quickly to where the Buddha was. I immediately removed the priceless jewel I was wearing and scattered it over the Buddha; the scattered jewels all remained suspended in mid-air as I prostrated at his feet in worship.
"At that time, the youth Mañjuśrī was the Buddha’s attendant; Mañjuśrī then addressed me, saying:
'Noble daughter!
You should swiftly resolve to attain the unsurpassed mind of enlightenment.'"
"At that time, I first gave rise to the unsurpassed Bodhicitta.
Vāsukamitrā said to Sudhana:

"I have obtained only this single dharma-door of the 'Adornment of Non-attachment through Ten Million Stains-free Transcendences of Desire. As for the dharma-door of the Samādhi of the Ocean-like Profundity and Vastness of the Great Bodhisattvas' Wisdom, Skillful Means, and Transformation of Sentient Beings—the realm of great wisdom-power that cannot be destroyed or subdued—how could I possibly know or speak of those meritorious practices?"

"Good son! From here, travel south; there is a great city named Śānta. In that city, there is an elder named Abhijña-uccagāmin-guṇarāja. That great elder constantly makes offerings to a precious sandalwood stūpa during the six periods of the day and night. Go to him and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?'"

Then the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at the feet of that woman in respectful salutation, took his leave, and traveling southward by gradual steps, arrived at that great city and went to the householder’s dwelling, saying:
“O Noble One!”
"I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how to learn the conduct of a bodhisattva or cultivate the path of a bodhisattva.

The elder replied: "I have only accomplished the bodhisattva dharma-gate of the non-extinction of the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*). Abiding in this dharma-gate, I now clearly know that all Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, do not enter parinirvāṇa, nor do they enter extinction. The Tathāgatas of the three periods of time never enter nirvāṇa; they possess no mark of nirvāṇa. It is only through the Buddha’s skillful means—because he seeks to deliver sentient beings who are deluded and false—that he manifests nirvāṇa. This is because he desires to cause the relics to be widely disseminated, so as to enable all beings everywhere to enter into the practice of discipline."
"Good son!
If a person can know that the Tathāgata ultimately does not enter parinirvāṇa, that person can open the precious sandalwood stūpa.
Good son!"
"You should now go there to pay homage and make offerings.

Sudhana the youth immediately went to the site of the stupa and prostrated himself with his head at the feet [of the Buddha] to pay respectful homage. As he opened the sandalwood stupa, throughout the continuous succession of his thoughts, he attained the Dharma-gate of the Inexhaustible Samādhi of the Perfectly Radiant, Pure, and Inexhaustible Buddha-nature.

“Good son! In every single moment, my mind constantly enters into meditative absorption (*samādhi*). Within that absorption, I attain the immeasurable and innumerable *Samādhi of Perfect Radiance and Purity*, and in every thought-moment, I enter the stages of progressive advancement.”
The youth Sudhana said:
"O Great Sage!
What is the scope of this Dharma-door?"
He replied: "Good son!

When I enter this samādhi, I universally enter the gateways of all samādhi paths. By the power of this samādhi, I am able to see immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions—Tathāgatas, Arhats, Samyaksaṃbuddhas named Kāśyapa—as well as immeasurable oceans of worlds in each of the ten directions, numbering as many as the atoms in a Ganges River, each containing Tathāgatas likewise named Kāśyapa."
The Buddha Kanakamuni, as well as the Buddhas named Kanakamuni in world-oceans numbering as many as the atoms in immeasurable Ganges-sands in the ten directions;
the Tathāgata Śikhin, as well as the Tathāgatas named Śikhin in world-oceans numbering as many as the atoms in immeasurable Ganges-sands in the ten directions;
and the Tathāgata Vipaśyin, as well as the Tathāgatas named Vipaśyin in world-oceans numbering as many as the atoms in immeasurable Ganges-sands in the ten directions.
The Tathāgata Tiṣya, as well as the Tathāgatas of the same name Tiṣya in world-oceans numbering as many as the atoms in immeasurable Ganges-sands in the ten directions;
the Tathāgata Puṣya, as well as the Tathāgatas of the same name Puṣya in world-oceans numbering as many as the atoms in immeasurable Ganges-sands in the ten directions;

and the Unsurpassed Victorious Buddha, as well as the Buddhas of the same name Unsurpassed Victorious in world-oceans numbering as many as the atoms in immeasurable Ganges-sands in the ten directions.

The Unsurpassed Lotus Buddha, as well as those in the oceans of worlds throughout the ten directions—numbering as many as the atoms in immeasurable Ganges Rivers—who are all likewise named the Unsurpassed Lotus Buddha.
In this way, the practices of these immeasurable Buddhas proceed one after another without mutual obstruction.

Within the white tuft of hair between the eyebrows (*ūrṇā-kośa*) of a single Tathāgata, all the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions are reflected; likewise, within the white tufts of hair of all the immeasurable Buddhas of the ten directions, a single Buddha is reflected. The light from the pores of all these Buddhas reflects one another in the same manner, as they sit within the sandalwood stūpas.

In a single instant, I beheld all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, their minds succeeding one another without any interval or gap. Furthermore, in that same instant, I saw as many Buddhas as there are atoms in Jambudvīpa; then I saw as many as there are atoms in hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of Jambudvīpas; and even as many Buddhas as there are atoms in unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds, like the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions. Beyond these numbers, I saw Buddhas as numerous as infinite and boundless atoms, even unto Buddhas as numerous as the atoms in unspeakable oceans of worlds.
