Furthermore, they saw all Buddhas from their initial aspiration, sporting with spiritual powers in unimpeded mastery; they also saw the fulfillment and discernment of the merits of all great vows and pure, wondrous practices through the Dharma-door of non-duality; they also saw the successive stages of all Bodhisattvas—the fulfillment of the *pāramitās* of vows and the purity of the *pāramitās*—whereby they attained universal patience and pure spiritual play, nurtured roots of goodness, subdued the four Māras, matured sentient beings, purified Buddha-lands, realized the path to Bodhi, turned the wonderful wheel of Dharma, and radiated great light.
The entire great assembly beheld this sign, their minds succeeding one another in an uninterrupted continuity.
Then, the Bodhisattva Noble Virtue King said to the youth Sudhana: "O noble son!
Do you now see within this sandalwood stupa the Tathāgatas, adorned with immeasurable, pure, radiant, and perfectly bright supernatural powers?
Have they all entered together into the *Vilomaga* samādhi, the wheel of supernatural powers, and the dharma-gate of non-duality?

By the power of this luminous, pure, and non-dual dharma-gate of supernatural penetration, the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, pervade all places, turning the wondrous wheel of Dharma, and fill the entire Dharma-realm with their luminous, pure mirror-bodies.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to the Great Holy One:

“I have now beheld the pure realms of the supernatural play of all Buddhas, and I have heard the sounds of the Buddhas preaching the Dharma with perfect clarity, without impairment to my faculty of hearing. I have received and retained them without forgetting, contemplating them with right mindfulness, not losing a single word or meaning, distinguishing them in their proper sequence, and expounding them for others to instruct, benefit, and gladden them. By the power of wisdom, I distinguish the various teachings of the Buddhas to instruct sentient beings. I see Maitreya and other future Buddhas—hundreds, thousands, hundreds of thousands, billions, and as many as *akṣobhya-vibhava-a-saṃkhyeya* Buddhas—and in every thought-moment, in an instant, my mind’s contemplation is bright and pure.”

I also see, throughout future eons, sentient beings as numerous as the atoms in unspeakably, unspeakably many worlds, equal to the sands of the Ganges, who resolve their minds upon Bodhicitta, cultivate the Bodhisattva path, practice the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, fulfill the six *pāramitās*, sport with supernormal powers, transform sentient beings, purify Buddha-lands, take up the auspicious grass, sit beneath the Bodhi tree, subdue the four Māras, attain equal and perfect enlightenment, turn the wondrous wheel of Dharma, radiate great light, and manifest *nirvāṇa*.
From the period of the True Dharma and the Semblance Dharma, through the kalpas of formation and destruction, he clearly understands the continuous succession of every thought-moment.
Just as he perceives this present realm, so it is with future lands and the worlds of the ten directions.

I also see all the present Buddhas—Vairocana Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, and others, immeasurable and innumerable—from their initial generation of the mind of enlightenment, through sitting at the site of awakening, turning the wondrous wheel of Dharma, and manifesting parinirvāṇa; as well as the duration of the True Dharma and the Semblance Dharma, the number of kalpas of formation and destruction, and the length of time they remain in the world.
As it is with this world, so it is in all ten directions.
When the fire calamity arises at the end of an eon, all Buddha-lands throughout the ten directions and the three periods of time will become even more clearly manifest within these sandalwood stupas.

Furthermore, they hear all the Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time—those who have already taught, those who are currently teaching, and those who will teach—and by the power of their wisdom, they are able to receive and uphold them all, surpassing the reach of all worldly beings, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and even lesser bodhisattvas.
“Good son! I know only this Bodhisattva Dharma-door of the Adornment of Equality of the Reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi), which is neither arising nor ceasing.
All great Bodhisattvas, in a single thought-moment, fully know that the fundamental limit of the Buddhas’ teachings throughout the three periods of time is equal.”
In a single instant, they adorned the ocean-gates of the realms of immeasurable samādhis;
they dwelt in the reality-limit (bhūtakoṭi), free from the marks of self and other, and without dualistic intent.
They abided where the Buddhas abide, possessing no fear toward anything, dwelling in the Dharma-realm of joy, pure and adorned, like the noble ones of the three vehicles.
True wisdom is equal and non-dual; it is unattached to the world and the fruits of the world.
The seals and the methods of receiving prediction from all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time completely fill the Dharma-realm, abiding eternally and never ceasing.
The voices of all Tathāgatas pervade the Dharma-realm, which is inconceivable and immeasurable.
They are boundless and cannot be fully described; how could I possibly know or speak of those meritorious practices? Good son!

To the south of here, there is a solitary mountain named Vajramaṇḍala-alaṃkāra-abhyudgata; on its summit dwells a bodhisattva named Avalokiteśvara. Go to him and ask: how does a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?

Then the youth Sudhana, having prostrated his head at the feet of the Bodhisattva Noble Virtuous King, circumambulated him a hundred thousand times, gazing up at him with longing and reverence, and took his leave to travel south.
At that time, the youth Sudhana, with right mindfulness, contemplated the instructions of that elder; he followed the treasury of the Bodhisattva’s liberation,
maintained right mindfulness of the various powers of a Bodhisattva’s recollection, and, sustained by the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha and the power of the Buddha’s original vows,
through the correct reception of samādhi, remained constantly in every thought-moment without interruption or gap.
Mindfully recollecting the immeasurable Buddhas within the sandalwood jewel stupa, he wept with compassion as tears fell like rain; proceeding along the path,
he sequentially distinguished all the Buddhas and their various Dharmas, and within a single mind, he adorned the supernatural powers,
mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom of the Buddhas, desiring to nurture the roots of goodness of Bodhi while contemplating the Right [Dharma].
Mindfully recollecting the inconceivable deeds of all Buddhas, he gradually traveled until he reached that solitary mountain;
climbing step by step, he remained mindful of Avalokiteśvara, never abandoning right mindfulness.

From afar he saw [the Bodhisattva] walking in meditation on the western slope of the cliff; everywhere there were flowing springs and flowering trees, with groves and ponds of clear, limpid water, fragrant golden flowers, and lush green grasses—soft, fresh, and pure—all produced from the merit of the Bodhisattva.

Upon reaching the summit of that mountain, he saw Avalokiteśvara seated upon an eight-sided adamantine throne. Light radiated from the seat, its adornments beyond compare, as he taught the Dharma while surrounded by an immeasurable retinue of bodhisattvas.

At that time, Avalokiteśvara, his body the color of pure gold, holding a great compassionate white jewel lotus in his hand, preached the Sūtra of Great Compassion, exhorting and gathering in all sentient beings to enter the Dharma-door of Manifestation through the Universal Gateway.

At that time, having seen him, the youth Sudhana leaped for joy, unable to contain himself; filled with a sense of wonder, he joined his palms and gazed intently, not averting his eyes for a moment, and thought to himself:

"A spiritual friend is the Tathāgata; a spiritual friend is the true cause of the Buddha-way; a spiritual friend is a cloud of the Dharma-treasure; a spiritual friend is a treasury of meritorious deeds; a spiritual friend is the wondrous jewel of the ten powers; a spiritual friend is difficult to see and difficult to encounter, most supreme and peerless, and unfathomable; a spiritual friend is the practice of the twelve dhūtas as the true cause; a spiritual friend is an inexhaustible treasury of wisdom; a spiritual friend gives birth to the sprouts and stems of merit; a spiritual friend can open and reveal the gateway to all-knowledge (sarvajñatā); a spiritual friend can enable all sentient beings to enter the ocean of omniscience (sarvajña) and the ultimate, pure, unsurpassed realm of Buddha-nature and bodhi."
Having thus praised the spiritual friend, Sudhana gradually drew near.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara saw Sudhana from afar and said in praise:
"Excellent, excellent!"
Welcome, young man! You who single-mindedly seek the Mahāyāna, who embrace sentient beings and protect all living beings, who have given rise to a mind of gentleness,
a mind of uprightness, a profound mind, and a mind that seeks the Buddha-dharma, and who have aroused great compassion— come forward!
The conduct of Samantabhadra is the practice of purifying all great vows; it is the accomplishment of the adornments of all great vows;

it is the constant joy in receiving and upholding the precious clouds of all Buddha-dharma without the mind ever diminishing, increasing roots of goodness, cultivating all merits without weariness or satiety, and following spiritual friends without...
Transcending their teachings, he followed the great ocean of Mañjuśrī’s wisdom, bringing his mental activities to maturity.
He attained the Buddha-power Radiance Samādhi; his body and mind became adorned and pure, free from all defilement.
Forever departing from indolence, he never regressed; constantly beholding the Buddhas, his heart was filled with joy, and he remained far removed from all [worldly] attachments.
Abandoning evil, they cultivate all wholesome deeds, achieve wisdom, and possess a mind free from hindrance, as pure as space.
They swiftly attain the Dharma-gate of remediation that transcends suffering, abide in the luminous realm of all Tathāgatas,
guard the city of the Dharma, and widely proclaim the teachings.

At that time, the youth Sudhana went to the place where the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara was, prostrated himself at his feet, circumambulated him a hundred thousand times, joined his palms in reverence, stood to one side, and said:
"O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind on *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should train in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
He replied: "Excellent, excellent!
O son of good family!"
"You have now been able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Son of good family!
I have already accomplished the Dharma-gate of the Great Compassion Samādhi called Vīramatā."
"Good son!
This Vīramagha-samādhi, the Dharma-gate of Great Compassion, is the practice of Bodhisattvas;
all the merit and wisdom of all Bodhisattvas enter into it. By the power of this samādhi, without leaving this seat, they manifest everywhere."
With all pure form-bodies, through the practice of the light of purity via the Dharma-gate of universal manifestation,
they teach and bring to maturity the sentient beings of the six destinies throughout the worlds of the ten directions;
they constantly appear before all Buddhas as appropriate for those to be transformed, either gathering in those who are stingy and greedy through generosity, or...

They gather those who violate the precepts through the observance of ethical discipline; they gather those who harbor anger and affliction through patience; they gather those who are indolent through diligence;
they gather those with distracted minds through meditative concentration; they gather those who are deluded through wisdom;
they accord well with sentient beings through the six points of respectful harmony; and they gather the multitude through the four methods of attraction.
Upon birth, he emits a great net of light that extinguishes the feverish pain of the afflictions of sentient beings;
through the practice of the perfection of skillful means, he gathers in sentient beings by means of giving, kind words, beneficial conduct, and cooperation;
and with subtle voices from his entire net of light, he universally expounds all [teachings] for the sake of all sentient beings throughout the ten directions.
The noble dharma of liberation accomplishes all the pāramitās.

According to the needs of sentient beings, he manifests his body in whatever form—whether that of a Buddha, a bodhisattva, a śrāvaka, or a pratyekabuddha—and with whatever dignified demeanor is required for their deliverance. Seated upon the vajra-seat and holding white flowers in his hands, he expounds for them the noble dharma of liberation, the Dharma-gate of the Great Compassion of the Original Conduct of the Bodhisattva Vīramatiga.

If there are sentient beings who should be delivered by means of the forms, colors, and deportments of the six realms of existence, he manifests bodies of those six realms, sits upon the vajra-seat, and holding white flowers in his hands, preaches for them the holy dharma of liberation—the Dharma-gate of Great Compassion, Vīramāga—causing all those sentient beings to attain joy. With his wondrous form-body, manifesting with sovereign mastery, he displays bodies identical to their own to universally deliver all, conforming to their deportments and even sharing their minds to gather in and sustain sentient beings.

"Good son! I constantly practice this Dharma-gate of Great Compassion, the Bodhisattva Vīramatā’s Samādhi of the Perfect Radiance of Wisdom. Because I made pure vows in the past and have fulfilled them, by the power of the fruit of these pure vows I abide in this Dharma-gate. Therefore, this samādhi-gate is called the 'Dharma-gate of the Samādhi of Vīramatā, the Bodhisattva Practice Endowed with Great Compassion. It teaches and transforms all sentient beings, acting as a house, a refuge, a shelter, and a place of reliance for them; it acts as a great bridge and a great island for sentient beings; it acts as a great torch and a great guide for sentient beings, leading them even to the ultimate destination."
For the sake of transforming sentient beings, I have made great vows so that all who see or hear me may attain joy;
I desire to cause all sentient beings within the five realms of existence to remain far removed from the terrors of perilous and evil paths,
the terrors of feverish affliction, the terrors of ignorance, the terrors of bondage, the terrors of slaughter, and the terrors of poverty.
The fear of poverty, the fear of lack of livelihood, the fear of litigation, the fear of great assemblies, the fear of death,
the fear of falling into the four evil destinies, the fear of the various realms of existence, the fear of disagreement,
the fear of the pleasant and the unpleasant, the fear of all evils, and the fear of physical oppression.
Fearing the terror of a constrained mind, the terror of sorrow and anxiety, the terror of indolence, and the terror of lustful craving for sensual forms;
fearing birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, and despair, as well as the suffering of not obtaining what one seeks,
the suffering of separation from the beloved, and the suffering of encountering the hated— he makes the great vow in order to deliver all sentient beings from the sea of fear and suffering.
"May you dwell in this Dharma-gate of the Radiance of Pure Wisdom.

Furthermore, noble son, there is the Dharma-gate of the Wheel of Dharma consisting of the names of the teachings on Right Mindfulness that rescues and protects all sentient beings of the three periods from fear, which gives birth to present right mindfulness. For the sake of liberating sentient beings wandering in the three realms, one enters the Dharma-gate of Discourse; by dwelling in this Dharma-gate, one manifests various skillful means with bodies equal to those of all sentient beings. According to what is appropriate for each, these skillful means eliminate their terrors, causing them all to resolve upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, attain non-retrogression, make offerings to the Buddhas, and uphold the True Dharma."

“Good son! I know only this Bodhisattva Dharma-door of the Radiance of the Great Compassionate, Pure Vairocana-mārga. As for all the great Bodhisattvas, they all possess the pure great vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva; they have perfected the ultimate practices of Samantabhadra; they do not sever the stream of any roots of goodness, nor do they extinguish the stream of any samādhis; they constantly cultivate the practices of *avaivartika* (non-retrogression) without ever ceasing; they well understand the signs of the formation and destruction of worlds; they destroy the sprouts of the unwholesome roots of all sentient beings and give rise to the streams of all roots of goodness; they extinguish the stream of the birth-and-death minds of all sentient beings and bring forth the stream of the roots of goodness in the minds of sentient beings. How could I possibly know or speak of their meritorious conduct?”
The Rāma-kaṇḍa Sūtra, Volume One;
The Rāma-kaṇḍa Sūtra, Volume Two,
translated by the Xiqin śramaṇa Śrīghana.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva from the eastern direction named Avikṣiptacaryā (No Different Practice).

Supported by precious flowers beneath his feet, he traveled through the void and arrived at Mount Vajramaṇḍala in the Sahā world. As his feet stepped upon the mountain, the Sahā world shook in six ways and was transformed into various jewels as an adornment.

From every pore of his body, he universally radiated light that completely eclipsed the sun, moon, and stars; the splendor of the fire-pearls and mani-jewels of Brahmā, Śakra, the Four Heavenly Kings, and all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—all became like a mass of ink.

Furthermore, this light universally illumines the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, animals, and King Yama, as well as all dark and hidden places; it extinguishes all suffering, eradicates the afflictions of illness and fear, and brings peace and security to all.

A universal rain of jewels fell, filling the Buddha-fields, as well as a rain of all manner of articles for offering; with these various offerings, they made worship to the Tathāgata. Manifesting his body according to what each sentient being was able to perceive, he appeared throughout the six realms of existence. Having traversed them all, he reached the Vajra-wheel Mountain and arrived at the abode of Avalokiteśvara.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara addressed Sudhana, saying:
"Good son! Do you see this seat?
Do you see the Bodhisattva Avivartyacaryā?"
He replied: "Great Sage!
Indeed, I have seen it."
Then Avalokiteśvara said to Sudhana:
"Go to him and ask: How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?"

Then the youth Sudhana prostrated himself at the feet of Avalokiteśvara, circumambulated him countless times, gazing upon him without weariness. Mindfully reflecting on the holy teachings and deeply entering the ocean of wisdom, he withdrew and took his leave. Arriving at the abode of Ananyagāmin, he prostrated himself at his feet, circumambulated him seven times to the right, and then stood with palms joined, saying:
"O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva practice and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
He replied,
"Good son! I have already accomplished the Dharma-door of the Universal Manifestation of Swift Movement."
The youth Sudhana said:
"O Great Sage!
From which Buddha did you receive this Dharma-door?"
“From which land do you come? How far is it from here? And how long has it been since you set out?
He replied, “O son of good family!...”

This place is difficult to know; it cannot be fathomed by any devas, humans, asuras, humans, or non-humans. Only those who practice with diligent vigor and do not regress, who draw near to spiritual friends, and who are protected and remembered by the Buddhas, are able to understand it.

If one does not possess the power of roots of goodness from past lives, a pure and straightforward mind, the faculties of a bodhisattva, and the opened eye of wisdom, then even with extensive learning and vast knowledge, one will still fail to hear [this teaching] and be unable to penetrate deeply into the wisdom of the noble ones; how much less could one believe and understand the sphere of practice of a bodhisattva?
Sudhana the youth said:
"O Great Sage!

I pray that you will tell me the name of the Tathāgata in that land; by relying upon the spiritual power of the Buddha, the power of the spiritual friend, the power of the five faculties of faith, and the power of accomplishing supernormal knowledges, I shall attain faith and understanding."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Avikalpachara replied to Sudhana:

"The land from which I have come is named Wondrous Chief Dharma-Treasury; the Buddha there is named Samantabhadra-Crested. It was in the presence of that Buddha that I attained this Dharma-door of the Universal Manifestation of Swift Movement."

It has been an unspeakable number of eons, as numerous as the atoms in a Buddha-field, since I set out from there. In a single thought-moment, I have taken steps as numerous as the atoms in an unspeakable number of Buddha-fields; with each step, I have passed through worlds as numerous as the atoms in an unspeakable number of Buddha-fields. In all the lands I have traversed, the Buddhas are currently present, and with every inexhaustible offering of all Bodhisattvas, I have made offerings to the *amṛta* bodies of those Buddhas.

Why is this so? Because I have attained this Dharma-gate of the Samādhi of the Seal of the True Mark of the Unattached, Pure Dharmatā-Born Body; by virtue of this merit, I am able to make offerings to the Tathāgata’s unattached Dharmakāya. With all those things rare for other Bodhisattvas to behold, I make offerings to the Buddhas. According to the roots of goodness cultivated by sentient beings in past lives, I manifest form-bodies for them and preach the Dharma. I emit great radiance that universally illumines the ten directions, adapting to the minds of the multitude and fulfilling their needs as they desire. I accomplish the treasury of the Dharma, produce subtle and wondrous sounds, and expound the True Dharma to benefit sentient beings. By means of this sublime Dharmakāya, I deliver sentient beings, and even throughout the ten directions, it is likewise so.

“Good son! I only know this Bodhisattva Dharma-door of Universal Manifestation and Swift Action. As for the great Bodhisattvas, they reach everywhere throughout the ten directions; their spheres of activity are immeasurable and indestructible. Their pure Dharma-body fills the entire Dharma-realm; they discern and understand the paths of all sentient beings; they fill all lands, accord with all dharmas, and contemplate the three periods of time with equanimity. They preach the Dharma of equality, conforming to the world yet remaining unattached to the Buddha-way. Universally reaching all places without attachment or obstruction, they skillfully explain that the true nature and original essence of all dharmas are empty and quiescent. How could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?”
"Noble son!

To the south of here, there is a city named Bharaputra. There dwells a deva named Mahādeva; go to him and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?'"

Then the youth Sudhana bowed his head at the feet of the Bodhisattva Viśeṣagamana in reverent salutation, circumambulated him countless times, gazed up at him with deep observation, and took his leave to travel south.

At that time, the youth Sudhana, with right mindfulness, contemplated the unobstructed conduct of the Bodhisattva Vairocana-mārga. Single-mindedly and exclusively seeking the light, wisdom, and supernatural powers arising from the sphere of the Bodhisattva’s non-dual conduct, as well as the sphere adorned by all merits, he gave rise to immeasurable and inconceivable dharma-gates of sustained practice through his courageous diligence, firm joy, and playful mastery of supernatural powers. Having attained definitive wisdom, his heart was deeply delighted and his entire body filled with joy. Endowed with all merits, the stages of samādhi, the stages of dhāraṇī, the stages of great vows, the stages of eloquence, and the stages of the powers, he gradually traveled until he reached the city gate and inquired where Mahādevī currently resided.
At that time, someone said: "Good man!
He is currently in the multi-storied hall within the city, having attained a subtle, wondrous, and pure physical body; surrounded by a great assembly, he manifests himself to preach the Dharma."
At that time, the youth Sudhana went to where Mahādeva was, prostrated himself with his head at [the deity’s] feet in respectful salutation, and said:
"O Great Sage!
I have already set my mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, yet I do not yet know how a bodhisattva should learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path."

At that time, Mahādeva extended his four arms, took up the waters of the four oceans, and placed them in his four palms without allowing a single drop to fall. He then washed his face and rinsed his mouth for the sake of the youth Sudhana, took a golden lotus, scattered it over Sudhana, and spoke these words:
"How rare, O son of good family!"
"How most marvelous and extraordinary it is that you have come from so far away to seek a spiritual friend (*kalyāṇamitra*).

Son of good family! The practices of the bodhisattvas are difficult to hear and difficult to see; they are profoundly deep, subtle, and inconceivable. They are characterized by courageous diligence and a sublime appearance; they are white lotuses (*puṇḍarīka*) among men. They serve as a refuge for sentient beings, providing protection and benefit to all. They gather in and do not abandon them, bringing peace and security to all, universally illuminating the oceans of lands throughout the ten directions, manifesting the true path, and remaining far removed from ignorance. Acting as great guides, they uphold the True Dharma, leading sentient beings to safety and freedom from affliction, reaching the other shore, and will certainly arrive at the city of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*). This is truly rare."

The three karmas of a bodhisattva are fully accomplished; that which is difficult to purify, they purify. Forever free from all evils, they always employ kind speech toward all classes of sentient beings, manifesting themselves before each according to what is appropriate, never missing the opportune moment.
"Good son!
I have only accomplished the bodhisattva dharma-gate of the Cloud-Net Radiance.
Sudhana the youth said:
“Great Sage!
What is the scope of this Dharma-door of the Cloud-Network Radiance?
At that time, Mahādeva piled up a heap of celestial gold before Sudhana, like the king of mountains.
Heaped up masses of white silver; heaped up masses of lapis lazuli; heaped up masses of crystal; heaped up masses of musāragalva; heaped up masses of agate;
heaped up masses of nocturnal luminosity; heaped up masses of rock crystal; heaped up masses of refined gold;
heaped up masses of *maṇi* jewels that guide and enlighten sentient beings; heaped up masses of *maṇi* jewels with deep-blue hair; heaped up masses of *cūḍāmaṇi* jewels.
There were clusters of *ni* gems, clusters of water-light *maṇi* gems, clusters of rose-apples, clusters of purple rose-apples,
clusters of sun-essence pearls, clusters of *mīlakha* jewels, clusters of multicolored jewels,
clusters of *vibhūra* jewels, clusters of red pearl nets, and clusters of sandalwood *maṇi* gems.
There were heaps of ornaments for all the limbs and members of the body, as numerous as Mount Sumeru; likewise, there were heaps of all kinds of flowers,

all kinds of incense, all kinds of ointments, all kinds of powdered incense, all kinds of flower garlands, all kinds of celestial garments, all kinds of precious parasols, all kinds of banners and streamers, all kinds of musical instruments, all kinds of couches and curtains, various articles of worship, the objects of the five desires, and such manifold jewels, accumulated like Mount Sumeru.
Furthermore, there appeared before him hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of *asaṃkhyeya* maidens, who said to Sudhana:
"O son of good family!

You should take all these various jewels to make offerings to the Tathāgata, bestow them upon all, and gather in sentient beings, causing all beings to cultivate the *dānapāramitā* and study the *dānapāramitā*. Because of this total relinquishment, use this mind of renunciation to instruct all; let them universally practice so that all sentient beings may be able to relinquish what is difficult to relinquish."
"Good son!
By means of these objects, I instruct you in giving; my instruction to all beings is likewise.

I cause all sentient beings to perfume and cultivate their bodies and minds with the wholesome root of non-attachment; I cause all beings everywhere to practice the conduct of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, to draw near to spiritual friends, to make offerings, to show reverence, to honor, and to praise them, thereby generating wholesome roots, nurturing wholesome roots, and bringing all wholesome roots to full completion, so that they may resolve to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
"Furthermore, good son!
If there are sentient beings who crave the five desires, for them he manifests impure realms;
for those who crave kingdoms, he preaches impermanence."

For those who are terrified by anger and hatred, arrogant and negligent, quarrelsome and harboring resentment like rākṣasa demons, who kill living beings without restraint, drinking blood and eating flesh—manifesting before all such various sentient beings, he teaches them to cultivate great compassion, causing them all to forever leave behind anger, negligence, and indolence.

If there are those who are lazy, he manifests for them the perils of water, fire, thieves, evil kings, and enemies, using the teaching of impermanence to transform them and cause them to give rise to roots of goodness.
"Good son!

By means of such various kinds of sentient beings of evil nature, through the wisdom of skillful means, one eliminates all evils and all obstacles that are enemies to wisdom, thereby accomplishing all the pāramitās."

“Good son! I know only this Dharma-door of the Radiance of the Cloud-Net of Bodhisattvas. The great bodhisattvas extinguish afflictions just as the King of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven extinguishes the calamities of the asuras; the bodhisattvas are like water, able to extinguish the blazing fires of the afflictions of sentient beings; the bodhisattvas are like fire, able to burn away the accumulated fuel of the afflictions of sentient beings;
the bodhisattvas are like wind, blowing away the various attachments of craving and greed in sentient beings, and destroying all hearts of defiled attachment and delusion.”
All bodhisattvas are like vajras, utterly destroying all attachment to self and possessions.
Since these great bodhisattvas have accomplished such great merits, how could I possibly know or describe their bodhisattva conduct?
"Good son!

To the south of this Jambudvīpa, there is a land named Magadha. Beneath the Bodhi tree at the site of the terrace of enlightenment, there is a spirit named Anvaya. Go to him and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?'"

Then the youth Sudhana, having bowed his head in reverent salutation at the feet of Mahādevī, took his leave and proceeded toward the country of Magadha to visit the goddess Ananyagāminī at the site of the terrace of enlightenment.
At that time, ten thousand earth deities each spoke these words:

“This youth who has come is able to rescue and protect all sentient beings; he is the Tathāgatagarbha himself. He can shatter the shell of ignorance of sentient beings and is always born into the family of the Supreme and Wondrous Dharma King. Stainless and unobstructed, his head is crowned with immeasurable celestial silks and jeweled diadems. Possessing a great treasury of wisdom, he subdues the various masters of debate among the heterodox and those of different schools, and as a Wheel-Turning Dharma King, he transforms and teaches sentient beings.”

At that time, ten thousand deities of the Earth-abiding Heaven caused the great earth to tremble, raining down fragrant water and sweeping with fragrant winds. These ten thousand deities of the Earth, with one voice and in unison, produced a subtle and wondrous sound that filled the trichiliocosm, emitting a great radiance that shone universally throughout the trichiliocosm.
Furthermore, there were palaces made of various jewels as adornments;
all the flowering trees were in full bloom and lush, with their branches bending downward;
and all the fruit trees were laden with produce, likewise hanging low.
All the fragrant waters—springs, sources, rivers, ponds, eddying pools, and swirling currents—flow into one another in mutual confluence, producing various sounds of entertainment.

The celestial palaces, adorned with myriad jewels, are filled with qilin, lions, fragrant elephants, white deer, phoenixes, peacocks, and diverse species of birds and beasts; each accompanied by its own retinue, they carry offerings and, all being filled with joy, emit harmonious and plaintive sounds.
Immeasurable treasuries of jewels spontaneously gush forth.

Winds arose from the four quarters like golden wheels, blowing various flowers that scattered over the site of the bodhimanda; devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others filled the grove.
At that time, the earth goddess Anuvartinī said to Sudhana:
"Welcome, son of good family!
Do you wish to see for yourself the fruits of the merit and roots of goodness you previously planted in this very place?"
At that time, the youth Sudhana bowed his head in respectful salutation at the feet of the goddess Pratiṣṭhā, circumambulated her countless times, and then stood to one side, saying:
"O Great Sage!
"Indeed, I wish to see it.

At that time, the Earth Goddess Anvaya pressed this great earth with her toe, whereupon immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya-nayuta* treasures of *maṇi* jewels were opened and revealed, and various auspicious vases spontaneously welled up.
“Good son! This treasure store has been brought about by the fruit of your past acts of giving; you may use it as you wish for the purpose of further giving. Good son!”
I have already accomplished the bodhisattva dharma-gate of the indestructible treasury of wisdom. Since the time of Dīpaṃkara Buddha,
I have acquired great roots of goodness and have constantly dwelt in this place, successively protecting all bodhisattvas,
causing them to enter deeply into the realm of wisdom, exhaust its very source and bottom, fulfill their great vows, and purify their bodhi.
The practice of the bodhisattva gives birth to all samādhis, cultivates all supernormal powers,
and fulfills all the power of the vast and great merit of bodhisattvas; it fulfills the great majestic power of all bodhisattvas,
accomplishes the unfathomable wisdom of a bodhisattva, possesses a mind so firm it cannot be destroyed, and radiates light.
Illuminating nets that travel through all Buddha-fields, hearing the wheels of Dharma of the predictions bestowed by all Tathāgatas,
and all the wheels of Dharma turned by all Tathāgatas; [I behold] the clouds of all *sūtras*, which universally transform sentient beings with the light of the Great Dharma,
uphold the sovereign spiritual powers of all Buddhas, and protect the power of the great Dharma-illumination of all Buddhas.
He instructed, exhorted, benefited, and gladdened me, saying, "I know only this bodhisattva dharma-gate of indestructible wisdom,
noble son! In the remote past,
beyond kalpas as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, there was a kalpa named Radiant Purity, a world named Moon Banner, where the Tathāgata was named Good Eye."
"Good son!
During the Radiant Purity Eon (*Prabhāsa-viśuddha-kalpa*), under the Buddha Fine Eye (*Sudarśana*), I contemplated and attained this Dharma-gate;
I cultivated, nurtured, purified, advanced, expanded, and universally expounded this Dharma-gate throughout that interval."
I have constantly been able to behold the Buddhas from the Radiant Eon (*Prabhāsa-kalpa*) through to the Auspicious Eon (*Bhadrakalpa*).

During this interval, passing through eons as numerous as the atoms within unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, I have personally approached all the Buddhas of those eons and made complete offerings to them.
Having thus served these Buddhas, I proceeded to the site of enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree.
I beheld all their various ornaments; at each and every Buddha’s place, I listened to and practiced the teachings, thereby attaining this Dharma-gate.

Having cultivated roots of goodness in the presence of all those Buddhas, through these roots of goodness and by virtue of hearing the Dharma, I have attained the Dharma-gate of indestructible treasury wisdom.
“Good son! I know only this Bodhisattva’s Dharma-door of the indestructible treasury of wisdom.

These great Bodhisattvas, having personally approached and made offerings to all Buddhas, hear and receive and uphold all the teachings spoken by those Buddhas. Following the voices of the Buddhas, they expound them for others, with mindfulness succeeding mindfulness, until they enter the heart of the Buddha, abide in the Buddha’s secrets, and attain the pure Dharma-body. They transcend the shell of ignorance and habitual tendencies of Bodhisattvas, give birth to the shadow-treasury of all Buddhas, skillfully explain the meanings of phrases, remember and maintain them without forgetting, universally manifest all physical forms, yet remain in the non-dual nature of the body.”
The practices of all bodhisattvas are immeasurable and boundless; how could I possibly know them or describe them? Good son!

In this Jambudvīpa, there is a land named Untroubled and a city named Supreme Patience. Within that city, there is a night goddess named Vaśavartī. You should go to her and ask: "How does a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva practices and cultivate the bodhisattva path?"

Then the youth Sudhana, having prostrated his head in respectful salutation to the goddess Ananyagāminī, circumambulated her countless times; looking up at her with devotion, he took his leave and, traveling by stages, went to the place where the Night Goddess resided.
At that time, the youth Sudhana, with right mindfulness, contemplated the teaching of the Earth Goddess regarding the bodhisattva dharma-gate of indestructible wisdom;
he cultivated the light of bodhisattva samādhi, entered into it according to his will,
observed the rules and methods of bodhisattva discipline, and his mind clearly understood the sovereign play of the supernatural powers of all bodhisattvas.
Contemplating the pure nature of all phenomena, they enter deeply into the ultimate realm of the bodhisattvas' profound wisdom;
they enter deeply into the dharma-gate of the ocean of bodhisattva knowledge; they accord with the bodhisattvas' dharma-gate of observing the indestructible ocean of wisdom;
and they contemplate the bodhisattvas' dharma-gate of the profoundly deep, boundless, pure, and indestructible. They observe...
Observing the Bodhisattva’s Dharma-door of the Cloud of Dharma and the Ocean of Dharma that provides shelter and protection, he gradually traveled until he reached that great city,
circumambulated it countless times, entered through the eastern gate, and stayed within the city center.
At that time, not long after the sun had set, Sudhana, yearning for the Great Teacher like one parched with thirst for a drink,
followed all the instructions of the Bodhisattvas; with single-minded palms joined, he desired to see the Great Teacher,
the Night Goddess Vasudhārā, and toward his spiritual friend, he conceived [the perception] of a Tathāgata, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Possessing the perception of universal knowledge and the sphere of the Universal Eye, they manifest all physical bodies and the power of wisdom throughout the ten directions,
reaching everywhere. Delighting in seeing spiritual friends who dwell in pure realms,
they universally behold the wondrous treasury of the Dharma-gate of the compassionate mind of all spiritual friends, thereby attaining the correct wisdom of all dharmas.
With the eye of wisdom, one observes the ocean of samādhi-intelligence of the ten directions and the universal eye’s sphere; neither emerging nor entering,
it is of the same nature as suchness— the ocean of wisdom of the all-illuminating dharma-realm— wherein the great eye of wisdom is profound, vast, and boundless.

He saw that night goddess dwelling in the void above the city, situated within a precious pavilion in the world adorned with fragrant lotus treasuries. She sat upon a precious lotus flower; her body was the color of pure gold, her topknot was spiral-textured with the luster of refined gold, and her eyelashes were deep blue. Her features were distinct and clearly defined, her physical marks were upright and majestic, and she was the most exquisite and peerless of all. Her body was adorned with various jewels, rare and beyond compare, bringing joy to all who beheld her; one could never tire of gazing upon her form. She wore crimson robes exquisitely decorated with wonderful gems, and the hair of her topknot was like that of Brahmā.
At that time, the Night Goddess spoke for the youth Sudhana the *dhāraṇī* of the Dharma-body Seal of the Brahma King Śaṅkhaśikha, and she uttered this mantra:
“Ladan | Brahmaprasana | Dhāraṇi | Niścavarmajaṭhena | Śarira | Makūṭa | Dhāraṇi | Niścakara-dhāraṇi-ta svāhā svāhā. “Good son! ...”

If there are those who obtain this dhāraṇī, within all the pores of their bodies, they will universally manifest all the suns, moons, five planets, and twenty-eight lunar mansions, as well as the radiance of all the stellar deities (*tithi*). With this radiance, they will universally illuminate all sentient beings in immeasurable worlds; in a single kṣaṇa, they will be able to see sentient beings undergoing the sufferings of the eight difficulties within the three evil realms, beholding them all from within a single pore.

Regarding the sentient beings to be converted: whether there are those who delight in being born in the heavens, or those who delight in attaining the Śrāvaka vehicle, or those who delight in attaining the Pratyekabuddha vehicle, or those who delight in attaining all-knowledge (sarvākārajñatā), [the Buddha] manifests them all within a single pore.

Or if there are those who wish to see various skillful means, physical forms, dignified demeanors, voices, the preaching of the Dharma, and all manner of speech, they shall behold them all in a single thought-moment.

Such is the subtle and wondrous sound of the Dharma, pure and penetrating; according to what beings wish to hear, even throughout incalculable eons, they likewise see and hear it all within a single pore, as well as all the practices of the bodhisattvas. They may see bodhisattvas practicing with courageous diligence the various gates of samādhi and supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), the spheres of the bodhisattvas' sovereign spiritual power, the dwellings of the bodhisattvas, the radiance of the bodhisattvas, and the gates of the bodhisattvas' vigorous display of supernormal powers. Such various things, according to the beings to be transformed, are all seen and heard within a single pore; these are all obtained through the original practices of the bodhisattvas.

At that time, having seen and heard this, the youth Sudhana was filled with great joy. He prostrated himself at the feet of that night goddess, circumambulated her countless times, and standing to one side with palms joined in reverence, he said:
"O Celestial Being!

I have already first resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and with a mind of faith and understanding, through the influence of spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), I have been able to see the various Buddhas and hear the merit of the Dharma. I only pray that the celestial deity will now reveal and manifest for me the path to omniscience (*sarvajñatā*) practiced by all Bodhisattvas; if any Bodhisattva proceeds toward this path, they shall attain the ten stages (*bhūmi*) and the ten powers (*bala*) of a Bodhisattva.
At that time, the Night Goddess said to Sudhana:
"Excellent, excellent, noble son!"
"You are able to revere spiritual friends and comply with their instructions.
If there are bodhisattvas who revere spiritual friends and comply with their instructions, they shall swiftly attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
"Good son!
It is I alone who has accomplished the Bodhisattva Dharma-gate of the Universal Radiance of Light that Illumines All Dharmas, Dispels the Ignorance of Sentient Beings, and Shatters the Demons.
Good son!"

I give rise to a mind of great loving-kindness toward sentient beings who hold wrong views; I give rise to a mind of great compassion toward sentient beings who commit unwholesome deeds and act in opposition; I give rise to a mind of sympathetic joy toward sentient beings who cultivate goodness; I give rise to a mind of non-duality toward sentient beings who are both good and evil; I give rise to a mind of purity toward sentient beings who are defiled; I give rise to a mind of equanimity toward sentient beings who are attached to a self through wrong views; I give rise to a mind of sympathetic joy toward sentient beings who are lowly and impure; I give rise to a mind of purity toward sentient beings who are attached to pleasure; I give rise to a mind that skillfully accords with and understands the wheel of birth and death for sentient beings who delight in the cycle of saṃsāra; and I give rise to the mind of bodhi—the path to omniscience—for the sake of establishing sentient beings who delight in the vehicles of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
"Good son!

I constantly contemplate and teach all sentient beings in this way, so that they may accomplish the Bodhisattva Dharma-gate of Universally Shining Radiance that Dispels the Ignorance and Shatters the Demons of Sentient Beings."

During the latter part of the night when all is still and silent, when all ghosts and spirits run about crosswise, when thieves roam about, when a bhikṣu has abandoned his proper deportment, and when smoke, clouds, dust, and mist obscure the sun and moon so that their forms cannot be seen—at those times and in those places, I shall act as a clear eye for them, guiding them across.

If there are sentient beings who, whether in cities, towns, villages, hamlets, mountain crags, wildernesses, or within the great oceans of the eight directions—even throughout all waterways, lands, forests, perilous paths, or lost ways—encounter fears, the hardships of clouds, thunder, and lightning, the terrors of fools and wild beasts, the dangers of bandits in the wilderness, the calamities of famine, pestilence, and epidemics in their lands, or the perils of war and destruction; by the power of this dhāraṇī, their terrors shall be extinguished.

If there are sentient beings who encounter maritime disasters—where black winds raise the waves and great billows overturn the ship, leaving merchants bewildered and unable to see the shore—and if they face such various perils on water or land, I shall act as their refuge in those places; I may become an island, or take the form of a ship to rescue those drowning, or manifest as a caravan leader (*sārthavāha*), or as a *jāṅghika* (sea-dweller), or take the forms of an elephant king, a horse king, a young elephant, a tortoise, a crocodile, or a turtle, or the form of an *asura* king, a sea deity, or a *nāga* king, or even the forms of a dog king, a mosquito, or a gadfly. Manifesting in such diverse forms, I shall serve as their destination and provide the skillful means to deliver them from all suffering and hardship. May all sentient beings be freed from the suffering of the five aggregates and attain the path of liberation.
When all people, during the darkness of night, encounter shards, rubble, thorns, mounds, and hills;
or face venomous snakes, lions, tigers, wolves, vipers, and all manner of poisonous harms;

or suffer from the afflictions of cold, heat, and wind—at that time, I shall manifest in the form of the sun and moon, the form of a brilliant star, the form of a shooting star, or the form of a comet.
As for their forms, some manifest as the sound of thunder and lightning; some manifest as the form of precious radiance;
some manifest as the forms of various calamitous stars and strange portents such as Mars and Venus; some manifest as the palaces of the devas; some manifest as the forms of celestial kings;
some manifest as the forms of the eight classes of beings, including devas, nāgas, and spirits; or some manifest as a wheel-turning [monarch].
In the form of a wheel-turning monarch, the forms of various minor kings, or the forms of diverse beings;
or appearing in the form of a bodhisattva, or appearing in the form of a Tathāgata—through the power of dhāraṇī and various skillful means, may they protect and shelter all sentient beings.
May all sentient beings always attain peace and security; may they be protected by great compassion and abide where the Buddhas abide.

Some take the form of mountain crags and stone caves; some take the form of streams, ravines, springs, ponds, groves, trees, medicinal herbs, flowers, and fruit-bearing trees; some take the form of a hundred kinds of sweet delicacies and fragrant, delicious foods; some take the form of ice and snow; some take the form of shadows, echoes, and cool shade; some take the form of level ground, roads, and lanes; some take the form of various birds such as the *kalaviṅka* and the king of peacocks; some take the form of a king of medicinal trees emitting light; some take the form of mountain deities and earth deities; and some take the form of torches and lightning flashes.
If there are sentient beings in places of peril—whether on treacherous mountains, in plains, or marshes—I shall provide protection for them through the power of dhāraṇīs.

By means of such various skillful expedients, I shall cause all sentient beings to escape sorrow and suffering and leave the ocean of birth and death; I shall inspire them with this thought, enabling all sentient beings to transcend the mountain of self-conceit.

Furthermore, may all sentient beings transcend the stream of birth and death; with the blazing flames of the torch of wisdom, may they shatter the darkness of ignorance, burn down the village of the five aggregates, and cross over the marsh of birth and death.

“Good son! For sentient beings who are mired in the perils of birth and death and shrouded in ignorance, I shall, by the power of dhāraṇī, sever the net of birth and death and the terrifying bonds of malicious abuse, incantations, slander, harsh speech, and treacherous calumny.”

At that time, I shall produce the subtle and wondrous voice of a kalaviṅka bird and recite dhāraṇīs to bring them joy and liberation from sorrow and suffering. Whether they be infants, children, adults, or the elderly; whether they be deaf, blind, mute, or speech-impaired; whether they be crippled, maimed, or paralyzed; or afflicted by scabies, leprosy, abscesses, or even the four hundred and four types of diseases—I shall, through the power of the dhāraṇī, act as a great king of physicians. Appearing before these sick people, I will explain various methods for treating illnesses so that each may be healed and cured.
"Good son! I further formed this thought as I beheld sentient beings: those who delight in and cling to the thorny forest of the five desires;

those who delight in and cling to the perverse teachings of false views; and those who delight in and cling to kingdoms, giving rise to arrogance. Thus, by various forms of attachment and suffering, their bodies are oppressed, yet they neither perceive nor know it. Following these sentient beings wherever they may be, and according to what they contemplate and what they think, I manifest my body through the power of *dhāraṇī* to show them the correct path and enable them to attain peace and happiness. Through the power of my grace, they leave behind all sufferings and hardships and reach a place of security."

For the sake of those beings, I further made this vow: to cause all sentient beings to distance themselves from the three miserable realms, to forever attain liberation from all sufferings, to single-mindedly seek wisdom and advance upon the path to Bodhi, to be free from all anxieties and afflictions, to always abide in peace and security, and to be released from the bonds of the five aggregates.

If there are small kingdoms in remote border regions, where kings, princes, sons of good family, or daughters of good family suffer from disputes and litigation concerning their kingdoms; from anxieties regarding their livelihoods, fields, and houses; or from worries about reputation, honor, rank, and sovereignty—regarding such various perils, calamities, fears, and difficulties, I shall, by means of the power of this dhāraṇī, cause them to reach reconciliation and attain peace and security in all respects.

Furthermore, he makes this vow: may all sentient beings eliminate all attachments to the five aggregates, the twelve bases, the eighteen elements, and so forth; may they cross over the river of birth and death and dwell securely on the other shore.

Furthermore, I vow that all sentient beings shall abide in the realm of the Buddha’s omniscience (*sarvākārajñatā*), forever free from attachment to views, and give rise to the peaceful and blissful practices of all Buddhas.

If there are sentient beings who are attached to the affairs of villages, bound by ignorance, and entangled in the sixty-two views and various attachments to views, thereby undergoing manifold sufferings—truly pitiable—I shall, through the skillful means of *dhāraṇī*, preach the Dharma for them, causing them to attain weary detachment and gathering them in through the Dharma.
Again, he forms this thought: "May all sentient beings abide securely in the ground of the unsurpassed path of the True Dharma.

Again, he forms this thought: "May all sentient beings completely distance themselves from the empty village of the six sense bases, transcend the ultimate realm of birth and death, and dwell peacefully in the city of *sarvajñā* (omniscience), the place of the bliss of cessation."
"Furthermore, good son!
It is like a person who has lost their way, taking east for west and west for east, south for north and north for south; it is the same with the four intermediate directions and the zenith and nadir.
All people in the world who are deluded regarding the Dharma and do not know the right path are just like this."

"Good son! There are three kinds of people in the world: first, the insane; second, the deluded; and third, those afflicted by wind-disorders (*vāta*). These three types of people recklessly give rise to poisonous harm; grasping a sharp sword in their hands, they wish to strike the east but instead strike the west, wish to strike the west but instead strike the east, wish to strike the south but instead strike the north, and wish to strike the north but instead strike the south; it is the same for the four intermediate directions and the zenith and nadir."

Those who slander the Dharma are likewise: because their minds are inverted, they perceive false characteristics within the True Dharma; they conceive the notion of True Dharma regarding false dharmas; they conceive the notion of impermanence regarding eternal dharmas; they conceive the notion of permanence regarding impermanent dharmas; they conceive the notion of suffering regarding pleasant dharmas; they conceive the notion of pleasure regarding painful dharmas; they conceive the notion of purity regarding impurity; they perversely conceive the notion of self regarding dharmas that are non-self; they conceive the notion of rugged terrain upon level ground; they conceive the notion of level ground upon rugged terrain; they conceive the notion of famine in an age of abundance and prosperity; they conceive the notion of abundance and prosperity in an age of famine; they conceive the notion of desolation in an age of flourishing populations; and they conceive the notion of flourishing populations in an age of desolation.

For these sentient beings who are thus deluded and have lost the Way, for those who are confused and those whose natures are lost, I employ various skillful means and the power of dhāraṇīs to radiate great light. To those in dark places who wish to emerge from the path, I open their gates; for the ignorant, I radiate great light to open the eye of wisdom; and for sentient beings who have lost the Way, I reveal the correct path and lead them forth.

If there are sentient beings who wish to cross the current, he acts as a bridge, a boat, a ferry, a crossing, or an island for them, enabling them to reach the other shore. To those who do not know the directions, he shows them a land of bliss; he transforms mounds, ruins, pits, and hollows into level ground, where soft grass grows. Or again, he manifests cities, villages, and various exquisite forms, bestowing them upon sentient beings to enable them to obtain happiness.

Furthermore, he manifests rivers, flowing springs, groves, and bathing pools; he causes the population to flourish and dwell in peace, security, and abundance, so that all sentient beings turn toward one another with hearts of loving-kindness, like fathers and sons, brothers and sisters.

He further made this vow: "I have now bestowed upon all sentient beings all forms of peace, happiness, wisdom, and light, so that those beings may forever leave behind the darkness of ignorance. May they no longer be deluded by the long night of craving, nor obscured by the gloom of nescience; may those who lack eyes obtain the eye of wisdom, and may all be universally made bright and pure."
If there are sentient beings who are attached to the notions of self, person, or sentient being, may they be led to abandon such conceptions of self, person, and sentient being.

If there are sentient beings who perceive the impermanent as permanent, the non-self as self, suffering as pleasure, the impure as pure, the non-aggregates as aggregates, or the non-life-principle as life-principle; who conceive of what is not the intermediate state (*antarābhava*) as the intermediate state; who conceive of what are not the aggregates, elements, or sense-bases (*skandha-dhātu-āyatana*) as the aggregates, elements, or sense-bases; who conceive of grasses and trees—which lack a life-span—as having a life-span, or of sentient beings—which are not grasses and trees—as being grasses and trees; who conceive of what is not cause and effect as cause and effect; who conceive of what is not the path of wholesome conduct as the path of wholesome conduct; or who conceive that by killing living beings and sacrificing to the heavens one may seek eternal bliss—even regarding the karma of the ten unwholesome paths and false views—may all sentient beings universally be freed from these various conceptions.
They are unfilial toward their parents; they do not respect śramaṇas or brahmins; they lack gratitude and fail to recognize kindness;
they distance themselves from the right path and perform unwholesome deeds; they fully possess the sixteen types of evil observances;
they slander the right path and destroy the true teachings; they are deeply attached to false views and revile the Buddha.
Regarding the Dharma and the Saṅgha, they sever the true Wheel of Dharma, destroy the assembly of Bodhisattvas, increase malice toward the Mahāyāna, and slay Bodhisattvas;
they do not praise the Bodhisattva-Saṅgha. Through such various unwholesome karmas, sentient beings of diverse classes are oppressed by manifold sufferings;
their minds harbor grief and affliction, they lose their original wisdom-mind, and they no longer know the Dharma.
For those who are greedy, deranged, deluded, and ignorant, who do not recognize the correct path and have been constantly subjected to slander throughout immeasurable kalpas;
for those who are confused by false views and fail to discern the directions— toward such as these, who act contrary to the Dharma and the Vinaya,
I give rise to profound compassion so that they may receive protection and refuge.

At that time, the Night Goddess Vasudhārā, for the sake of those sentient beings who were deranged and slandered the Dharma, spoke the *dhāraṇī* for purifying, subduing, and eliminating the karmic obstacles of immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, and she spoke the mantra as follows:

“*Dṛṣaṃ-bhara-puṭanaya-samamañji-tāpaya-vi-male-śuddhanaye vi-mala-śuddhanide śuddhaniye svāhā | mahā-śuddhanama-dṛṣe svāhā.* “If there are sentient beings who slander the True Dharma, disparage the Bodhisattva Saṅgha, break the harmony of the Saṅgha, sever the teachings of the noble wisdom of the Mahāyāna, and increase their haste in practicing the path of the Bodhisattvas without any sense of reciprocity or gratitude—such persons as these are not called true men, nor do they possess the body of a man.”
They were unfilial toward their parents and committed patricide or matricide; they engaged in disputes, litigation, and fraud against spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*);
they killed eight persons and *arhats*; they were unkind and unrighteous;
they stole property belonging to the Buddha, stupas, the Dharma, the *caitya* Sangha, and the resident Sangha; and they violated the four grave prohibitions.
Those who, through the thirteen saṃghāvaśeṣa offenses, the ten unwholesome paths of action, or the five crimes of immediate retribution,
swiftly and directly head toward the evil realms, and who are submerged in the ocean of suffering, shrouded by the darkness of ignorance— I, by means of the power of my great wisdom-light,
shall eliminate their darkness of ignorance, their grave sins of immediate retribution, and their obscurations of delusion, so that they may quickly [attain liberation].
Having resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, they adorn themselves with the Mahāyāna and fulfill the conduct of Samantabhadra;
for them, he explains the realm of the Tathāgata, the Dharma King— the ten powers of a Tathāgata,
the four fearlessnesses, the eighteen unique qualities, supernatural powers, and other such matters— thereby bringing all great wisdom to fulfillment.
O Wisdom Ground, I now manifest the power of the Tathāgata’s ten powers, four fearlessnesses, and other dhāraṇīs,
abiding in the true path of all Buddhas. By the power of these dhāraṇīs, I am able to cause all Buddhas of the ten directions to be of one and the same Dharma-body.
"Furthermore, good son!

I now act for the sake of sentient beings who have long been afflicted by the suffering of illness—those emaciated by many diseases, those ravaged by epidemics, the aged and infirm, the stingy, greedy, and impoverished; those in peril, distress, and exhaustion; those whose nations have perished and families destroyed; those wandering and displaced from their lands; the destitute, orphaned, and exiled; those who are solitary and fallen from power, having no one to protect them—all of whom, due to a lack of compassion in previous lives, suffer the retribution of evil karma, are bound to others, and wear the eight sufferings and decaying afflictions as their raiment. For such as these who have no refuge, I provide protection through the skillful means of great compassion;
and for all those in poverty and suffering, I cause their treasuries to overflow spontaneously through the power of dhāraṇī."

If there are those who are stingy and greedy, not relinquishing their attachments even unto death and becoming "wealth-guarding ghosts," for the sake of such beings and their various forms of craving and attachment, he employs all manner of skillful means to guide and transform them, so that all those sentient beings may attain liberation.

He further made this vow: "I shall act as a great protector for all those sentient beings, bestowing upon them the medicine of the Dharma. Those who take this medicine will be able to eliminate the diseases of all afflictions; they will be freed from the fear of the eight sufferings of birth, old age, and death; they will forever depart from all sufferings associated with the twelvefold cycle of ignorance, old age, and death; they will distance themselves from evil associates and draw near to virtuous friends; through the universally victorious Dharma, they shall embrace all beings and cause them to abide securely in the three pure karmas; and by reverently believing in the Tathāgata’s true and wondrous Dharma-body, they shall forever depart from birth, old age, sickness, and death, ultimately dwelling eternally in the realm of purity."
"Furthermore, good son!
I see those sentient beings with wrong views and their retinues who practice evil precepts;
I see sentient beings who have abandoned the right path and entered upon deviant tracks, clinging to inverted views and being deluded by falsehoods."
Their actions of body, speech, and mind are unwholesome; they are variously negligent and rely upon false teachings.
They conceive the notion of true awakening regarding that which is not true awakening, and the notion of non-true awakening regarding the truly awakened one.
They associate with evil friends and practice painful dharmas, such as throwing themselves into abysses, leaping into fire, falling from high cliffs, or constantly standing on one foot.

Scorching their bodies with five fires, smearing themselves with ashes and dirt, lying upon beds of thorns, starving themselves to death, or submerging themselves in deep pools during the height of winter to lie beneath the ice;

they observe the precepts of chickens, dogs, oxen, deer, and other such beings—through various such heterodox views and ascetic practices, they seek liberation. With various skillful means, I [address them].
He eliminates their wrong views, causing them to dwell securely in right view, and brings the highest bliss to all humans and devas.
He further makes this vow:

"May all sentient beings transcend the world and not cling to wrong views; may they abide securely in the unsurpassed, true, and correct path, attain non-retrogression, and achieve all-knowledge (*sarvajñā*). May they ultimately fulfill the practices of the great vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, turn toward all-knowledge, never depart from any of the bodhisattva stages, and, without harboring the nature of suffering of any sentient being, attain liberation."

At that time, the night goddess Vasudhārā, wishing to reiterate the bodhisattva dharma-gate of the "Universal Radiance of Light Illuminating All Dharmas and Dispelling the Ignorance of Sentient Beings," received the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, surveyed the ten directions, and then addressed the youth Sudhana in verse:
"The wondrous dharmas I have accomplished, The stages and gateways for knowing the proper time,
Illuminate and eliminate the darkness of ignorance, Universally observing all phenomena."
My Dharma-gate is tranquil, attained through long cultivation of a compassionate mind;
throughout immeasurable and countless eons, great compassion has covered all living beings,
achieving an ocean of great compassion that gives birth to the Buddhas of the three periods of time.
Having extinguished all suffering, Sudhana swiftly reaches the ultimate goal.
The Son of the Buddha’s heart is filled with joy; forever free from worldly evils, he transcends the suffering of the three realms and partakes in the bliss of the worthy and holy ones.
Far removed from conditioned evils, The wisdom and liberation of the śrāvakas,
And the fulfillment of the Buddhas' wisdom— These the sons of the Buddha should bring to ultimate completion.
With my all-pervading pure eye, I universally observe the lands of the ten directions.
In those worlds, the Buddhas sit at the site of enlightenment,
their bodies adorned with the marks and signs; surrounded by immeasurable multitudes,
they radiate oceans of great light, universally transforming all living beings.
Beholding all classes of sentient beings, dying here and being born there,
circling through the six realms of existence and undergoing every kind of bitter suffering;
with my ocean of pure ears, I universally hear the sounds from the ten directions.
The entire ocean of all languages, I am able to receive and uphold it all.
With my purified faculty of the nose, I am unimpeded within the ocean of Dharma;
I can enter all gateways of the Dharma, and you, Sudhana, should bring this to ultimate completion.
I have attained the mark of a Great Man, With a pure and broad tongue;
I expound the Dharma according to what is appropriate, And the sons of the Buddha should reach its ultimate realization.
The pure and wondrous Dharma-body Is equal to the suchness of the three periods of time.
According to those who are to be transformed, there is nothing that does not appear.
My mind is free from attachment, as clear and pure as space;
it universally encompasses the realm of the Buddhas, yet remains without dualistic characteristics.
I fully know the immeasurable lands and the ocean of the various minds of sentient beings;
I discern their faculties and intentions, remaining far removed from all false and illusory phenomena.
By the power of my spiritual penetrations, I travel everywhere throughout immeasurable lands.
Universally covering all multitudes, Taming all sentient beings.
Wisdom pure as space, An incomparable and inexhaustible treasury,
Making offerings to all Buddhas, Bringing benefit to all sentient beings.
With vast and pure wisdom, They thoroughly understand the ocean of all phenomena;
Having eliminated all delusions and doubts, The sons of the Buddha should reach ultimate realization.
I have entered the ocean of the Buddha-dharma And attained mastery over the dharmas of the three periods of time.
Having clearly realized all-knowledge, there is none able to measure it;
within every single atom, one sees oceans of Buddha-fields,
or beholds the Buddhas of the three periods of time— this is the power of true wisdom.
"I see the Buddha Vairocana attaining perfect enlightenment at the site of awakening;
in as many lands as there are motes of dust throughout the ten directions, he everywhere turns the wheel of the True Dharma.
At that time, the youth Sudhana said to the celestial deity:
“How long has it been since you first resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?
How long has it been since you obtained this Dharma-gate, such that you are now able to benefit sentient beings in this way?”
He replied: "O Son of the Buddha!

In the distant past, beyond as many eons as there are atoms in Mount Sumeru, and further beyond that number by immeasurable and boundless amounts, there was a world named Collection of Seven-Jewel Merits; the eon was named Radiant Tranquility; the land was named Jewel-Moon Radiance; and the city was named Lotus Light Place. Within this eon, five hundred billion Buddhas appeared in the world in Jambudvīpa."

At that time, in that city, there was a Wheel-Turning Sage King named Sudharmapāla, who ruled the world with the righteous Dharma of a sage king. The seven treasures appeared spontaneously, and he reigned over the four quarters of the world. His lifespan lasted for one kalpa; his power and majesty were sovereign, and without the use of weapons, peace prevailed naturally.

The king’s most esteemed first consort was named Candrasūryamati. While the king and his consort were amusing themselves with music, it became deep midnight and they fell into a profound sleep. She then dreamed that within this city there was a night-goddess named Samyaksambuddhaśāntiprabhā, who came before her, stood with palms joined, and spoke these words: "Ho!..."
"Good woman, do you know this?

To the east of the great city Padmaprabha, there is a forest named Śāntaprabhā-sūkṣmaguṇa. Within this forest is a bodhi tree named Sarvabuddhavaiśvarya-prabhā. There resides a Buddha, a World-Honored One named Sarvadharmanirghoṣarāja, who sat beneath this tree and attained equal and perfect enlightenment, fully endowed with the ten titles. He emits a great radiance called Maṇirāja-sarvatravyāpin."
"Seven days have already passed since that Buddha, King of Thunderous Sound, appeared in the world and first attained perfect enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree!

At that time, the night goddess extolled and praised the Tathāgata’s immeasurable merits and sovereign spiritual powers, causing the lady to resolve upon the unsurpassed path and to praise all the vows and practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
At that time, the King’s consort, while still within her dream, paid homage to that Buddha, resolved her mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and made offerings to the Buddha.
Then the World-Honored One emitted a golden light that touched the consort’s heart, illuminating the entire palace city so that it was all of one golden color.
At that time, the lady awoke from her sleep.

Then the Buddha, together with his retinue of śrāvakas, bodhisattvas, and the entire great assembly, appeared before the lady. At that moment, the lady prostrated herself in respectful salutation to the Buddha and the great assembly; she made offerings, paid homage, revered, and praised them, and immediately made this vow:
"By the merit of this, may I be the most honored and most supreme among devas and humans in a future world."
"Good son! You should know now: was the king’s consort Candramatī at that time anyone else?
It was I myself."

In the presence of that Buddha, I first resolved my mind upon the Way, adorned myself with merit, and planted great roots of goodness. For kalpas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru, I have not fallen into the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, animals, or the domain of King Yama, nor have I been born into lowly families. My faculties are complete, all sufferings are extinguished, and I constantly obtain the most supreme karmic rewards among humans and devas. I am always able to remain close to and attend upon virtuous friends, am always born into the families of Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and am never born during the kalpas of the five turbidities.
"Good son! I have obtained excellent benefit;

in the presence of that Buddha, I deeply planted roots of goodness and nurtured those roots of goodness. For eighty billion eons, as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru, I constantly experienced happiness, yet I had not yet fulfilled the roots of goodness of a bodhisattva, nor had I attained samādhi or supernormal powers, even after passing eighty billion eons, as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru."

After this kalpa has passed, and after another ten thousand kalpas have elapsed, there will be a kalpa named Pure and Free from Sorrow, and a world named Pure Majestic Virtue Supreme. In that world, five hundred billion Buddhas will appear in the world, attaining equal and perfect enlightenment and being fully endowed with the ten titles; the lands of those Buddhas will be either pure or defiled.
I then made offerings to those Buddhas in succession.

In the world-system of one of those Buddhas, there was a four-continent realm named Vimaladhvaja; its capital city was named Vyūha. At that time, I was the daughter of the elder Prabhāsaśrī, named Jñānaprabhā, and I was exceptionally beautiful and sublime.
In that world, I encountered the first Buddha, named Sumeru-Śāntaketu.

At that time, there was a deva named Vimalabuddhicandra who, by the power of his original vow, was born in that city. There was also a night goddess named Viśuddhacakṣus, who entered the royal palace while I was asleep; she came to where I was, manifested a wondrous body, praised the Tathāgata, and exhorted me to resolve my mind for enlightenment, sending me to the Buddha’s presence, saying these words:
"The Buddha Sumeru-Śāntaketu has newly attained perfect enlightenment and emitted a great radiance seven days ago!"
At that time, the Night Goddess guided me; I immediately awoke in alarm and saw a great radiance filling the palace chambers.
My parents were filled with wonder and joy, and they said to me:
"What light is this? It is a brilliant golden hue, illuminating our room."
At that time, I immediately said to my parents:

"In a dream, I saw a night goddess praising the supreme and wondrous merits of the Tathāgata. There is a Buddha, a World-Honored One, named Sumeru-Śāntadhvaja, who has appeared in the world for seven days now."
"I only pray that my parents, together with all our kinsmen, will go to where the Buddha is to make offerings and pay him respect, and to listen to the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma.
His parents were filled with joy and immediately gave their consent.

At that time, the Night Goddess led the way before us; I, together with my parents and kinsmen, went to where the Buddha was, prostrated ourselves at his feet, and withdrew to sit on one side. Beholding the subtle and wondrous radiance of the Buddha’s physical body, I immediately attained the Bodhisattva Samādhi of the Pure Wisdom-Light of the Three Times.

Having attained this samādhi, one recalls all the Buddhas seen throughout kalpas as numerous as the atoms of Mount Sumeru, as well as the sūtras and dharmas they taught; by receiving, upholding, and never forgetting them, one immediately attains the Dharma-gate of Universal Radiance that Illumines All Dharmas, Dispels the Delusions of Sentient Beings, and Destroys Māra.

Having attained this Dharma-gate, he further recalled the events of worlds throughout ten world-systems of atoms of kalpas in the past; he also beheld all those sentient beings, their karmic retributions, their beauty and ugliness, the sharpness or dullness of their faculties, their differing natures and inclinations, and their languages and voices. He saw how they had long cultivated wholesome deeds and drawn near to spiritual friends, and how he manifested physical bodies according to what was appropriate for them to bring them benefit. Seeing such matters, it was as if they were occurring right now in the present.
By the power of this samādhi, in every thought-moment, I increase the dharma-gates;
with mind following upon mind in continuous succession, I am able, with a single body, to fill worlds as numerous as the atoms of the ten directions,
even to fill oceans of worlds as numerous as their atoms, and further surpassing all those atoms of worlds.
In unspeakably unspeakable numbers of worlds, they see all the Buddhas within those worlds,
hear the Buddhas preaching the Dharma, and are able to remember, uphold, analyze,
