and fully comprehend the oceans of the original pure vows of those Buddhas; furthermore, they know the pure vows made by the Buddhas as they adorn their Buddha-lands.
I now likewise desire to purify all oceans of worlds and sentient beings, causing them to attain pure lands even as they appear before me now;
according to the bodies that those sentient beings ought to see, I immediately manifest them for them, taming their minds and transforming them through deliverance.
From the distant past until this very day, throughout the *kṣetras*...
That continuity nurtures and advances the cultivation of this dharma-gate;
such a dharma-gate is ultimately vast and expansive, equal to the dharma-realm. "Good son!
I know only this bodhisattva dharma-gate of the universal illumination of all phenomena by light, which shatters the afflictions of sentient beings and destroys the Māras.
As for the ultimate, immeasurable, and boundless ocean of practices and vows of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
which deeply penetrates the ocean of all dharma-realms and establishes the wisdom-banner samādhi of all bodhisattvas— I do not know them.
Sporting with spiritual powers, they fulfill their great vows and protectively uphold the ocean of great merit of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas.
In every thought-moment, they adorn and transform all sentient beings, bringing to completion the ocean of the nature of wisdom.
They eliminate ignorance, delusion, and inversion, universally bestowing pure insight, like the autumn...
The Moon Bodhisattva dwells in the world, illuminating the three realms universally;
unattached to any signs, he eliminates feverish afflictions and manifests the three periods of time through sovereign spiritual powers.
He carries sentient beings across, reveals the true path, and produces all sounds that are perfect, pure, and complete throughout the three periods of time, filling the ten directions as one.
Throughout the entire Dharma-realm, from the first generation of the bodhicitta until the tenth stage, during that interval,
they are all fully endowed with immeasurable merit, inconceivable supernormal powers, and the radiance of wisdom.
"How could I possibly know or explain the conduct of those bodhisattvas?

Good son, in this Jambudvīpa, in the kingdom of Magadha, there is a night goddess named Vimalaguṇatejāprabhā. That night goddess is my great teacher; she previously exhorted me to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, instructing, benefiting, and gladdening me. Go to her and ask: how does a bodhisattva train in the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?"
At that time, the youth Sudhana praised Vāsavadattā with a verse, speaking in颂 (śloka) as follows:
"I behold the Honored One’s pure body, Adorned by its own marks and signs;
Transcending the world, It is like Mount Sumeru."
The Dharma-body is profoundly serene and pure; throughout the three periods of time, all are entirely equal.
Universally gathering in all sentient beings, that person is free from attachment.
They manifest and expound the pure radiance, which shines universally upon all realms of existence.
Within a single pore, one sees all the stars and constellations;
with a pure mind that has no dependence, like the sun in the sky,
one grasps the Dharma of the Dharma-King— luminous, pure, and profound wisdom.
From each and every pore, light radiates, Illuminating the lands of the ten directions;
Before all the Buddhas, It spreads forth a rain from the clouds of Dharma.
Within every single pore, He manifests transformation bodies.
Pervading the lands of the ten directions, they deliver sentient beings through skillful means.
When first practicing as a bodhisattva, their pure karma is inconceivable;
within each and every pore, they manifest the lands of the ten directions.
Those who recognize, know, see, and hear [this] shall all obtain the benefits of merit;
by single-mindedly seeking the path to Bodhi, they will certainly attain Buddhahood without doubt.
For inconceivable eons, they shall constantly seek out spiritual friends.
I would rather fall into the three evil realms than abandon the bodhicitta.
Even if one were to praise all its virtues for hundreds of thousands of kalpas as numerous as motes of dust,
those kalpas might come to an end, yet the merit would never be exhausted.

At that time, the youth Sudhana bowed his head in respectful salutation at the feet of that night goddess, circumambulated her countless times, gazing up at her with longing and without ever tiring of the sight; then, taking his leave, he traveled south toward the kingdom of Magadha.
The Sūtra on Rāmaka Spoken by the Buddha, Middle Volume;
The Sūtra on Rāmaka Spoken by the Buddha, Lower Volume.
Translated by the Śramaṇa Shengjian of the Western Qin.
At that time, the youth Sudhana contemplated the instructions of that Night Goddess with single-minded focus;
his initial resolve for the Way became perfectly pure.

Having reflected thus, he immediately attained deep entry into the treasury of all Bodhisattvas and the ocean of dharmas that gives birth to the great vows of Bodhisattvas. He purified the path of the Bodhisattva perfections (*pāramitās*), exhausted the complete and supreme pure deeds of Bodhisattvas, and gave rise to the accomplishment of deep entry into the ocean of wisdom. By means of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), he protected all sentient beings throughout the ten directions, nourished and increased the vast clouds of great compassion, and within all Buddha-fields, brought forth the various great vows and practices of Samantabhadra.

Gradually traveling on, he arrived at the abode of the Night Goddess Viśvagambhīrasūkṣmavimalaguṇaprabhā; he prostrated himself with his head at her feet, circumambulated her countless times, and then withdrew to stand to one side, joining his palms in reverence and addressing her:
"O Celestial Deity!
I have already set my mind on Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi, yet I do not yet know how to cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva or fulfill the various stages.
He replied, “Excellent, excellent,
young man!”
They are thus able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, inquire about the conduct of bodhisattvas, and fulfill all the stages (*bhūmi*).
Son of good family!
When a bodhisattva accomplishes ten dharmas, they are then able to fulfill the conduct of a bodhisattva.
What are the ten?
First, they fully attain the samādhi of all Buddhas appearing before one’s eyes, seeing the form-bodies (*rūpakāya*) of all Buddhas with perfect clarity and distinctness.
Second, they attain the samādhi of the pure eye, seeing all Buddhas adorned with their bodies by the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics (*lakṣaṇānuvyañjana*).
Third, they attain the pure eye of immeasurable and boundless merit, by which they behold the great ocean of wisdom and profound, wondrous merits of all Buddhas.
Fourth, they behold the ocean of light of immeasurable and boundless Buddhas, which is able to universally illumine the entire dharma-realm.

Fifth, there is the immeasurable and inconceivable radiance of the Buddha-dharma: from a single pore, he emits a great light that universally illumines as many sentient beings as there are in number, causing all such diverse beings to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and become an ocean of radiance. With the universally compassionate and impartial mind of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas, in every moment of thought, he performs buddha-works throughout the worlds of the ten directions, delivering sentient beings according to their needs and enabling immeasurable beings to attain liberation.
Sixth, within each and every pore, one sees oceans of flaming mani-jewels with the radiance of all precious gems.

Seventh, in every thought-moment, there emerge great oceans of the transformations of all Buddhas, filling the Dharma-realm, reaching the ultimate bounds of the spheres of all Buddhas, and teaching and transforming sentient beings without obstruction.

Eighth, they produce the great ocean of the subtle and wondrous voices of all Buddhas that abide nowhere, turning the pure wheel of Dharma of the Buddhas of the three periods of time, and expounding the oceans of all sūtras and the oceans of clouds of Dharma; their meanings are profound and far-reaching, beyond the reach of exhaustion.
Ninth, they exhaustively master the ocean of the voices of all Buddhas, penetrating deeply into the ocean of all Tathāgatas and reaching the ultimate limit of the ocean of all Tathāgatas.

Tenth, they penetrate deeply into the manifestation of the inconceivable sovereign spiritual powers of the Buddhas, transforming and delivering sentient beings so that they dwell within the ocean of the immeasurable and boundless renown of all Buddhas.
"Good son! These are called the ten dharmas of a bodhisattva.
If there is a bodhisattva who possesses these ten dharmas, they will be able to fulfill all the practices of a bodhisattva and will also be fully equipped with the conduct and vows of Samantabhadra."

“Good son! I have already accomplished the Bodhisattva Dharma-gate of the Diligence of the Joyful Samādhi of Quiescence. By the power of this samādhi, I see all Buddhas and their oceans of retinues within all the pure and adorned Buddha-lands of the three periods of time. I see the oceans of supernatural powers of immeasurable and boundless Buddha-Tathāgatas; I discern and understand the names of all Buddhas and the oceans of the Tathāgatas turning the wheel of Dharma; I know the short lifespans and the immeasurable lifespans of those Buddhas; I know the oceans of the immeasurable, subtle, and pure voices of those Buddhas; and I know that the pure Dharma-bodies of those Tathāgatas are immeasurable and boundless, filling the Dharma-realm. Furthermore, I do not cling to any of the marks of the Tathāgata, nor do I harbor the thought of ‘marklessness.’”

Why is this? Because the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, possess no marks of coming or going; they have extinguished all marks of coming and going, and do not abide in the limit of suchness within the three periods of time.

Furthermore, they are not of the past and do not abide in the present, for they have extinguished all marks of worldly phenomena and do not grasp at any marks of coming or going. Therefore, they are called Tathāgatas—neither coming nor going.
The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are neither born nor arisen, neither recede nor disappear, neither cease nor manifest; therefore, they are called the Dharma-body.
The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, do not give rise to the nature of speech, nor do they extinguish the nature of speech; they transcend all language because language has been severed.
The Tathāgatas do not truly undergo the extinction of the body; they manifest parinirvāṇa because the nature of phenomena is like an illusion and is indestructible.
Thus, the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are neither real nor unreal, for they desire to bring benefit to all sentient beings.
All Tathāgatas appear in the world through the path of the Tathāgata, which is neither coming nor going.

The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are neither born nor do they perish; they are neither extinguished nor do they abide; they do not come here, nor do they go there, for the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is pure and indestructible.
The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are without nature and without marks, for they are beyond all paths of language.

The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, enter the same single mark of suchness into the dharma-nature, because it is without limit and because they have ultimately realized the nature of the entire dharma-realm.

“Good son! Thus do I understand all Tathāgatas: having attained only this Dharma-gate of the vigor of the bliss of the samādhi of quiescence, I illuminate and increase vast roots of goodness; I enter deeply into and accord with the profound universal manifestation of the realm that is as tranquil as space; I discern and understand the mark of the equality of the false; I expound the profound Great Dharma of equality; with a heart of great compassion, I universally gather in all beings without ever abandoning them; with a single mind of sublime tranquility, free from thoughts of arising or ceasing, I increase my meditative attainments (*samāpatti*), enter the samādhi of quiescence, and arise from the first dhyāna.”
Eliminating mental karma and attaining the power of tranquil wisdom, one gathers in sentient beings with joy and delight, entering the second dhyāna.
Abandoning birth and death for the sake of the tranquility of nirvāṇa, one contemplates the nature of sentient beings and cultivates the third dhyāna.
To extinguish the suffering of the afflictions of all sentient beings, yet without perceiving the mark of a sentient being, they cultivate the fourth dhyāna.

They increase the vows of the bodhicitta of all-knowledge, give birth to the skillful means of the ocean of all bodhisattva concentrations, and enter deeply into the ocean of all dharma-gates. They accomplish the playful supernatural powers of a bodhisattva, give birth to the luminous and pure wisdom of a bodhisattva’s sovereign spiritual power, and enter deeply into the universal gate of the dharma-realm.
"Furthermore, good son!
I have only thus cultivated this Dharma-gate of the Bodhisattva’s joyful diligence in the samādhi of quiescence, using various skillful means to deliver and liberate sentient beings."
At the stillness of midnight, for the sake of householders who are greedily attached to the five desires, he preaches the mark of impurity.

For those who reckon things as pleasant, he preaches the perception of suffering and affliction, the perception of oppression and bondage, the perception of the impurity of food, the perception of mental madness and delusion, and the perception of rākṣasa demons.

For those who conceive of permanence, he teaches the perception of impermanence, the perception of the body as a collection of the eight kinds of suffering, the perception of non-self in what is taken as self, the perception of non-mastery, and the perception of emptiness; such are the perceptions of permanence, impermanence, suffering, and the absence of suffering.

Having contemplated this visualization, he instructs those sentient beings to cultivate revulsion for the five desires; to censure the perception of body and mind; to foster the perception of leaving home from the household life to study the Way; and, while practicing seated meditation in seclusion, to contemplate and eliminate all obstacles, evils, and the sounds of distracting paths.

During the stillness of night, for the sake of bringing peace and stability to the minds of all sentient beings, he manifests such [powers]; through the power of spirits and deities, he removes their terrors and causes them to resolve upon the path to enlightenment.

If there are those who desire to seek renunciation, I shall open for them the gate of the mind of the True Dharma, illuminating their path with light to dispel all darkness and ensure they have no fear; I shall then praise the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha for that person, causing them to resolve upon the Way, and further praise the cultivation of meritorious conduct through associating with virtuous friends.

“Good son! By the power of this Dharma-gate, I now cause all sentient beings to prevent unarisen evil dharmas from arising through skillful means, to extinguish already arisen evil dharmas through skillful means, to cause unarisen wholesome dharmas to arise through skillful means, and to cause already arisen wholesome dharmas to increase through skillful means. They shall extensively practice the bodhisattva deeds, cultivate the various pāramitās, fulfill their great vows, and give birth to all wisdom and compassion. Desiring to enable sentient beings to obtain the bliss of humans and devas, to eliminate false imaginings, and to increase wholesome dharmas, they shall accord with and assist in the accomplishment of inexhaustible, boundless, and non-receptive dharma-practices.”
“Good son! I know only this bodhisattva dharma-gate of the diligence of the bliss of the samādhi of quiescence.

As for these great Bodhisattvas, who have fulfilled the vows of Samantabhadra and are fully endowed with the practices of Samantabhadra; who have ultimately attained the state of being free from darkness and achieved the power of all roots of goodness, as well as the power of the Tathāgata’s realm of light through merit and wisdom; whose Buddha-minds are entirely unobstructed, who have emerged from the darkness of birth and death without being defiled, and who are fully possessed of all the vows of omniscience (*sarvajñā*); who enter deeply into the ocean of all Buddha-lands, who gather up the ocean of all Buddha-dharmas, and who accomplish the ocean of clouds of all sublime Dharmas; and who, through the Tathāgata’s wisdom, are able to universally benefit all sentient beings submerged in the darkness of birth and death, illuminating the night of saṃsāra with the light of wisdom—how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?
"Good son!

Not far from here, toward the right side of the Tathāgata, there is a night goddess named Observing Sentient Beings with Joyful Eyes. Go to her and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct and cultivate the bodhisattva path?'"
At that time, the night goddess Vimalaprabhā, of profoundly deep and subtle merit, wishing to restate the meaning of this Dharma-gate,
spoke in verse: "Deeply entering the samādhi of presence, Universally beholding the Buddhas of the three periods of time,
With pure eyes called 'Stainless,' She discerns the oceans of all Buddhas."
Observing the pure and wondrous body, One enters deeply into the Buddha’s marks and signs;
With infinite power in a single thought, One universally knows the nature of the Dharma-realm.
The pure body sits at the site of enlightenment, The perfect awakening of Vairocana.
Throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm, you turn the pure and wondrous wheel of Dharma.
The Buddha’s awakened wisdom is most supreme; its marks of cessation are non-dual.
Adorned with all manner of exquisite features, you manifest yourself for the sake of all beings.
The Buddha’s body is inconceivable, a single body like empty space;
it manifests universally throughout the lands of the ten directions, teaching and transforming all beings at once.
It emits perfectly pure light, encompassing all Buddha-lands and the like.
Inconceivable pure form universally illumines all dharma-realms.
From every single pore, he manifests immeasurable Buddha-lands and immeasurable,
subtle, wondrous forms, universally shining upon all worlds.
Inconceivable radiance manifests from every pore,
Universally illuminating all classes of sentient beings and extinguishing their manifold afflictions.
Transformation Buddhas emit wondrous sounds, Filling the realms of the ten directions.
Universally beholding all Buddha-fields, they are all like thunder and lightning.
The wondrous voice of the Tathāgata fills the realms of the ten directions,
universally raining down the Dharma of nectar, causing [beings] to resolve upon Bodhicitta.
Having practiced for incalculable eons, gathering in and sustaining all sentient beings,
he universally beholds Vairocana and all the Buddha-fields.
All sounds and voices in the world— the Tathāgata has completely transcended them.
Universally manifesting before all classes of beings, causing the multitudes to abide within their spheres;
the inconceivable practices of all Bodhisattvas,
they are able to know them all in a single instant within a single pore of the Buddha.
"Not far away is a night goddess named Priyadarśanālokā;
you should go to her and ask: 'How does a bodhisattva practice?

At that time, the youth Sudhana bowed his head in respectful salutation at the feet of that night goddess, circumambulated her countless times, and with a look of longing admiration, took his leave and proceeded toward the night goddess Priyadarśanālokā-sattva-darśanī.

At that time, the youth Sudhana single-mindedly sought spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra), maintaining right mindfulness of the instructions of spiritual friends; through spiritual friends, he gave rise to all merits and awakened the bodhicitta.
Spiritual friends are difficult to see and difficult to encounter; upon seeing a spiritual friend, one gives rise to a heart of joy, which extinguishes all distracted thoughts.
Spiritual friends eliminate doubt and confusion, and are able to destroy all obstacles.
Upon seeing a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), one should know that one immediately draws near to all-knowledge (sarvajñatā);
upon seeing a spiritual friend, one immediately gains deep entry into the ocean of the Buddhas' Dharma;

upon seeing a spiritual friend, one should give rise to the perception of all Tathāgatas of the ten directions; when hearing what a spiritual friend proclaims, one should know that one immediately attains the perception of the *dhāraṇī* of the Cloud of Right Mindfulness of the Dharma (*samyaksmṛti-dharmamegha-dhāraṇī*), upholds all pure Buddha-Dharmas, and perceives all Buddhas turning the wheel of Dharma.
Upon seeing a spiritual friend, one immediately possesses the entire ocean of great compassion to rescue and protect all sentient beings;
upon seeing a spiritual friend, one should give rise to joy, for their wisdom becomes bright and pure, capable of universally illuminating the entire ocean of the Buddha-dharma realm.
At that time, the Night Goddess Joyful Eye Observing Sentient Beings, through her majestic spiritual power, empowered the youth Sudhana and praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
"Good son!

To be able to seek spiritual friends in this way, to go to spiritual friends, and to draw near to and make offerings to spiritual friends—this itself is bodhi; seeking spiritual friends is great diligence."

Good son! A spiritual friend is difficult to see and difficult to encounter; the power of a spiritual friend is indestructible; a spiritual friend wanders throughout the ten directions, eliminating birth and death, severing all afflictions, and being able to bring about eloquence.
A spiritual friend deeply enters all immeasurable great matters and adorns the path that is upright and compliant.

A spiritual friend is entirely a dharma-gate of universal manifestation; they can cause all beings to attain non-obstruction, reaching all the abodes of the Buddhas throughout the ten directions without departing from their original place.

In seeking a spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra), one should give rise to this conception: that they neither come nor go, are neither moving nor shaking, and are devoid of the characteristics of coming and going; for the sake of protecting all sentient beings through omniscience (sarvajñatā), one should seek such a virtuous friend.
At that time, the youth Sudhana, upon seeing the spiritual friend, immediately attained the realization of the infinite and boundless ocean of great vows;
he attained all-knowledge to benefit sentient beings, and by drawing near to virtuous friends,
he served all sentient beings throughout oceans of worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and as many as atoms for the duration of this entire life.
Throughout the ocean of realms, reaching to the very limits of this world and extending beyond those boundaries for immeasurable,
boundless, and unspeakably unspeakable numbers of great hells, he gives rise to compassion for those sentient beings,
turning directly toward Bodhi to eliminate the suffering of beings throughout immeasurable eons, pervading all with a single voice.
Throughout all worlds in the ten directions, the sublime Dharma is proclaimed; if there are those who hear it, their karmic obstacles of birth and death from immeasurable kalpas will be extinguished.
Adorned by great wisdom and vows, they cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva, and in every thought-moment, they attain the marks of omniscience and possess supernormal powers regarding all things.
In every dwelling, they constantly see all Buddhas, Tathāgatas, whom they approach and make offerings to as spiritual friends;
they adorn themselves with the adornments of the Buddhas, universally purifying the Dharma-realm of all Buddhas of the three periods of time;
they do not enter the stream of birth nor abide in the stream of death, possessing the supernatural powers of the Buddhas, neither abiding within the Dharma-realm nor...
Without departing from the Dharma-realm, they are able to travel to the worlds of the ten directions and reach the presence of spiritual friends who fill the Dharma-realm;
unattached to words, in every single moment, they cultivate the bodhisattva practices,
fulfill the realm of their nature, achieve omniscience (*sarvajñā*), and are endowed with all the playful manifestations of a Buddha’s supernormal powers.
He adorned the Buddha-way through the dharma of equality; with body and mind unmoving, he universally gathered in all sentient beings.
By the power of his spiritual friends, he manifested throughout the three periods of time.
At that time, the youth Sudhana went to the place where the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocana was. Then...

That night goddess, seated upon a lion throne of precious lotuses amidst the great assembly, was correctly receiving the bodhisattva dharma-door of the "Joyful Purity of the Banner of Universally Manifesting Light. From all her pores issued forth clouds of exquisite colors;
those who beheld them were filled with joy and never grew weary, as each and every pore manifested clouds of various jewels.
What is called the retribution of the practice of wisdom benefits sentient beings and brings them away from strife and litigation.
With an impartial mind, one does not cling to any phenomena; with supreme and wondrous knowledge, one gathers in all sentient beings.
Manifesting throughout the three periods of time, one cultivates the bodhisattva practices with a heart free from stinginess, able to relinquish what is difficult to give, bestowing universally.
All things are equal in body and mind, inconceivable; by the merit of giving, they universally gather in all sentient beings.
Toward all sentient beings, they give rise to no defiled attachment and perceive no manifold signs, yet they do not abandon sentient beings.
They fully possess the ascetic practices of Bodhisattvas throughout the three periods of time for all sentient beings in the worlds of the ten directions.
Bound by ignorance and dwelling within the fetters of delusion and existence, the Bodhisattva immediately employs the supernormal powers of great compassion to untie those bonds.

Furthermore, from every pore, he brings forth clouds of transformation-bodies of Bodhisattvas—equal in number to all sentient beings—each possessing sovereign mastery and appearing according to the needs of others. These clouds of bodies fill the entirety of space and the Dharma-realm; before the presence of sentient beings, they manifest physical forms in meditative absorption, remaining unmoving. Before these beings, through samādhi and supernormal powers, they awaken them, causing them to take no pleasure in the world, to distance themselves from the three realms, and to extinguish birth and death as if avoiding a pit of fire. Yet, amidst all things, they manifest the cycle of birth and death, displaying the various joys of gods and humans, as well as the signs of success and failure.
For the sake of all sentient beings, he teaches the contemplation of impurity, causing all sentient beings to practice it universally and eliminate their inverted perceptions.
For the sake of all sentient beings, he teaches the dharma of the suffering of change, [showing that] all conditioned dharmas involving the assumption of a body are entirely impermanent.

May all sentient beings enter deeply into the realm of the Buddhas, forever leave behind impermanence, and abide in the inconceivable *śīlapāramitā*; may they constantly receive the pure prohibitions and precepts of all Buddhas, never violating them, and have no doubts or hesitations in their minds.
They demonstrate to all sentient beings the fulfillment of the prohibitive precepts, perfuming all beings with the fragrance of the precepts.

Furthermore, from their pores, they produce clouds of bodies of every exquisite form; whether their hands and feet or various limbs and members are cut off, or they are beaten, coerced, rebuked, reviled, falsely slandered, or defamed, they endure it all. Toward those beings, they do not give rise to anger or harmful intent; rather, they praise even wicked people, never violating their conduct, and with body and mind full of reverence, they develop deep affection for them, just as parents cherish an only son with compassion.

Although they practice these deeds, they do not give rise to a mind of arrogance or conceit; they manifest the *dharmakṣānti* of the *tathatā* of all phenomena; they are skillfully able to harmonize with all wicked sentient beings in every world; they deeply understand the wisdom of emptiness regarding the nature of exhaustion and non-exhaustion; they practice the patience of a bodhisattva; and with the Buddha-mind wisdom, they sever all afflictions and extinguish all fetters and habitual tendencies. They are fully capable of bearing the burden of all the ugly and evil sentient beings of the world, protecting them as they would their own eyes.
They vow that all sentient beings shall achieve the adamantine patience-virtue of all Buddhas, becoming pure and free from blemish.
Furthermore, within each and every pore, he manifests the pure form-body (*rūpakāya*) of the Tathāgata, so that all sentient beings who are ready to be delivered may behold it.

Moreover, from each and every pore, he produces various form-bodies corresponding to all realms of existence, manifesting courageous and diligent effort to cause sentient beings to practice as if their hair were on fire, thereby subduing all demonic adversaries and attaining supreme non-retrogression.

They rescue and protect all beings, uprooting them from the ocean of birth and death; they are forever free from all afflictions and the terrors of ignorance, and have crossed over the mountains of saṃsāra. They are eternally detached from the currents of desire, making offerings to and revering all Buddhas with a mind free from weariness. They uphold and protect the Dharma wheels of all Buddhas, practicing with courageous diligence to eliminate all obstacles.
Universally gathering all sentient beings, they cause them all to be tamed and enter into the practice of the precepts, their minds free from indolence.
Universally manifesting all pure Buddha-lands, they teach and transform sentient beings, adorning the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Such merits as these all arise from the karmic retribution of the fundamental practices of the *vīryapāramitā*.

From every single pore, there appear all manner of forms and colors; through various skillful means, they eliminate the sorrows, afflictions, and sufferings of sentient beings, causing them all to rejoice. They cause [beings] to reproach and weary of all five desires, to give rise deeply to a sense of shame and remorse, to subdue their faculties, and to practice the unsurpassed and most supreme Brahma-conduct. They purify the karma of body, speech, and mind, and manifest that all worldly desires are ultimately not to be enjoyed.

Manifesting such various forms and colors, they cause all beings to experience joy; they always delight in upholding [the teachings], giving rise to the True Dharma, and with minds undistracted, they dwell securely and deeply enter the nine successive concentrations, extinguishing all afflictions of sentient beings and causing them to attain peace and happiness.

He manifested the ocean of bodhisattva samādhis, the supernormal powers of penetrating clarity, and the sphere of sovereign spiritual might, causing the bodies and minds of all sentient beings to rejoice, extinguishing the heat of their afflictions, attaining cool and refreshing bliss, increasing wholesome dharmas, ensuring that their physical, verbal, and mental actions were always tranquil, delighting their faculties, and enabling them to attain the joy of the Dharma.

Furthermore, within each and every pore, they manifest all places of birth within the five destinies, causing those in the five destinies throughout the ten directions to see their bodies; they proceed to the abodes of all Buddhas, reaching the limits of all Buddha-fields, where they reverently make offerings to all Buddhas, teachers, and spiritual friends, their minds never wearying.
They are able to receive and uphold all the wheels of Dharma turned by all Tathāgatas, never becoming weary or exhausted, nor giving rise to regression.

They exhaustively traverse the ocean of all Buddha-fields to transform and deliver sentient beings, manifesting the ocean of all dharmas and upholding the True Dharma. Seeing no marks of phenomena, they manifest all gateways of samādhi within the single true reality. With body and mind pure, they are able to sever the doubts and delusions of all sentient beings. By the power of wisdom, they discern the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings; with adamantine wisdom, they shatter the mountains of all false views of sentient beings, and give birth to the perfect, bright, and pure sun of wisdom.

In a single thought-moment, they are able to dispel the dark obscurations of ignorance for sentient beings, causing them to distance themselves from the stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas, as well as from doubt, perversion, and the two extremes of existence and non-existence; all become filled with joy, attain the bliss of wisdom, and are all taught to dedicate their merit toward the Buddha-way.

Furthermore, from every single pore, they manifest bodies as numerous as the dust motes of all sentient beings, displaying various physical forms and inconceivable bodies. According to those who are to be delivered, they appear before them all; within a single sound they speak infinite sounds, and within infinite sounds they expound a single sound. Adapting to the languages of all classes of sentient beings, they proclaim the treasury of the merits of all Buddhas. They demonstrate the performance of worldly actions—whether conditioned, unconditioned, determinate, or indeterminate—and fully comprehend the karmic fruits and retributions of the three periods of time. Having no attachment to the triple world, they praise the supramundane Dharma that transcends the triple world. They cause all those suffering from the famine of inverted views and false attachments to escape and turn toward the path of ambrosia, proceeding toward omniscience and surmounting the fears of the various stages and the two vehicles.

Regarding the conditioned and the unconditioned, their minds have no attachment; they turn their backs on birth and death and head directly toward Nirvana. They do not abandon various practices nor depart from the various realms of existence; though they come and go through the five paths, they never grow weary. They give rise to the mind of supreme progress and achieve equanimity, using the Dharma of perfect enlightenment to teach and transform sentient beings, thereby attaining all-knowledge.

From each and every pore, there emerge and manifest clouds of transformation bodies as numerous as the atoms within all buddha-fields. These appear before all sentient beings, cultivating the practices of Samantabhadra and fulfilling all vows without end. They exhort sentient beings toward omniscience (*sarvajñā*), and in a single thought-moment, they manifest the cultivation of all pure conduct and the offering and reverent service to all Tathāgatas with insatiable devotion. They raise the banner of the Dharma to subdue non-Buddhists, protect all bodhisattva practices, and maintain an uninterrupted continuity of mind, fully perfecting all the *pāramitās*.

Within each and every ocean of atoms, there arise oceans of the nature of all phenomena, and oceans of the sounds of all teachings are proclaimed, pervading the oceans of lands as numerous as atoms throughout the ten directions. By means of these sounds, for as long as an ocean of world-systems as numerous as atoms and for as many eons as there are atoms in an ocean of worlds, they nurture the roots of goodness of all sentient beings. They abide for as many unspeakably unspeakable eons as there are atoms in an ocean of Buddha-lands as numerous as the *asaṃkhyeya* of all infinite and boundless [atoms], causing all sentient beings to attain progress; furthermore, exceeding even this number, they abide in life without ceasing.

At the time of the kalpa’s destruction, by virtue of the Buddha’s spiritual power, they shall attain non-extinction. They shall go before all Buddhas appearing in the Buddha-fields of every atom throughout the three periods of time, paying them respect and making offerings; they shall protect and uphold the Buddhas’ true wheel of Dharma, sport in supernatural powers, purify Buddha-lands, and transform sentient beings. Reaching each and every such place, they shall cause all sentient beings to experience great joy, radiance, and happiness.
From each and every pore, he emanates all transformation bodies, appearing within a single pore in accordance with the karmic retributions of all sentient beings.
Furthermore, from each and every pore, he rains down all manner of offerings to worship all Buddhas and bestow them upon sentient beings;
by the power of the mind of the Dharma King, his realm is indestructible and inexhaustible.

Firmly abiding in the nature of reality (*tathatā*), neither regressing nor sinking, with mental activities characterized by equanimity, free from dwelling or attachment, they give rise to the practice of infinite, pure joy.
By the power of their compassionate mind, they eliminate the evils and sins of all sentient beings;
through the power of the Bodhisattvas' original vows and virtuous aspirations, they crush the four Māras and extinguish [all afflictions].
Having eliminated the mountain of all afflictions and karma, exhausted all worldly dharmas, and cultivated great compassion,
they attain non-retrogression in the bodhisattva practices. Universally gathering all sentient beings with whom they have a karmic connection throughout the worlds of the ten directions,
they cause them to practice the various pāramitās and manifest the inexhaustible merits of a bodhisattva, reaching...
They attain the supreme and wondrous bodhi-dhāraṇīs of the Bodhisattva’s banner for turning the wheel of Dharma; by means of this sublime wisdom, they subdue those of external paths.

Possessing the power of the Bodhisattva’s practice and the pāramitās, for the sake of all sentient beings and in order to lead them toward sarvajñatā (all-knowledge), they manifest from every single pore the marks of a body equal to all sentient beings, causing all beings to delight in beholding them.

Furthermore, within each and every pore, there appeared oceans of all categories of sentient beings; moreover, there appeared immeasurable and innumerable bodies of wondrous form, equal in number to the atoms of unspeakably many oceans of worlds in the ten directions, all of which were fully manifested.
According to the power of the bodhisattva’s wisdom and conduct in accordance with sentient beings, they manifest unspeakably unspeakable oceans of wisdom;
they skillfully know the ocean of the minds of all sentient beings, skillfully know the ocean of the faculties of all sentient beings,
and know the ocean of the primary and secondary mental states of all sentient beings, penetrating deeply into the ultimate dharma-realm of wisdom.
In every moment of thought, they are able to universally fill all dharma-realms;
they liberate themselves from the mundane world, praise that which transcends the world, adorn and purify buddha-lands, and praise the sentient beings of those pure lands.
They study and practice the playful supernatural powers of all Buddhas, and they praise the supernatural powers and the power of vows of all Buddhas, proceeding to them...
In the presence of the Buddha, they made offerings, paid homage, and protected and upheld the cloud-like wheel of the True Dharma;

they manifested the ten pāramitās of wisdom, causing all sentient beings to rejoice greatly, extinguishing their feverish afflictions, leading them far away from sorrow and the eight worldly dharmas, causing them to abandon all evils, and subduing their sense faculties. Within a single...
They attain all-knowledge and reach the stage of non-retrogression.
Through these various *pāramitās*, they bring joy and peace to sentient beings and transform them.

These great Bodhisattvas, by means of this supreme Dharma, thunder the great Dharma-thunder to awaken all sentient beings who are asleep. With the light of the power of wisdom and the Dharma from their supreme insight, they are universally able to rectify the deluded and evil conduct of others. They also perceive the inherently pure conduct of the Buddhas, which is manifested within a single pore without any obstruction.

The night goddess Priyadarsana-avalokita cultivates meritorious virtues by seeking spiritual friends, approaching all Buddhas to attend upon and make offerings to them, practicing various forms of goodness, and performing the dāna-pāramitā. She is able to relinquish what is difficult to give, completely renouncing her royal throne, kingdom, cities, palaces, ministers, concubines, subjects, and retinue to leave the household life and study the Way; this is called the practice of the dāna-pāramitā.

Practicing the perfection of ethical discipline (śīlapāramitā) means cultivating and upholding pure precepts as if guarding one's only eye; even while undergoing all the various sufferings of the world, one does not violate the precepts one has undertaken. That which no sentient being is capable of doing, the Bodhisattva performs—this is called practicing the perfection of ethical discipline.

Practicing the perfection of patience (*kṣānti-pāramitā*), one endures all instances where sentient beings respond with anger, abuse, physical assault, or slander, even when their bodies are subjected to such oppression; yet one remains free from any expression of resentment.
One is likewise able to endure all such hardships as when sentient beings deprive one of profit or happiness, or cause harm to one’s loved ones.

Even if one were to burn one's body with the three fires and undergo all manner of suffering, the mind would be filled with great joy; it would be like a bhikṣu entering the third dhyāna, experiencing physical and mental bliss, having deep faith in all dharmas and being capable of receiving them as neither arising nor ceasing—this is called practicing the pāramitā of kṣānti.

Practicing the *vīryapāramitā* for the sake of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), one endures all manner of suffering; even when each limb is burned by fire, one never feels terror. For the sake of omniscience, one arouses great valor and diligence as if putting out a fire on one's own head, seeking awakening with exclusive devotion. With body and mind firm and indestructible, free from thoughts of exhaustion, one never regresses—this is called practicing the *vīryapāramitā*.

Practicing the dhyānapāramitā with body and mind undisturbed, pervading all directions, fulfilling the pure dhyānapāramitā, and being courageous and diligent without abandoning samādhi—this is called dhyānapāramitā.

Attaining ultimate purity in all pure practices, entering superior samādhis, sporting with supernormal powers, and crossing the great ocean of wisdom—wherein every thought-moment continues in succession and one enters pure concentration step by step—this is called the dhyāna-pāramitā.
To fulfill all skillful means while keeping body and mind perpetually pure is called the dhyāna-pāramitā.
To exhaustively master the ocean of all meditative concentrations and the ocean of all samādhis, continuing them in succession without ever interruption, is called the dhyāna-pāramitā.

Practicing the *prajñāpāramitā*, one is attached neither to that nor to this; within the dharma of emptiness, one attains great liberation. This is the pure and perfect *prajñāpāramitā* of the Great Bodhisattva, the natural wisdom from which the sun of pure insight arises; with body and mind unattached, one enters the treasury of wisdom and ultimately contemplates the ocean of great wisdom—the *prajñāpāramitā*. Unattached to the marks of phenomena, one practices the realm of supreme, pure knowledge—the auspicious *prajñāpāramitā*. It gives birth to the ocean of wisdom of wondrous meanings—the *prajñāpāramitā*.

One who practices skillful means gives birth to all bodies of skillful means and universally knows the power of supreme progress within the luminously pure Dharma-realm of omniscience; this is called the perfection of skillful means (upāya-pāramitā).

Through pure wisdom and skillful means, one gives birth to the body born of the dharma-nature; within the interval of a single inhalation and exhalation, one attains the non-dual practice of pure skillful means—this is called the perfection of skillful means (upāya-pāramitā).

The bodhisattvas, by virtue of their original great vows, manifest pure bodies and take birth fully endowed with all attributes to gather in and sustain sentient beings; regarding all sentient beings and all virtuous deeds, their minds are pure and free from attachment—this is called practicing the perfection of skillful means (upāya-pāramitā).

The perfection of the practice of vows gives birth to the body of the ocean of all vows; it penetrates deeply into the ocean of all wisdom-samādhis; it transcends all stages of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas; it manifests the birth of the originally pure perfections of vow and practice; it neither abandons nor grasps, but according to whatever is sought through the original practices of wisdom, it purifies the bodies of all vows—this is called the purity of the perfection of the practice of vows.

Practicing the perfection of power (*balapāramitā*), being fully endowed with all merits, attaining mastery according to one's will, and cultivating the factors conducive to enlightenment—this is called the perfection of power.

Because of these factors conducive to enlightenment, one benefits sentient beings, cultivates all merits, yet remains unattached to those merits and does not perceive the marks of merit—this is called the perfection of power.
Being fully endowed with both the power of causes and the power of results, like the great ocean—this is called the perfection of power (*bala-pāramitā*).
To manifest the various sequences of phenomena and explain the powers of knowledge—this is called the perfection of power.

The power of the intellect that expounds the intermingled forces of cause and effect, wherein wisdom is intermingled with the force of karma—this is called the perfection of the power of practice (*caryā-bala-pāramitā*).

The body of the perfection of the power of practice is the purity of the name of the perfection of wisdom; the sphere of wisdom is the perfection of wisdom; the correct and swift progression is the perfection of wisdom; the universal manifestation of radiance is the perfection of wisdom. It is like a wondrous fragrance that permeates other substances alike, or like an echo that responds to every call; this is called the perfection of wisdom (*jñāna-pāramitā*).

The light of the flames of wisdom, with its supreme and wondrous sounds, expounds the flavor of meaning without end, universally encompassing all; this is called the perfection of wisdom (jñāna-pāramitā).

The perfection of wisdom (*jñānapāramitā*) is that which brings forth and fulfills the fruits of original practices, its nature and characteristics being pure; this is called the perfection of wisdom.

The perfection of wisdom is unattached and unguarded, gathering all forms of omniscience and the aids to enlightenment (*bodhipakṣadharma*) that are free from attachment. With clear and lucid wisdom, it possesses the stages of supreme progress and enters deeply into the sphere of profound cognitive activity; this is called the perfection of wisdom.

The perfection of wisdom (*jñānapāramitā*) is profoundly subtle; it consists in knowing the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*) through the knowledge of dharmas, embracing all phenomena, and conforming to wisdom. It skillfully discerns the characteristics of fields of merit (*puṇyakṣetra*) and non-fields of merit as they truly are; this is called the perfection of wisdom.

The wisdom of all Tathāgatas transcends the triple world and thoroughly penetrates the three periods of time. It skillfully knows all the practices and deeds of Bodhisattvas, universally gathering all forms of wisdom without any obstruction. It also knows the dwelling place of a Bodhisattva’s correct wisdom and the right conduct that should be cultivated. Furthermore, it skillfully knows how to progress from the initial aspiration toward the higher stages; with a mind of skillful means, it skillfully knows dedication, and skillfully knows the suchness of all phenomena, the suchness of karma, the suchness of retribution, and the suchness of the wheel of Dharma. Knowing the characteristics of the suchness of the wheel of Dharma is called the perfection of wisdom (jñānapāramitā).
Supremely wondrous and unattached, he upholds the True Dharma. One who upholds the True Dharma comprehensively knows all dharmas.
One who comprehensively knows all dharmas knows the Tathāgata as the Dharma and knows the Tathāgata as the Thus-Gone.
He skillfully knows the realms of karma and karma, skillfully knows the realms of lands and lands, skillfully knows all kalpas, and skillfully knows...
The wisdom of the three periods of time gives birth to the wisdom of all Buddhas; it knows the Buddha-wisdom of equal and right enlightenment,
knows the wisdom of Bodhisattvas, knows the wisdom of the knowledge of Bodhisattvas, knows the wisdom of the dwelling of Bodhisattvas, knows the wisdom of the merit and wisdom of Bodhisattvas,
knows the wisdom of the dedication of the pure mind of Bodhisattvas, knows the wisdom of all great vows, and turns the Dharma wheel.
The wheel-wisdom; the wisdom that knows the discrimination of phenomena; the wisdom that enters the ocean of phenomena; the wisdom that knows the ocean of skillful means;
the wisdom that knows the *dhāraṇī* of the revolving flow of phenomena; the wisdom that knows the ultimate destination of all phenomena;
and suchlike all-perfected wisdoms (*sarvajñatā-pāramitā*), which are profound and bottomless, vast and boundless, and ultimately inexhaustible.

In this manner, these ten supreme perfections of wisdom are all manifested within a single pore; likewise, within every pore, all transformation bodies are manifested to edify and deliver sentient beings.
Furthermore, from every single pore, he produces immeasurable clouds of bodies, namely: clouds of bodies of the Akaniṣṭha devas,
clouds of bodies of the Śuddhāvāsa devas, clouds of bodies of the Sudarśana devas, clouds of bodies of the Atapa devas,
clouds of bodies of the Bṛhatphala devas, clouds of bodies of the Śubhakṛtsna devas, and clouds of bodies of the Apramāṇaśubha devas.
Clouds of the bodies of the Parīttābha devas, clouds of the bodies of the Śuddhāvāsakāyika devas,
clouds of the bodies of the Bṛhatphala devas, clouds of the bodies of the Apramāṇaśubha devas, clouds of the bodies of the Parīttaśubha devas, clouds of the bodies of the Ābhāsvara devas,
clouds of the bodies of the Apramāṇābhāsvara devas, clouds of the bodies of the Parīttābhāsvara devas, and clouds of the bodies of the Mahābrahmā devas.
Clouds of the bodies of the Brahmā-purohita devas; clouds of the bodies of the Brahma-pārṣadya devas;
clouds of the bodies of the Mahābrahmā devas; clouds of the bodies of the Brahmottara devas; clouds of the bodies of the Brahmendra kings;
clouds of the bodies of the Paranirmita-vaśavartin Indra kings, their sons, and their daughters; and clouds of the bodies of the Nirmāṇarati Indra kings and the Nirmāṇarati devas.
Clouds of the bodies of the sons of the gods and goddesses; clouds of the bodies of the Tuṣita Heaven kings, Tuṣita Heaven sons, and Tuṣita Heaven goddesses;
clouds of the bodies of the Yāma Heaven king, his sons, and his goddesses;
clouds of the bodies of Śakra Devendra, the thirty-two attendant ministers, their sons, and their goddesses; and the Dhṛtarāṣṭra Heaven king...
Clouds of the bodies of all the sons, daughters, and retinues of the devas; clouds of the bodies of all the male and female gandharvas;
clouds of the bodies of the deva-king Virūḍhaka and his retinue of sons, daughters, and all kumbhāṇḍas, male and female;
and clouds of the bodies of the deva-king Virūpākṣa and his retinue of sons, daughters, and all nāgas, male and female.
Clouds of Vaiśravaṇa, King of the Heavenly World, together with his retinue of devaputras, devakanyās, and all male and female yakṣas;
clouds of the bodies of kinnara kings and all male and female kinnaras;
clouds of the bodies of mahoraga kings and all male and female mahoragas; and clouds of garuḍa kings.
And clouds of the bodies of all male and female garuḍas; clouds of the bodies of asura kings and all male and female asuras;
clouds of the bodies of Yama and all male and female yamas; as well as clouds of the bodies of those in the hells and evil destinies;
clouds of the bodies of human kings; and clouds of the bodies of men and women, boys and girls.
Clouds of male children with female bodies, and such clouds of bodies from all realms of existence as these—
clouds of the bodies of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and rishis; clouds of earth deities, water deities, fire deities, wind deities, ocean deities, river deities,
mountain and forest deities, tree deities, grain deities, flavor deities, and medicinal herb deities.
The deities of gardens and groves, the deities of springs and seas, the deities of city walls, the deities of places of practice (*dharma-paryāya*),

the deities of night, the deities of day, the deities of space, the deities of the directions, the deities of paths, the deities of bodily forms, the deities of the solar spirit, the deities of various *chi-mei* (goblins),
the deities of the *vajra*-powerful ones (*vajrapāṇi*), and the deities who walk on foot— such as these one [hundred thousand].
Clouds of the bodies of all deities pervade all worlds throughout the ten directions,
manifesting bodies that are joyfully beheld for the sake of all sentient beings who are equal to the dharma-realm.

At that time, the Night Goddess Joyful Eye Observing Sentient Beings, from her first generation of the mind of enlightenment, accumulated immeasurable *pāramitās* through her practiced merits; she underwent successive births, dying here and being born there, revolving through the five destinies. She [remembers] their names, her proximity to spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*), her encounters with all Buddhas, her proximity to and making offerings to them, her hearing and upholding the True Dharma, and her practice of the bodhisattva path. With a mind free from hindrance, she attained various *samādhis* and successively beheld all Buddhas, their physical bodies and marks of excellence. She saw all Buddha-lands and witnessed the successive formation and destruction of all eons (*kalpa*). Having attained pure wisdom and deeply entered the Dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), she observed sentient beings and knew the ocean of sentient beings as they die here and are born there.
They attain the pure divine ear and hear all sounds in their proper sequence;
by hearing these sounds, they acquire the knowledge of others' minds and fully know the thoughts and mental states of all sentient beings;
with unimpeded supernormal powers, they exercise mastery in succession, remain unattached to the world, and do not undergo further existence.
Pervading the entirety of the realm of empty space, his pure Dharma-nature body has attained supernatural powers and the pure, wondrous fruits of retribution, filling the ten directions.
He has attained the successive Dharma-gates of all bodhisattvas and reached the ultimate ocean of all bodhisattva Dharma-gates.
Possessing the sovereign mastery of a bodhisattva, he is courageous and diligent; his bodhisattva strides are as if non-existent.
Free from fear, they reach the correct course, depart from the marks of birth and death, and attain the supreme, wondrous, and pure Dharma-door that gathers all merit according to one's wishes.
Equal to the entire dharma-realm, they equally manifest clouds of bodies of all merits and clouds of bodies of all wisdom;
they proclaim the sounds of the Dharma, revealing and transforming beings.
Causing them to attain refuge, manifesting the Great Way in all places,
fanning and stirring sounds within the wind-circles to manifest the preaching of the Dharma, causing them to receive, uphold, and be inspired by the teachings with joy;
contemplating without attachment, [hearing] the sounds of the earth shaking, water flowing, ocean waves, fire flames, and mountains clashing, as well as those of the devas...
The sound of the palace-city shaking; the thunderous roar of the mani-jewel halls;
the sounds of the celestial kings’ forms and colors dancing with joy; the sounds of the dragon kings raising clouds and rolling thunder;
and all those of the yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and so forth.
The divine king [heard] the various sounds from the ten jewel mountains; the voices of the universal monarchs, the minor kings, and all the multitudes of men and women;
the voice of Brahmā; the sounds of the songs and hymns of all the devas;
the sounds of celestial music; the sounds of the divine jewels and mani-gem kings; and the voices of the devas.
The voices of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas; the voice of the Tathāgata;
and the voices emanated by the transformation bodies of the Tathāgata—such various voices as these are expounded in detail for the sake of all sentient beings.

The Night Goddess *Ratnalocanā* (Joyful Eye Observing Sentient Beings), from her first resolution for enlightenment, has attained that which is difficult to attain regarding the sphere of her merit; she has performed all ascetic practices that are difficult to perform. Through such deeds, all sustained by the power of the Buddha, she has attained mastery over clouds of transformation bodies of all merits. Within each cloud of transformation bodies, she continuously and without interruption proclaims this pure and unattached Dharma-cloud. In every moment of thought, she travels through the worlds of the ten directions to cultivate pure lands. Furthermore, she causes immeasurable and boundless sentient beings who would otherwise suffer the pains of the evil realms to achieve the bliss of devas and humans;

she enables immeasurable and boundless sentient beings to cross the ocean of birth and death, and immeasurable and boundless sentient beings to dwell securely in the stages of Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas.

Infinite and boundless sentient beings leave behind the stages of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas and attain the non-retrogressive state of bodhisattvas; they practice the inconceivable, vast, and expansive *dharmaparyāya* of the Sovereign Banner of Joy, and in every thought-moment, cause infinite and boundless sentient beings to abide in the stage of the Tathāgata.

At that time, the youth Sudhana saw and heard all of these things; he thoroughly understood and comprehended these extraordinary events, contemplating them with right mindfulness, examining and discerning them, deeply entering into meditative concentration and wisdom, and abiding in equanimity.

Why is this? Because they practice together with that Night Goddess Prabhāśarīrā; because they are protected and remembered by the Buddhas; because they have accomplished inconceivable, illusion-like roots of goodness; because they are endowed with the inconceivable faculties of a bodhisattva; because they have perfected the various roots of goodness of a bodhisattva; because they have been born into the family of the Tathāgata lineage; because they have obtained the power of the grace of spiritual friends; because they are sustained by the unattached supernatural powers of all Tathāgatas; because of the power of the original vows of Vairocana Buddha; and because they have accomplished roots of goodness capable of receiving the various vows and practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.

At that time, the youth Sudhana attained the bodhisattva dharma of the ocean-banner of the pure light of joy; he attained the power of all Tathāgatas of the ten directions; and he attained the dharma-gate of the banner of the night goddess Virocana. Having attained that dharma-gate, he entered deeply into the observation of the samādhi of the ocean of dharmas of light universally illuminating the ten directions.
At that time, the youth Sudhana rose with reverence and, joining his palms, praised that Night Goddess with these verses:
"Throughout immeasurable and innumerable eons, You have deeply entered the most supreme Dharma.
Manifesting the wondrous Dharma-body, You appear according to what each being should see."
Fully knowing the minds of all beings, And their delusions of ignorance and perversion,
He employs various skillful means To deliver and liberate the multitudes of sentient beings.
His eternally pure and wondrous Dharma-body Has long since eliminated all burning afflictions.
Though non-dual, they manifest duality for the sake of liberating sentient beings.
Regarding the aggregates, sense bases, and elements, they are entirely without attachment;
through all practices and the form-body, they are liberated from all existence.
Not clinging to internal or external phenomena, he has crossed the ocean of birth and death;
with the light of pure and brilliant wisdom, he universally illuminates the darkness of saṃsāra.
With eyes of joy and senses free from attachment, he eradicates all doubts and delusions.
To manifest all worldly pleasures for the sake of joy,
the Buddhas appear throughout the ten directions by the power of the unimpeded samādhi. From every single pore,
they emit clouds of transformation bodies, arising through the samādhi born of mental recollection.
By the power of the samādhi of mental recollection, they make offerings to the Buddhas of the ten directions,
gather in all sentient beings, and bring all dharmas to ultimate completion.
They observe the ocean of all realms of existence, wherein karmic actions serve as their own adornment.
He expounds the path of unimpeded eloquence in order to purify all beings.
Adorned with the full array of marks and signs, like the very image of Samantabhadra,
he manifests an unimpeded body according to those who are ready to be transformed.
At that time, after the youth Sudhana had praised her with these verses, he said: "O Devī,
how long has it been since you first resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*?"
"How long has it been since you attained this Dharma-gate?
At that time, the Night Goddess replied in verse:
"I recall a past age, As many eons ago as there are atoms in immeasurable lands."
At that time there was an eon named Silent Sound;
in its city there was a wheel-turning king with a pure and wondrous physical form,
endowed with the thirty-two marks and adorned by the eighty minor characteristics.
With a wondrous body like a perfect banner, the color of Jāmbūnada gold,
his radiance illuminating all, he moves serenely through the void;
the thousand sons of the Wheel-Turning King are valiant, strong, and upright in form.
He had one hundred million ministers, all of whom were wise and sagacious;
he had one billion court ladies, as beautiful and dignified as celestial queens,
who, with great compassion and gentleness, attended upon the Great King.
At that time, that Wheel-Turning King always governed by the True Dharma,
presiding over all mountains and lands throughout the four continents under heaven.
Abandoning his kingdom and renouncing worldly glory, he left the home life to seek the path of the Buddha.
I am the queen of a noble king; my voice is endowed with the Brahma-sound, and from my body issues a golden light that shines all around for forty thousand *li*.
Now that the sun has already set, the midnight is tranquil and still.
At that time, I shall receive divine portents and auspicious dreams.
Hearing that a Buddha has appeared in the world, named Guṇasāgara (Ocean of Merit),
he manifests his sovereign power, filling the realms of the ten directions.
They emit oceans of nets of light, illuminating all buddha-fields;
their immeasurable bodies of mastery fill the worlds of the ten directions,
while various bodies of transformation arise through the power of the retribution of their radiance.
Filling as many worlds as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, Illuminating all realms of existence,
the great earth shakes in six ways, And a wondrous sound issues forth spontaneously.
As the Tathāgata appears in the world, All sentient beings rejoice.
From within every single pore, oceans of Buddha-nirmāṇakāyas emerge,
filling the realms of the ten directions and preaching the Dharma according to the needs of beings.
Such was my dream, [witnessing] the sovereign power of the Tathāgata.
Hearing the teaching of the subtle and wondrous Dharma, my body and mind were filled with great joy.
Ten thousand night deities filled the expanse of space,
praising that Tathāgata and awakening me to understanding.
That deity addressed me, saying:
"Wise one, arise now! A Buddha has appeared in your land, one difficult to encounter even in oceans of kalpas.
Hearing these words, I was filled with joy, and immediately I beheld a bright and pure light.
Observing from where it comes, [I see it] from beneath the King of Trees at the site of enlightenment.
I behold the body of the Tathāgata, like Sumeru, the king of mountains;
from every single pore, he emits a great ocean of radiant light.
Beholding the Buddha’s power of mastery, his heart gave rise to great joy;
he immediately made a vast vow, praying: "May I become like the World-Honored One.
The lady, having awakened, spoke to the king, as well as his retinue and the court ladies:
"I dreamed of the Buddha’s light, and joy and bliss filled my body.
Immediately, together with the Great King and an immeasurable number of nayutas of followers—
the fourfold army— I went to where the Tathāgata was."
For twenty thousand years, I constantly made offerings to the Tathāgata,
presenting him with all the seven treasures and the four continents of Jambudvīpa as gifts.
That Buddha then preached for me the *Sūtra of the Universal Cloud of Merit*.
Adorned by an ocean of great vows, I deliver sentient beings according to what they hear.
I have made this great vow: in the future, may I become a Night Goddess, and cause all those who are heedless to distance themselves from all evils.
At that time, I first gave rise to The unsurpassed mind of bodhi;
Amidst the conditioned states of birth and death, I have never once forgotten it.
From then on, I made offerings To ten billion nayutas [of Buddhas].
Experiencing joy within the ocean of birth and death, they bring benefit to all sentient beings.
First was the Buddha Guṇasāgara; second, Guṇapradīpa;
third, Ratnajvāla Buddha; fourth, Prajñāsaṃbhava.
The fifth was Puṣpadhara, the sixth Anāvaraṇacandraruta,
the seventh Dharmacandrarāja, the eighth Paripūrṇajñānarāja,
and the ninth Ratnajvālābuddha— the unsurpassed Honored One among gods and humans.
On the tenth day, I have made offerings to the Buddha Ghosadatta.
To all such Buddhas as these, numbering ten billion nayutas,
I have yet to attain the eye of wisdom to reach the far shore of the ocean of birth and death.
Next there was another eon, named Devasudharmottara;
the world was called Ratnaprabhā, where five hundred Buddhas appeared in the world.
The first Buddha was Pūrṇacandra, and the second was Vimalasūrya.
The third was Light Banner Buddha; the fourth, King of Mount Sumeru;
the fifth, Flower Flame Ocean; the sixth, Wisdom Ocean Banner;
the seventh, Dīpaṃkara Buddha; and the eighth, Celestial Virtue Treasury.
The ninth was Prabhāketu, and the tenth was Samantajñānarāja.
To all such Buddhas as these, I have made offerings;
yet, not having escaped the suffering of the five aggregates, I did not perceive pleasure in what is not pleasure.
They do not give rise to doubt regarding the Dharma, nor do they doubt the True Dharma.
Subsequently, there was an eon named Brahma-Voice Adornment;
at that time, there was a world named Lotus-Lamp Cloud.
There were immeasurable Buddhas there, along with their retinues;
I have made offerings to them all and heard and upheld the True Dharma.
The first Buddha was named Ratnagiri, and the second was Guṇasāgara.
Dharmadhātu-Sumeru-Dhvaja, Fourth, Dharma-Sumeru;
fifth, Dharmadhvaja Buddha; Sixth, Bhūmi-Mahātejas;
seventh, Dharmabala Buddha; Eighth, Gaganamati.
The ninth is Mount Dharma-flame, and the tenth is Mount Illumination.
To all such Buddhas as these, I have made offerings in their entirety;
yet I have not yet realized the truth, nor have I reached the ultimate end of the ocean of dharmas.
Next there was another eon, named Joyful Virtue;
at that time there was a world named Radiant Merit.
In that eon, there were eighty nayutas of Buddhas.
I have made offerings to them all, And paid homage to the Most Victorious Honored Ones:
First, the Gandharva King; Second, the King of the Life-Span Tree;
Third, Merit of Mount Sumeru; Fourth, the Buddha Jewel-Eye.
Fifth is Vairocana; sixth is the Adornment of the Holy Ones;
seventh is Dharmottara-rāja; eighth is Vimala-guṇa;
ninth is Loka-rāja; tenth is Sarva-dharma-rāja.
All such Buddhas as these I have already made offerings to,
yet I had not yet attained the wondrous wisdom that deeply enters all dharma-doors.
Following this, there was another eon named Pure and Indestructible.
At that time there was a world named Universal Radiance Adornment,
where ten Buddhas appeared in the world; having eliminated immeasurable afflictions and being adorned with perfected merit, they purified all sentient beings.
There arose a thousand Buddhas in the world, adorned with immeasurable virtues;
they extinguished the defilements of affliction and caused all beings to become completely pure.
The first Buddha was named Araṇa (Free from Strife), and the second was Anāvaraṇabala (Power of Non-obstruction).
Third was Dharmadhātuprabha; fourth, Brahmamaulirāja;
fifth, Vairocana; sixth, Sarvasattvanamaskṛta;
seventh, Paripūrṇakṣāntidīpa; eighth, Dharmapradīpasampanna.
The ninth is Ocean Adorned with Radiance, and the tenth is King of Majestic Power.
To all such Buddhas as these, I have already made offerings;
yet, still not having understood the True Dharma, I have wandered through all lands.
Next there was another eon, named Gandhapradīpa-kṣetra;
at that time there was a world named Viśuddhodaya,
where one hundred million Buddhas appeared in the world, adorning and purifying every eon.
The Dharma taught by those Buddhas, I heard and received it all in its entirety.
The first was named King Dharmakīrti; the second, Dharmakāyasāgara;
the third, Vīryaśikhara; and the fourth, Guṇadharmarāja.
The fifth was Jina-dharmamegha; the sixth was named Devamakuṭa;
the seventh was Jñānārcis Buddha; the eighth was named Gaganabala;
the ninth was named Samantavijayotthita; and the tenth was named Sumatimukha.
Having made offerings to that Buddha, one accomplishes the Eightfold Noble Path.
Subsequently, there was another eon named Vimalavajra;
at that time, there was a world named Ratnaketu-pati.
Five hundred Buddhas appeared in the world;
I have made offerings to all those Tathāgatas, seeking the dharma-gate of non-obstruction.
The first was named Perfect Virtue, and the second was Tranquil Sound.
The third was Guṇasāgara; the fourth was Vīraśrīrāja;
the fifth was Dharmāgryarāja; the sixth was named Merulakṣaṇa;
the seventh was named Dharmarāja; and the eighth was Guṇarāja.
The ninth was Guṇaparvata, and the tenth was Prabhāsa-rāja.
All such Buddhas as these I have fully made offerings to;
I have purified them all, along with every most excellent path.
Still not having attained full perfection, The ultimate profound patience (dharmakṣānti).
Subsequently there was another eon, Named Victorious Renowned Sound;
at that time there was a world-system, Named Tranquil Sound.
Eighty nayutas of Buddhas appeared in the world;
I have made offerings to them all while practicing the Right Path under them.
The first Buddha was named Kusumasaṃcaya, and the second was Sāgaragarbha.
The third was Guṇodaya; the fourth was Devacūḍa;
the fifth was Maṇigarbha; the sixth was named Suvarṇaparvatarāja;
the seventh was Ratnasaṃcaya Buddha; and the eighth was Śāntadhvaja.
The ninth was Dharma-dhvaja Buddha, and the tenth was named Vasumukha.
All such Buddhas as these I have fully made offerings to.
Following that, there was another kalpa named Sahastra-mukha-guṇa.
At that time there was a world named Good Flower Lamp,
where six hundred million nayutas of Buddhas appeared in the world;
I have already made offerings to all those Buddhas.
The first Buddha was Śāntadhvaja; the second, Jñānamudrārāja;
the third was named Śatapradīpa; the fourth, Guṇamegharāja;
the fifth, Śāntaprabharāja; and the sixth, Vimalasūrya.
The seventh was Dharmapradīparāja, the eighth Guṇaśirirāja,
the ninth Guṇagarbharāja, and the tenth Prajñāmeghagarjanarāja.
All such Buddhas as these have I already honored and made offerings to.
Without yet having attained the patience of non-arising, he brought all dharma-gates to ultimate completion.
Subsequently, there was another eon named Unattached Radiant Flame;
at that time, there was a world named Immeasurable Supreme Light.
There appeared thirty-six billion nayutas of Buddhas;
all such Buddhas as these, I have already made offerings to.
The first was named Universal Mountain King, and the second was Empty Mind.
The third is Saṃjñāna, the fourth is Vyūharatnagarbha,
the fifth is Dharmasāgaraghoṣa, the sixth is Ghoṣadharin,
the seventh is Nirmitaghoṣa, and the eighth is Nirmitameghasāgara.
Ninth is Guṇasvarasāgara, tenth is Svaradhvaja,
eleventh is Samantatejas, twelfth is Dharmasāgara,
thirteenth is Ghoṣasaṃcaya, and fourteenth is Guṇasāgara.
Fifteenth was Pradīpottama, sixteenth Ratnārciṣa,
seventeenth Pradīparāja Buddha, eighteenth Guṇārcis,
nineteenth Candradeva Buddha, and twentieth Guṇajaya.
I have encountered all those Tathāgatas;
when those World-Honored Ones among two-legged beings appeared in the world,
I was Śrīdevī and made offerings to those Most Excellent Ones.
At that time, the Buddha explained to me how to adorn the great ocean of vows;
through the power of dhāraṇī and mindfulness, I was able to receive and uphold them all.
I attained the bright and pure eye, as well as samādhi and dhāraṇī.
Within each and every thought-instant, They see countless lands;
Giving birth to the treasury of great compassion, They enter deeply into clouds of skillful means.
Their minds are pure like space, All arising from within a dream.
First I gave rise to the bodhicitta, vast as space,
ultimately without limit, for the sake of delivering all sentient beings.
Through kalpas reaching to the end of the future, I vow to seek the power of all Buddhas.
Observing all sentient beings, who are inverted by the misconceptions of permanence, pleasure, self, and purity;
shrouded by the darkness of ignorance; giving rise to afflictions and delusions such as false views and craving; and committing immeasurable evil karmas.
Throughout all realms of existence, one fully experiences the retribution of unwholesome deeds;
throughout all realms of existence, one assumes a body through various karmas,
beset by the afflictions of birth, old age, sickness, and death, and oppressed by immeasurable suffering.
I have resolved upon the unsurpassed mind to bring peace and happiness to all sentient beings,
leading them to the presence of all Buddhas; may I fulfill the powers of the Tathāgatas,
satisfy the clouds of great vows, and constantly behold all Buddhas.
Cultivating the Noble Path, they are fully endowed with all merits.
Single-mindedly and extensively seeking the immeasurable clouds of merit,
they enter the Rāmaka-samādhi, which fills all dharma realms.
The vast *pāramitās* resound throughout the lands of the ten directions;
at the abodes of all Buddhas, upon hearing this *Lokamaṅgala*,
one immediately fulfills the conduct of Samantabhadra and enters the pure, profound *dharmadhātu*.
Upholding all dharmas, they fulfill all stages;
With oceans of skillful means throughout the three times, they cultivate immeasurable practices.
With a single mind, they possess Buddha-wisdom, And their wisdom penetrates everything completely.
At that time, having spoken these verses, the Night Goddess prostrated herself in reverence before all the Buddhas.
Before she had even raised her head, she beheld the thousand-spoked wheels on the soles of the feet of all the Tathāgatas;
she then looked back upon all the marks and signs of the Tathāgatas, and within those marks and signs, her body and mind became clear and lucid, yet she remained unattached to them.
With a vast and expansive mind, they swiftly hear the fragrance of the Buddha’s fivefold Dharma-body (*pañcāṅga-dharmakāya*),
bring all *pāramitās* to ultimate fulfillment, and dwell upon the stages of Bodhisattvas. Exhausting the ocean of the Buddha-dharma,

they remain far removed from all forms, sounds, fragrances, tastes, tangibles, and mental objects of the three periods of time, abiding in the stage of the ultimate, universal practice of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva, and attaining perfection.
In the ground of the vast realm of perfect purity, within a single moment of thought, they universally manifest immeasurable Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions;
these possess ten dharma-gates, and each individual dharma-gate is fully endowed with immeasurable,
boundless, inconceivable, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) oceans of all dharma-realms, exhausting the limits of all suffering and being utterly profound.
Faith. “O Son of the Buddha!
Such various merits as these I have long cultivated; with faith, understanding, and acceptance, I uphold them and am fully endowed with the practices of Samantabhadra.”
"Good son!

As for that Wheel-Turning Sage King Prajñā at that time, who continued from kalpa to kalpa, always succeeding to the royal throne, receiving the lineage of the Buddhas, being born into the Śākya clan, and never severing the lineage of the Tathāgata’s sublime tranquility—could this be anyone else? It was none other than me."
"The youth Mañjuśrī is that very person!
At that time, the virtuous and wise lady, the noble consort of the Wheel-Turning Sage King, was none other than I, the Night Goddess Observing Sentient Beings with Joyful Eyes!
The night goddess who awakened me at that time was none other than the emanation-body of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra!

Son of good family, at that time, having awakened from my night dream, I beheld the Buddha’s radiance and first gave rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
