Having given rise to this mind, for as many eons as there are atoms in immeasurable Buddha-fields, I did not fall into the evil realms; I was constantly born in the heavens and, descending into the human world, I experienced all manner of happiness and encountered various Buddhas. Throughout that interval, passing through immeasurable eons, I eventually reached the presence of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Karmapratibhāsavarṇaśrīdhvaja, where I attained this Dharma-gate of the Banner of Joyous Radiance.

Having attained this Dharma-gate, one manifests various bodies to subdue sentient beings, developing them in accordance with their needs and causing them all to draw near to spiritual friends—whether they be devas, humans, or any others. In future ages, those who hear the name of this Buddha, as well as the name of this Dharma-gate, the *Vilomaga Samādhi* of Universal Radiance and Joyful Banner, and who uphold, read, recite, explain, or transcribe it, shall likewise transcend the sins of birth and death for as many oceans of kalpas as there are atoms in immeasurable Buddha-fields. They shall not fall into the evil realms but will always be born among gods and humans, experiencing every form of happiness. They shall constantly behold the Buddhas, hear the Dharma, and receive and uphold it, never forgetting it until the end.

“Good son! In the presence of the Buddha Jewel-Light Merit-Flame, I attained this Dharma-door of the Swift Banner of Universal Radiant Joy. Having attained this Dharma-door, I have single-mindedly sought out spiritual friends; with my body, mind, and faculties filled with joy and delight, I travel through all directions to tame sentient beings and cause them to enter into the practice of the precepts.”
“Good son! I know only this Dharma-gate of the Universal Radiance Joy Banner, the Vīramāgata Samādhi, which is the realm of perfect, pure, and supreme light.

All these great Bodhisattvas, in every moment of thought, never depart from spiritual friends; they enter deeply into the great ocean of skillful means and wisdom. Through spiritual friends, they give birth to and nurture the dharma-gates of swift progress, giving rise to the ocean of all great vows. Throughout all kalpas, they do not depart from their roots of goodness, maintaining continuity in every thought-moment as they draw near to spiritual friends, seek sublime merit, and rescue and protect sentient beings, fully possessing all the paths practiced by Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.

At that time, the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā, for the sake of the youth Sudhana, manifested the physical marks and signs of a bodhisattva adorned with the majestic features of the sphere of the dharma-gate for teaching all worlds. From the white tuft of hair between her eyebrows, she emitted a great light called "Infinite Radiance of the Pure Banner of the Lamp of Universal Wisdom Flames. Having illuminated all worlds, it entered the crown of Sudhana’s head and filled his entire body.
At that time, the youth Sudhana immediately attained the *Vilomāga-paripūrṇa* samādhi. Having attained this samādhi,
each and every one of his bodies filled the entire dharma-realm (*dharmadhātu*), pervading all atoms of earth, water, fire, and wind,
as well as atoms of various jewels, atoms of incense, atoms of diamond (*vajra*), and atoms of *maṇi*.
Within each and every ocean of atoms— be they atoms of jewels, atoms of pulverized dust, or atoms of all manner of adornments—
one perceives the formation and destruction of worlds as numerous as the atoms of a Buddha-field; one perceives the signs of the arising and passing away of the four great elements,
as well as the various arrays of the wind-circle, water-circle, diamond-circle, and earth-circle.
Surrounded by the Arrayed Mountains, there were the palaces of the devas amidst the immeasurable great oceans; the palaces of the nāgas, adorned with various kinds of jewel trees;
and the cities and palaces of yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, humans, non-humans, and others, as well as those of the hells, hungry ghosts, and Yama.
In the abode of King Yama, they fully understand the causes and effects of all phenomena regarding death here and birth there; within each and every body,
they universally manifest bodies equal to the entire dharma-realm, seeing all buddha-fields as they are, and according to those who should be transformed,
they deliver sentient beings from the beauty or ugliness of their karmic retributions with subtle and wondrous voices.
He universally expounded the Dharma, causing this sound of the Dharma to enter through the pores [of all beings], so that all sentient beings might attain the practice of the Dharma.
They beheld each and every buddha-field, as well as as many fields as there are atoms in all worlds;
they beheld the infinite and boundless ocean of all Buddhas, Tathāgatas, and deeply entered roots of goodness within those Buddhas.
Abiding in all dharma-realms, they receive immeasurable dharma-gates from the presence of immeasurable Buddhas;

they transcend birth and death and sport with spiritual powers. In the presence of each and every Buddha, they reflect upon their own practice from the initial generation of the bodhicitta, including the cultivation of the fundamental practices of a bodhisattva, the universal gathering of roots of goodness, and the fruits and retributions of all such spheres of experience.
At each and every Buddha-field, they hear the wheel of Dharma turned by all Buddhas, receiving and upholding it without forgetfulness,

and protecting the True Dharma; through the power of the roots of goodness from their original vows, they behold the entire ocean of all Buddhas of the three periods of time and transcend the flow of birth and death.
“Good son! Since the great bodhisattvas have accomplished such immeasurable and boundless great merits, how could I possibly know or describe their meritorious conduct?”
At that time, the night goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā said to the youth Sudhana:

"By the power of this Dharma-door of the Banner of Universal Radiance and Joy, I constantly behold all Buddhas without any interval or gap. For this reason, I protect the Buddha-dharma everywhere throughout the entire realm of empty space, my mind never wearying or becoming exhausted. How am I able to protect the true Dharma of all Buddhas?"

By the power of the original vows of Vairocana Buddha and by the majestic spiritual power of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, this White Jewel Lotus Dhāraṇī mantra shall protect those who receive, uphold, read, recite, and practice the True Dharma.
At that time, the Night Goddess Pramuditanayanajagadvirocanā, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, spoke this White Jewel Lotus Dhāraṇī mantra:

“Tadete, morike, paśarāmorike śamatha ye, viśamatha ye, parāpattanike uttabhanike svāhā | Cāndrotundike svāhā | Śvetapadmāvatike svāhā | Indrābhanike svāhā | Māndanī svāhā | Yojanī svāhā. “If there be anyone who receives and upholds this mantra, they shall not fall into the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, or animals. In their present body, they shall never suffer an untimely death, nor shall they encounter imprisonment or bondage by officials or in prisons; they shall always experience all manner of pure happiness.”

If there are those who obtain this dhāraṇī, you should know that such persons will always be able to encounter and see the Buddhas without separation; they will also never be separated from hearing the Buddhas preach the Dharma and turning the wheel of the true Dharma. Furthermore, they will always obtain the inexhaustible, pure ocean of the sound of the Dharma, the eloquence, and the seal-dhāraṇī.
If there are those who hear this dhāraṇī, they will be fully endowed with all the pure practices of a bodhisattva; they will certainly cross the ocean of birth and death and reach the other shore.

At that time, having heard this dharani, the youth Sudhana paid homage at the feet of the Night Goddess Who Observes Sentient Beings with Joyful Eyes, bowing his head in reverence and circumambulating her countless times. With single-minded concentration, he contemplated and maintained right mindfulness of the Bodhisattva’s Dharma-door of the Perfectly Pure Banner; he reflected upon and analyzed it, observed it through meditative absorption, recollected the instructions of the spiritual friend, and deeply entered into accordance with the spiritual friend's teachings.
Then that night goddess said to Sudhana: "Good son!

Within this assembly of the Buddha, there is a night goddess named Universal Canopy of Majestic Virtue Covering All Beings. Go to her and ask: how does a bodhisattva learn the bodhisattva conduct, perfect the bodhisattva conduct, and cultivate the bodhisattva path?"

Then the youth Sudhana, having prostrated his head in respectful salutation at the feet of the night goddess Praśāntarutasvarā, took his leave and departed. He went to the place of the night goddess Viśvabhūtisandarśanatejā, seeking a spiritual friend with insatiable resolve; immediately, he was inspired to bring forth all the spheres of his roots of goodness from past lives.

By the power of this realm, one universally beholds the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and spiritual friends of the ten directions, their majestic deportment composed and orderly; having abandoned arrogance, one gives rise to deep reverence. Regarding the Bodhisattvas and spiritual friends one encounters, one maintains an uninterrupted continuity of thought without any divergent mind, taking refuge in all such spiritual friends.

Those bodhisattvas, from their first generation of the mind of enlightenment, were capable of being vessels for the Dharma; up until the tenth stage, they sought spiritual friends no differently than I have, and were constantly protected by such spiritual friends. Hearing the secret words spoken by these spiritual friends, they remembered and held them in their hearts, never forgetting them. For the sake of accomplishing Bodhi, they cultivated all roots of goodness and adorned themselves with merit, perfecting all skillful means—all of this because they had previously drawn near to spiritual friends in past lives.

At that time, the Night Goddess Universal Pervading Sentient Beings with Majestic Virtue universally radiated light. This light was named the "Dharma Gate of the Manifestation of the Discipline for Taming All Sentient Beings. Because she had attained this Dharma Gate, she was fully endowed with the primary and secondary marks (lakṣaṇa-vyañjana) to adorn her body. With this body of primary and secondary marks, she manifested before all sentient beings to cause them to rejoice. From each of these marks, she manifested the light of all various signs. Having manifested this light, she emitted all rays from the mark of the white tuft between her brows (*ūrṇā-kośa*). With this light, she universally illumined everything, taking all those rays as her retinue. This light is called the "Sphere of the Samādhi of Universal Wisdom Flame, Vimalamāga, Perfectly Pure and Radiant."

Furthermore, this light, immeasurable, boundless, and without limit, having universally illumined all worlds throughout the ten directions, entered the crown of the youth Sudhana’s head and filled his entire body. Within his body, he saw all beings dying here and being born there, and the retributions of their good and evil karma were all clearly manifested within Sudhana’s body.
At that time, the youth Sudhana immediately attained the most wondrous and pure Vīramagha Samādhi.

When he attained this samādhi, immeasurable and boundless sentient beings resolved their minds upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. The entire great assembly was filled with immense joy; they paid homage to the Buddha and withdrew.
